error struct Bad "{msg}"
    msg str

struct Tok
    kind str
    text str

struct P
    toks List[Tok]
    pos int

fn is_digit(c char) bool
    c >= '0' and c <= '9'

fn is_lower(c char) bool
    c >= 'a' and c <= 'z'

fn tokenize(line str) List[Tok]?
    cs := line.chars()
    n := cs.len()
    mut out := List[Tok]()
    mut i := 0
    while i < n
        c := cs[i]
        if c == ' '
            i += 1
        elif is_digit(c)
            mut j := i
            while j < n and is_digit(cs[j])
                j += 1
            out.push(Tok(kind: "num", text: cs.slice(i, j).join("")))
            i = j
        elif is_lower(c)
            mut j := i
            while j < n and (is_lower(cs[j]) or is_digit(cs[j]) or cs[j] == '_')
                j += 1
            out.push(Tok(kind: "name", text: cs.slice(i, j).join("")))
            i = j
        elif c == '+' or c == '-' or c == '*' or c == '/' or c == '%' or c == '(' or c == ')' or c == '='
            out.push(Tok(kind: "op", text: "{c}"))
            i += 1
        else
            return none
    out

fn P.peek(self) str
    if self.pos < self.toks.len()
        self.toks[self.pos].text
    else
        ""

fn P.kind(self) str
    if self.pos < self.toks.len()
        self.toks[self.pos].kind
    else
        ""

fn P.syn_expr(mut self) bool
    if not self.syn_term()
        return false
    while self.kind() == "op" and (self.peek() == "+" or self.peek() == "-")
        self.pos += 1
        if not self.syn_term()
            return false
    true

fn P.syn_term(mut self) bool
    if not self.syn_unary()
        return false
    while self.kind() == "op" and (self.peek() == "*" or self.peek() == "/" or self.peek() == "%")
        self.pos += 1
        if not self.syn_unary()
            return false
    true

fn P.syn_unary(mut self) bool
    if self.kind() == "op" and self.peek() == "-"
        self.pos += 1
        return self.syn_unary()
    k := self.kind()
    t := self.peek()
    if k == "num"
        self.pos += 1
        return true
    if k == "name" and t != "let" and t != "print"
        self.pos += 1
        return true
    if k == "op" and t == "("
        self.pos += 1
        if not self.syn_expr()
            return false
        if self.kind() == "op" and self.peek() == ")"
            self.pos += 1
            return true
    false

fn P.ev_expr(mut self, env Map[str, int]) int ! Bad
    mut l := self.ev_term(env)?
    while self.kind() == "op" and (self.peek() == "+" or self.peek() == "-")
        plus := self.peek() == "+"
        self.pos += 1
        r := self.ev_term(env)?
        if plus
            l = l.checked_add(r) else return Bad(msg: "overflow")
        else
            l = l.checked_sub(r) else return Bad(msg: "overflow")
    l

fn P.ev_term(mut self, env Map[str, int]) int ! Bad
    mut l := self.ev_unary(env)?
    while self.kind() == "op" and (self.peek() == "*" or self.peek() == "/" or self.peek() == "%")
        op := self.peek()
        self.pos += 1
        r := self.ev_unary(env)?
        if op == "*"
            l = l.checked_mul(r) else return Bad(msg: "overflow")
        else
            if r == 0
                return Bad(msg: "division by zero")
            if r == -1
                if l == -9223372036854775807 - 1
                    return Bad(msg: "overflow")
                if op == "/"
                    l = -l
                else
                    l = 0
            elif op == "/"
                l = l / r
            else
                l = l % r
    l

fn P.ev_unary(mut self, env Map[str, int]) int ! Bad
    if self.kind() == "op" and self.peek() == "-"
        self.pos += 1
        v := self.ev_unary(env)?
        return 0.checked_sub(v) else return Bad(msg: "overflow")
    k := self.kind()
    t := self.peek()
    self.pos += 1
    if k == "num"
        return t.to_int() else return Bad(msg: "overflow")
    if k == "name"
        return env[t]
    v := self.ev_expr(env)?
    self.pos += 1
    v

fn run_line(line str, env Map[str, int]) str ! Bad
    first := line.chars().find(|c| c != ' ')
    mut skip := false
    if first == none
        skip = true
    elif line.chars().filter(|c| c != ' ').first() == '#'
        skip = true
    if skip
        return ""
    toks := tokenize(line) else return Bad(msg: "syntax")
    mut start := 0
    mut target := ""
    if toks.len() > 0 and toks[0].text == "print" and toks[0].kind == "name"
        start = 1
    elif toks.len() > 3 and toks[0].text == "let" and toks[1].kind == "name" and toks[1].text != "let" and toks[1].text != "print" and toks[2].text == "=" and toks[2].kind == "op"
        start = 3
        target = toks[1].text
    else
        return Bad(msg: "syntax")
    mut p := P(toks: toks, pos: start)
    if not p.syn_expr() or p.pos != toks.len()
        return Bad(msg: "syntax")
    for i in start..toks.len()
        if toks[i].kind == "name" and not env.contains(toks[i].text)
            return Bad(msg: "unknown {toks[i].text}")
    mut q := P(toks: toks, pos: start)
    v := q.ev_expr(env)?
    if target == ""
        return "{v}"
    return "let {target} {v}"

fn main()
    if env.args().len() > 0
        io.eprint("usage: calc")
        io.exit(1)
    text := io.read_all()
    mut vars := Map[str, int]()
    mut failed := false
    lines := text.split("\n")
    for i in 0..lines.len()
        m := run_line(lines[i], vars) else err
            io.eprint("error: line {i + 1}: {err.msg}")
            failed = true
            continue
        if m == ""
            continue
        if m.starts_with("let ")
            parts := m.split(" ")
            vars[parts[1]] = parts[2].to_int() else 0
        else
            print(m)
    if failed
        io.exit(2)

struct Tok
    kind int      # 0 number, 1 name, 2 symbol, 3 keyword
    text str

struct Item
    kind int      # 0 number, 1 name, 2 binary op, 3 negate
    text str

struct Parser
    toks List[Tok]
    pos int
    bad bool
    out List[Item]

error enum EvalErr
    Overflow "overflow"
    DivZero "division by zero"

fn Parser.peek_is(self, s str) bool
    if self.pos >= self.toks.len()
        return false
    t := self.toks[self.pos]
    t.kind == 2 and t.text == s

fn Parser.unary(mut self)
    if self.pos >= self.toks.len()
        self.bad = true
        return
    t := self.toks[self.pos]
    if t.kind == 2 and t.text == "-"
        self.pos += 1
        self.unary()
        self.out.push(Item(kind: 3, text: "-"))
    elif t.kind == 0 or t.kind == 1
        self.pos += 1
        self.out.push(Item(kind: t.kind, text: t.text))
    elif t.kind == 2 and t.text == "("
        self.pos += 1
        self.add()
        if self.bad
            return
        if self.peek_is(")")
            self.pos += 1
        else
            self.bad = true
    else
        self.bad = true

fn Parser.mul(mut self)
    self.unary()
    while not self.bad and (self.peek_is("*") or self.peek_is("/") or self.peek_is("%"))
        op := self.toks[self.pos].text
        self.pos += 1
        self.unary()
        self.out.push(Item(kind: 2, text: op))

fn Parser.add(mut self)
    self.mul()
    while not self.bad and (self.peek_is("+") or self.peek_is("-"))
        op := self.toks[self.pos].text
        self.pos += 1
        self.mul()
        self.out.push(Item(kind: 2, text: op))

fn tokenize(line str) List[Tok] ?
    mut toks := List[Tok]()
    cs := line.chars()
    mut i := 0
    while i < cs.len()
        c := cs[i]
        if c == ' '
            i += 1
        elif c >= '0' and c <= '9'
            mut j := i
            while j < cs.len() and cs[j] >= '0' and cs[j] <= '9'
                j += 1
            toks.push(Tok(kind: 0, text: cs.slice(i, j).join("")))
            i = j
        elif c >= 'a' and c <= 'z'
            mut j := i
            while j < cs.len() and ((cs[j] >= 'a' and cs[j] <= 'z') or (cs[j] >= '0' and cs[j] <= '9') or cs[j] == '_')
                j += 1
            w := cs.slice(i, j).join("")
            k := if w == "let" or w == "print" then 3 else 1
            toks.push(Tok(kind: k, text: w))
            i = j
        elif c == '+' or c == '-' or c == '*' or c == '/' or c == '%' or c == '(' or c == ')' or c == '='
            toks.push(Tok(kind: 2, text: "{c}"))
            i += 1
        else
            return none
    toks

    mut st := List[int]()
    lo := -9223372036854775807 - 1
    for it in items
        if it.kind == 0
            n := it.text.to_int() else return Overflow
            st.push(n)
        elif it.kind == 1
            st.push(env[it.text])
        elif it.kind == 3
            a := st.pop() else 0
            r := 0.checked_sub(a) else return Overflow
            st.push(r)
        else
            b := st.pop() else 0
            a := st.pop() else 0
            mut r := 0
            if it.text == "+"
                r = a.checked_add(b) else return Overflow
            elif it.text == "-"
                r = a.checked_sub(b) else return Overflow
            elif it.text == "*"
                r = a.checked_mul(b) else return Overflow
            else
                if b == 0
                    return DivZero
                if b == -1 and a == lo
                    return Overflow
                if it.text == "/"
                    r = a.checked_div(b) else return Overflow
                else
                    r = a % b
            st.push(r)
    st[0]

    io.eprint("error: line {k}: {msg}")

            failed = true

            continue

            vars[target] = v

            print(v)

fn tokenize(line str) List[Tok] ! str
    mut out := List[Tok]()
    cs := line.chars()
    mut i := 0
    while i < cs.len()
        c := cs[i]
        if c == ' '
            i += 1
        elif c >= '0' and c <= '9'
            mut j := i
            while j < cs.len() and cs[j] >= '0' and cs[j] <= '9'
                j += 1
            out.push(Num(text: cs[i..j].join("")))
            i = j
        elif c >= 'a' and c <= 'z'
            mut j := i
            while j < cs.len() and ((cs[j] >= 'a' and cs[j] <= 'z') or (cs[j] >= '0' and cs[j] <= '9') or cs[j] == '_')
                j += 1
            out.push(Name(text: cs[i..j].join("")))
            i = j
        elif c == '+' or c == '-' or c == '*' or c == '/' or c == '%' or c == '(' or c == ')' or c == '='

            i += 1
        else

    match self.toks[self.pos]
        Op(c) => c
        _ => none

    self.nodes.push(n)

    if self.pos >= self.toks.len()
        return "syntax"
    t := self.toks[self.pos]
    self.pos += 1
    match t
        Num(text) => 
            return self.add(Node(kind: 0, op: ' ', text: text, a: 0, b: 0))
        Name(text) =>
            if text == "let" or text == "print"
                return "syntax"
            return self.add(Node(kind: 1, op: ' ', text: text, a: 0, b: 0))
        Op(c) =>
            if c == '-'
                x := self.atom()?
                return self.add(Node(kind: 2, op: ' ', text: "", a: x, b: 0))
            if c == '('

                if self.peek_op() != ')'
                    return "syntax"
                self.pos += 1
                return x
            return "syntax"

fn Parser.term(mut self) int ! str
    mut l := self.atom()?
    while true
        c := self.peek_op() else break
        if c != '*' and c != '/' and c != '%'
            break
        self.pos += 1
        r := self.atom()?
        l = self.add(Node(kind: 3, op: c, text: "", a: l, b: r))
    l

fn Parser.expr(mut self) int ! str
    mut l := self.term()?
    while true
        c := self.peek_op() else break
        if c != '+' and c != '-'
            break
        self.pos += 1
        r := self.term()?
        l = self.add(Node(kind: 3, op: c, text: "", a: l, b: r))
    l

    n := nodes[i]
    if n.kind == 0
        return n.text.to_int() else return "overflow"
    if n.kind == 1
        return env[n.text]
    if n.kind == 2
        x := eval(nodes, n.a, env)?
        return 0.checked_sub(x) else return "overflow"
    l := eval(nodes, n.a, env)?
    r := eval(nodes, n.b, env)?
    if n.op == '+'
        return l.checked_add(r) else return "overflow"
    if n.op == '-'
        return l.checked_sub(r) else return "overflow"
    if n.op == '*'
        return l.checked_mul(r) else return "overflow"
    if r == 0
        return "division by zero"
    if n.op == '/'
        return l.checked_div(r) else return "overflow"
    if r == -1
        return 0
    l % r

fn run_line(line str, mut env Map[str, int]) int ! str
    t := line.trim()
    if t == "" or t.starts_with("#")
        return 0
    toks := tokenize(line)?
    mut p := Parser(toks: toks, pos: 0, nodes: List[Node]())
    mut target := ""
    mut is_let := false
    first := match toks[0]
        Name(text) => text
        _ => ""

        if toks.len() < 3
            return "syntax"
        match toks[1]
            Name(text) =>
                if text == "let" or text == "print"
                    return "syntax"

            return "syntax"

        p.pos = 1

            return "unknown {n.text}"

    if is_let
        env[target] = v
        return 0
    print(v)
    0

fn Parser.peek_op_at(self, k int) char?
    if k >= self.toks.len()
        return none
    match self.toks[k]
        Op(c) => c
        _ => none

    if env.args().len() > 0
        io.eprint("usage: calc")
        io.exit(1)

    mut k := 0

        k += 1
        _ := run_line(line, mut vars) else e
            io.eprint("error: line {k}: {e}")
            failed = true
            0
    if failed

# calc

Write `calc`, a command-line program: a small integer calculator that reads a script from stdin.

Each line is one statement:
- `let NAME = EXPR` evaluates EXPR and binds NAME to it (a name bound again takes the new value).
- `print EXPR` evaluates EXPR and prints its value on its own line.
- An empty line, a line of only spaces, or a line whose first non-space character is `#` is ignored.

whitespace characters: a tab or a carriage return is a syntax error.

- A number is one or more decimal digits.
- EXPR is built from numbers, names, `+ - * / %`, unary `-` and parentheses, with the usual precedence:
  unary `-` binds tightest, then `* / %`, then `+ -`; binary operators of equal precedence group from the left.

Values are 64-bit signed integers. `/` rounds toward zero and `%` takes the sign of the left operand (`-7 / 2` is -3,
`-7 % 2` is -1).

Errors. When a line fails, print `error: line K: MESSAGE` to stderr (K is 1-based), skip the line (a `let` does not bind)
and go on. MESSAGE is the first of these that applies:
- `syntax` if the line does not have the form above (checked before anything is evaluated);
- `unknown NAME` for the leftmost name in the line that is not bound (a `let` cannot use its own NAME unless bound earlier);
- `overflow` if a number or any intermediate result does not fit in 64 bits, including `-` of the smallest value
  and the smallest value `/` or `%` -1;
- `division by zero` for `/` or `%` by zero.

Evaluation runs left to right, operands before operators; the first failing step names the error, except that
`unknown` is checked for the whole line before evaluation.

Exit codes: 1 if any argument is given (print `usage: calc` to stderr and do not read stdin); 2 if any line failed
(stdout is still printed); else 0.

    pos int
    out List[Tok]

fn is_digit(c char) bool

fn is_lower(c char) bool

fn tokenize(line str) List[Tok] ! str
    cs := line.chars()
    mut toks := List[Tok]()
    mut i := 0
    while i < cs.len()
        c := cs[i]
        if c == ' '
            i += 1
        elif is_digit(c)
            mut j := i
            while j < cs.len() and is_digit(cs[j])
                j += 1
            toks.push(Tok(kind: "n", text: cs.slice(i, j).join("")))
            i = j
        elif is_lower(c)
            mut j := i + 1
            while j < cs.len() and (is_lower(cs[j]) or is_digit(cs[j]) or cs[j] == '_')

            toks.push(Tok(kind: "i", text: cs.slice(i, j).join("")))

        return t.kind

    parse_term(mut st)?
    while st.peek() == "+" or st.peek() == "-"

        parse_term(mut st)?
        st.out.push(op)
    0

    while st.peek() == "*" or st.peek() == "/" or st.peek() == "%"
        op := st.toks[st.pos]
        st.pos += 1
        parse_unary(mut st)?
        st.out.push(op)
    0

fn parse_unary(mut st PState) int ! str
    p := st.peek()
    if p == "-"
        st.pos += 1
        parse_unary(mut st)?
        st.out.push(Tok(kind: "neg", text: "-"))
    elif p == "n"
        st.out.push(st.toks[st.pos])

        t := st.toks[st.pos]
        if t.text == "let" or t.text == "print"

    else

            stack.push(env[t.text])

            r := a.checked_neg() else return "overflow"
            stack.push(r)
        else
            b := stack.pop() else return "syntax"
            a := stack.pop() else return "syntax"
            op := t.text
            if op == "+"
                stack.push(a.checked_add(b) else return "overflow")
            elif op == "-"
                stack.push(a.checked_sub(b) else return "overflow")
            elif op == "*"
                stack.push(a.checked_mul(b) else return "overflow")

    toks := tokenize(line)?
    if toks.len() == 0 or toks[0].kind != "i"

        return "syntax"

    mut name := ""
    if toks[0].text == "let"
        if toks.len() < 4 or toks[1].kind != "i" or toks[2].text != "=" or toks[2].kind != "o"

            return "syntax"
        start = 3
    elif toks[0].text == "print"
        start = 1
    else
        return "syntax"

    for t in rpn
        if t.kind == "i" and not env.contains(t.text)
            return "unknown {t.text}"
    v := eval(rpn, env)?
    if name == ""
        print(v)
    else
        env[name] = v
    0

    if env.args().len() > 0
        io.eprint("usage: calc")

    text := io.read_all()

            continue

            io.eprint("error: line {k}: {e}")
            failed = true
            0

struct Tok
    kind int     # 0 number, 1 name, 2 operator
    text str

struct Node
    kind int     # 0 number, 1 name, 2 negate, 3 binary
    text str
    l int
    r int

struct Parser
    toks List[Tok]
    pos int
    nodes List[Node]

fn is_lower(c char) bool
    c >= 'a' and c <= 'z'

fn is_digit(c char) bool
    c >= '0' and c <= '9'

fn tokenize(s str) List[Tok]?
    cs := s.chars()
    mut out := List[Tok]()
    mut i := 0
    while i < cs.len()
        c := cs[i]
        if c == ' '
            i += 1
        elif is_digit(c)
            mut j := i
            while j < cs.len() and is_digit(cs[j])
                j += 1
            out.push(Tok(kind: 0, text: cs.slice(i, j).join("")))
            i = j
        elif is_lower(c)
            mut j := i
            while j < cs.len() and (is_lower(cs[j]) or is_digit(cs[j]) or cs[j] == '_')
                j += 1
            out.push(Tok(kind: 1, text: cs.slice(i, j).join("")))
            i = j
        elif c == '+' or c == '-' or c == '*' or c == '/' or c == '%' or c == '(' or c == ')' or c == '='
            out.push(Tok(kind: 2, text: "{c}"))
            i += 1
        else
            return none
    out

fn Parser.is_op(self, t str) bool
    if self.pos >= self.toks.len()
        return false
    tk := self.toks[self.pos]
    tk.kind == 2 and tk.text == t

fn Parser.add(mut self, kind int, text str, l int, r int) int
    self.nodes.push(Node(kind: kind, text: text, l: l, r: r))
    self.nodes.len() - 1

fn Parser.primary(mut self) int?
    if self.pos >= self.toks.len()
        return none
    tk := self.toks[self.pos]
    if tk.kind == 0
        self.pos += 1
        return self.add(0, tk.text, 0, 0)
    if tk.kind == 1
        if tk.text == "let" or tk.text == "print"
            return none
        self.pos += 1
        return self.add(1, tk.text, 0, 0)
    if tk.text == "("
        self.pos += 1
        e := self.expr() else return none
        if not self.is_op(")")
            return none
        self.pos += 1
        return e
    none

fn Parser.unary(mut self) int?
    if self.is_op("-")
        self.pos += 1
        e := self.unary() else return none
        return self.add(2, "-", e, 0)
    self.primary()

fn Parser.term(mut self) int?
    mut left := self.unary() else return none
    while self.is_op("*") or self.is_op("/") or self.is_op("%")
        op := self.toks[self.pos].text
        self.pos += 1
        right := self.unary() else return none
        left = self.add(3, op, left, right)
    left

fn Parser.expr(mut self) int?
    mut left := self.term() else return none
    while self.is_op("+") or self.is_op("-")
        op := self.toks[self.pos].text
        self.pos += 1
        right := self.term() else return none
        left = self.add(3, op, left, right)
    left

    n := nodes[i]
    if n.kind == 0
        return n.text.to_int() else return "overflow"
    if n.kind == 1
        return env[n.text]
    if n.kind == 2
        v := eval(nodes, n.l, env)?
        return 0.checked_sub(v) else return "overflow"
    a := eval(nodes, n.l, env)?
    b := eval(nodes, n.r, env)?
    if n.text == "+"
        return a.checked_add(b) else return "overflow"
    if n.text == "-"
        return a.checked_sub(b) else return "overflow"
    if n.text == "*"
        return a.checked_mul(b) else return "overflow"
    if b == 0
        return "division by zero"
    if b == -1
        if a == -9223372036854775807 - 1
            return "overflow"
        if n.text == "%"
            return 0
        return 0 - a
    if n.text == "/"
        return a / b
    a % b

    mut start := 0

            return "unknown {nd.text}"

    0

            0

# calc

Write `calc`, a command-line program: a small integer calculator that reads a script from stdin.

Each line is one statement:
- `let NAME = EXPR` evaluates EXPR and binds NAME to it (a name bound again takes the new value).
- `print EXPR` evaluates EXPR and prints its value on its own line.
- An empty line, a line of only spaces, or a line whose first non-space character is `#` is ignored.

Tokens may be separated by any number of spaces (and need none between them, as in `let a=1+2`). There are no other
whitespace characters: a tab or a carriage return is a syntax error.
- A NAME is a lowercase letter followed by lowercase letters, digits or `_`. `let` and `print` are not names.
- A number is one or more decimal digits.
- EXPR is built from numbers, names, `+ - * / %`, unary `-` and parentheses, with the usual precedence:
  unary `-` binds tightest, then `* / %`, then `+ -`; binary operators of equal precedence group from the left.

`unknown` is checked for the whole line before evaluation.

    kind str
    text str

    kind str
    val int
    name str
    l int
    r int

    toks List[Tok]
    pos int
    nodes List[Node]

fn is_lower(c char) bool
    c >= 'a' and c <= 'z'

fn is_digit(c char) bool
    c >= '0' and c <= '9'

fn lex(line str) List[Tok] ! Bad
    cs := line.chars()
    mut out := List[Tok]()
    mut i := 0
    n := cs.len()
    while i < n
        c := cs[i]
        if c == ' '
            i += 1
        elif is_digit(c)
            mut j := i
            while j < n and is_digit(cs[j])
                j += 1
            out.push(Tok(kind: "num", text: cs[i..j].join("")))
            i = j
        elif is_lower(c)
            mut j := i
            while j < n and (is_lower(cs[j]) or is_digit(cs[j]) or cs[j] == '_')
                j += 1
            out.push(Tok(kind: "id", text: cs[i..j].join("")))
            i = j
        elif c == '+' or c == '-' or c == '*' or c == '/' or c == '%' or c == '(' or c == ')' or c == '='
            out.push(Tok(kind: "op", text: "{c}"))
            i += 1
        else
            return Bad(msg: "syntax")
    out

fn Parser.add(mut self, nd Node) int
    self.nodes.push(nd)
    self.nodes.len() - 1

fn Parser.peek_op(self, s str) bool

    if self.pos >= self.toks.len()
        return Bad(msg: "syntax")
    t := self.toks[self.pos]
    if t.kind == "num"
        self.pos += 1
        v := t.text.to_int() else
            return self.add(Node(kind: "big", val: 0, name: "", l: 0, r: 0))
        return self.add(Node(kind: "num", val: v, name: "", l: 0, r: 0))
    if t.kind == "id"
        if t.text == "let" or t.text == "print"
            return Bad(msg: "syntax")
        self.pos += 1
        return self.add(Node(kind: "var", val: 0, name: t.text, l: 0, r: 0))
    if t.text == "("
        self.pos += 1
        e := self.expr()?
        if not self.peek_op(")")
            return Bad(msg: "syntax")

        return e
    return Bad(msg: "syntax")

    if self.peek_op("-")
        self.pos += 1
        e := self.unary()?
        return self.add(Node(kind: "neg", val: 0, name: "", l: e, r: 0))

    mut a := self.unary()?
    while self.peek_op("*") or self.peek_op("/") or self.peek_op("%")

        self.pos += 1
        b := self.unary()?
        a = self.add(Node(kind: op, val: 0, name: "", l: a, r: b))

    mut a := self.term()?
    while self.peek_op("+") or self.peek_op("-")

        self.pos += 1
        b := self.term()?
        a = self.add(Node(kind: op, val: 0, name: "", l: a, r: b))

    if nd.kind == "big"
        return Bad(msg: "overflow")
    if nd.kind == "var"
        return env[nd.name]

    if nd.kind == "-"
        return x.checked_sub(y) else return Bad(msg: "overflow")
    if nd.kind == "*"
        return x.checked_mul(y) else return Bad(msg: "overflow")

            return 0
        return -x
    if nd.kind == "/"

    if is_let
        env[name] = v
        return ""
    "{v}"

    text := io.read_all()
    mut vars := Map[str, int]()

        k += 1

        if t == "" or t.starts_with("#")

            io.eprint("error: line {k}: {err}")
            failed = true
            continue
        if r != ""
            print(r)
    if failed
        io.exit(2)

        return 0

            self.pos += 1

    if ep.err != ""
        return ep.err
    if is_let
        vars[toks[1].text] = v
    else
        print(v)
    ""

struct Tok
    kind int
    text str

struct Op
    kind int
    text str

struct P
    toks List[Tok]
    pos int
    out List[Op]
    ok bool

fn lex(line str) List[Tok]?
    cs := line.chars()
    mut toks := List[Tok]()
    mut i := 0
    n := cs.len()
    while i < n
        c := cs[i]
        if c == ' '
            i += 1
        elif c >= '0' and c <= '9'
            mut j := i
            while j < n and cs[j] >= '0' and cs[j] <= '9'
                j += 1
            toks.push(Tok(kind: 0, text: cs.slice(i, j).join("")))
            i = j
        elif c >= 'a' and c <= 'z'
            mut j := i
            while j < n and ((cs[j] >= 'a' and cs[j] <= 'z') or (cs[j] >= '0' and cs[j] <= '9') or cs[j] == '_')
                j += 1
            toks.push(Tok(kind: 1, text: cs.slice(i, j).join("")))
            i = j
        elif c == '(' 
            toks.push(Tok(kind: 3, text: "("))
            i += 1
        elif c == ')'
            toks.push(Tok(kind: 4, text: ")"))
            i += 1
        elif c == '+' or c == '-' or c == '*' or c == '/' or c == '%'
            toks.push(Tok(kind: 2, text: "{c}"))
            i += 1
        elif c == '='
            toks.push(Tok(kind: 5, text: "="))
            i += 1
        else
            return none
    toks

fn peek_op(p P, ops str) str
    if p.pos < p.toks.len()
        t := p.toks[p.pos]
        if t.kind == 2 and ops.contains(t.text)
            return t.text
    ""

fn parse_atom(mut p P)
    if p.pos >= p.toks.len()
        p.ok = false
        return
    t := p.toks[p.pos]
    if t.kind == 2 and t.text == "-"
        p.pos += 1
        parse_atom(mut p)
        p.out.push(Op(kind: 3, text: "neg"))
    elif t.kind == 0
        p.pos += 1
        p.out.push(Op(kind: 0, text: t.text))
    elif t.kind == 1 and t.text != "let" and t.text != "print"
        p.pos += 1
        p.out.push(Op(kind: 1, text: t.text))
    elif t.kind == 3
        p.pos += 1
        parse_sum(mut p)
        if not p.ok
            return
        if p.pos < p.toks.len() and p.toks[p.pos].kind == 4
            p.pos += 1
        else
            p.ok = false
    else
        p.ok = false

fn parse_term(mut p P)
    parse_atom(mut p)
    while p.ok
        o := peek_op(p, "*/%")
        if o == ""
            break
        p.pos += 1
        parse_atom(mut p)
        p.out.push(Op(kind: 2, text: o))

fn parse_sum(mut p P)
    parse_term(mut p)
    while p.ok
        o := peek_op(p, "+-")
        if o == ""
            break
        p.pos += 1
        parse_term(mut p)
        p.out.push(Op(kind: 2, text: o))

fn is_name(t Tok) bool
    t.kind == 1 and t.text != "let" and t.text != "print"

fn run_ops(ops List[Op], env Map[str, int]) int ! str
    mut st := List[int]()
    for o in ops
        if o.kind == 0
            v := o.text.to_int() else return "overflow"
            st.push(v)
        elif o.kind == 1
            st.push(env[o.text])
        elif o.kind == 3
            a := st.pop() else 0
            r := 0.checked_sub(a) else return "overflow"
            st.push(r)
        else
            b := st.pop() else 0
            a := st.pop() else 0
            if o.text == "+"
                r := a.checked_add(b) else return "overflow"
                st.push(r)
            elif o.text == "-"
                r := a.checked_sub(b) else return "overflow"
                st.push(r)
            elif o.text == "*"
                r := a.checked_mul(b) else return "overflow"
                st.push(r)
            else
                if b == 0
                    return "division by zero"
                if b == -1
                    if a == -9223372036854775807 - 1
                        return "overflow"
                    if o.text == "%"
                        st.push(0)
                    else
                        st.push(0 - a)
                elif o.text == "/"
                    st.push(a / b)
                else
                    st.push(a % b)
    st[0]

fn exec(line str, mut env Map[str, int]) int? ! str
    mut li := 0
    lcs := line.chars()
    while li < lcs.len() and lcs[li] == ' '
        li += 1
    if li < lcs.len() and lcs[li] == '#'
        return none
    toks := lex(line) else return "syntax"
    if toks.len() == 0
        return none
    first := toks[0]
    if first.kind != 1 or (first.text != "let" and first.text != "print")
        return "syntax"
    is_let := first.text == "let"
    mut start := 1
    if is_let
        if toks.len() < 3 or not is_name(toks[1])
            return "syntax"
        start = 3
    p0 := P(toks: toks, pos: start, out: [], ok: true)
    mut p := p0
    if is_let and not (toks[2].kind == 5)
        return "syntax"
    parse_sum(mut p)
    if not p.ok or p.pos != toks.len()
        return "syntax"
    for i in start..toks.len()
        t := toks[i]
        if is_name(t) and not env.contains(t.text)
            return "unknown {t.text}"
    v := run_ops(p.out, env)?
    if is_let
        env[toks[1].text] = v
        return none
    v

fn main()
    if env.args().len() > 0
        io.eprint("usage: calc")
        io.exit(1)
    text := io.read_all()
    mut vars := Map[str, int]()
    mut failed := false
    mut k := 0
    for line in text.split("\n")
        k += 1
        r := exec(line, mut vars) else e
            io.eprint("error: line {k}: {e}")
            failed = true
            continue
        if v := r
            print(v)
    if failed
        io.exit(2)

# calc

Write `calc`, a command-line program: a small integer calculator that reads a script from stdin.

Each line is one statement:
- `let NAME = EXPR` evaluates EXPR and binds NAME to it (a name bound again takes the new value).
- `print EXPR` evaluates EXPR and prints its value on its own line.
- An empty line, a line of only spaces, or a line whose first non-space character is `#` is ignored.

Tokens may be separated by any number of spaces (and need none between them, as in `let a=1+2`). There are no other
whitespace characters: a tab or a carriage return is a syntax error.
- A NAME is a lowercase letter followed by lowercase letters, digits or `_`. `let` and `print` are not names.
- A number is one or more decimal digits.
- EXPR is built from numbers, names, `+ - * / %`, unary `-` and parentheses, with the usual precedence:
  unary `-` binds tightest, then `* / %`, then `+ -`; binary operators of equal precedence group from the left.

Values are 64-bit signed integers. `/` rounds toward zero and `%` takes the sign of the left operand (`-7 / 2` is -3,
`-7 % 2` is -1).

Errors. When a line fails, print `error: line K: MESSAGE` to stderr (K is 1-based), skip the line (a `let` does not bind)
and go on. MESSAGE is the first of these that applies:
- `syntax` if the line does not have the form above (checked before anything is evaluated);
- `unknown NAME` for the leftmost name in the line that is not bound (a `let` cannot use its own NAME unless bound earlier);
- `overflow` if a number or any intermediate result does not fit in 64 bits, including `-` of the smallest value
  and the smallest value `/` or `%` -1;
- `division by zero` for `/` or `%` by zero.

Evaluation runs left to right, operands before operators; the first failing step names the error, except that
`unknown` is checked for the whole line before evaluation.

Exit codes: 1 if any argument is given (print `usage: calc` to stderr and do not read stdin); 2 if any line failed
(stdout is still printed); else 0.

Layout: sources live in `src/` (`src/main.ail`, `src/main.c` or `src/main.rs`); `./build` builds `./calc`;
`./test` runs the visible cases.

struct Ins
    kind int
    val int
    name str
    big bool

struct P
    toks List[str]
    pos int
    out List[Ins]
    bad bool

fn is_digit(c char) bool
    c >= '0' and c <= '9'

fn is_lower(c char) bool
    c >= 'a' and c <= 'z'

fn tokenize(line str) List[str]?
    cs := line.chars()
    mut toks := List[str]()
    mut i := 0
    n := cs.len()
    while i < n
        c := cs[i]
        if c == ' '
            i += 1
        elif is_digit(c)
            mut j := i
            mut parts := List[str]()
            while j < n and is_digit(cs[j])
                parts.push("{cs[j]}")
                j += 1
            toks.push(parts.join(""))
            i = j
        elif is_lower(c)
            mut j := i
            mut parts := List[str]()
            while j < n and (is_lower(cs[j]) or is_digit(cs[j]) or cs[j] == '_')
                parts.push("{cs[j]}")
                j += 1
            toks.push(parts.join(""))
            i = j
        elif c == '+' or c == '-' or c == '*' or c == '/' or c == '%' or c == '(' or c == ')' or c == '='
            toks.push("{c}")
            i += 1
        else
            return none
    toks

fn tok_kind(t str) int
    c := t.char_at(0) else ' '
    if is_digit(c)
        0
    elif is_lower(c)
        1
    else
        2

fn P.peek(self) str
    if self.pos < self.toks.len()
        self.toks[self.pos]
    else
        ""

fn P.expr(mut self)
    self.term()
    while self.peek() == "+" or self.peek() == "-"
        op := self.peek()
        self.pos += 1
        self.term()
        self.out.push(Ins(kind: if op == "+" then 3 else 4, val: 0, name: "", big: false))

fn P.term(mut self)
    self.unary()
    while self.peek() == "*" or self.peek() == "/" or self.peek() == "%"
        op := self.peek()
        self.pos += 1
        self.unary()
        k := if op == "*" then 5 elif op == "/" then 6 else 7
        self.out.push(Ins(kind: k, val: 0, name: "", big: false))

fn P.unary(mut self)
    t := self.peek()
    if t == "-"
        self.pos += 1
        self.unary()
        self.out.push(Ins(kind: 2, val: 0, name: "", big: false))
    elif t == "("
        self.pos += 1
        self.expr()
        if self.peek() == ")"
            self.pos += 1
        else
            self.bad = true
    elif t == "" 
        self.bad = true
    elif tok_kind(t) == 0
        self.pos += 1
        v := t.to_int()
        self.out.push(Ins(kind: 0, val: v else 0, name: "", big: v == none))
    elif tok_kind(t) == 1 and t != "let" and t != "print"
        self.pos += 1
        self.out.push(Ins(kind: 1, val: 0, name: t, big: false))
    else
        self.bad = true

# returns error message or "" ; sets result
fn run_line(line str, mut env Map[str, int], lineno int) str
    toks := tokenize(line) else return "syntax"
    if toks.len() == 0
        return ""
    if toks[0].starts_with("#")
        return ""
    is_let := toks[0] == "let"
    if not is_let and toks[0] != "print"
        return "syntax"
    mut start := 1
    mut target := ""
    if is_let
        if toks.len() < 3 or tok_kind(toks[1]) != 1 or toks[1] == "let" or toks[1] == "print" or toks[2] != "="
            return "syntax"
        target = toks[1]
        start = 3
    mut p := P(toks: toks, pos: start, out: List[Ins](), bad: false)
    p.expr()
    if p.bad or p.pos != toks.len()
        return "syntax"
    for ins in p.out
        if ins.kind == 1 and not env.contains(ins.name)
            return "unknown {ins.name}"
    mut st := List[int]()
    for ins in p.out
        k := ins.kind
        if k == 0
            if ins.big
                return "overflow"
            st.push(ins.val)
        elif k == 1
            st.push(env[ins.name])
        elif k == 2
            a := st.pop() else 0
            r := (0).checked_sub(a) else return "overflow"
            st.push(r)
        else
            b := st.pop() else 0
            a := st.pop() else 0
            if k == 3
                st.push(a.checked_add(b) else return "overflow")
            elif k == 4
                st.push(a.checked_sub(b) else return "overflow")
            elif k == 5
                st.push(a.checked_mul(b) else return "overflow")
            else
                if b == 0
                    return "division by zero"
                if b == -1 and a == (-9223372036854775807 - 1)
                    return "overflow"
                if k == 6
                    st.push(a.checked_div(b) else return "overflow")
                else
                    st.push(a % b)
    v := st[0]
    if is_let
        env[target] = v
    else
        print(v)
    ""

fn main()
    args := env.args()
    if args.len() > 0
        io.eprint("usage: calc")
        io.exit(1)
    text := io.read_all()
    mut vars := Map[str, int]()
    mut failed := false
    mut no := 0
    for line in text.split("\n")
        no += 1
        msg := run_line(line, mut vars, no)
        if msg != ""
            io.eprint("error: line {no}: {msg}")
            failed = true
    if failed
        io.exit(2)

struct Tok
    kind int
    text str

struct Node
    kind int
    text str
    l int
    r int

fn is_lower(c char) bool
    c >= 'a' and c <= 'z'

fn is_digit(c char) bool
    c >= '0' and c <= '9'

fn lex(line str) List[Tok] ! str
    cs := line.chars()
    mut toks := List[Tok]()
    mut i := 0
    while i < cs.len()
        c := cs[i]
        if c == ' '
            i += 1
        elif is_digit(c)
            mut j := i
            while j < cs.len() and is_digit(cs[j])
                j += 1
            toks.push(Tok(kind: 0, text: cs.slice(i, j).join("")))
            i = j
        elif is_lower(c)
            mut j := i
            while j < cs.len() and (is_lower(cs[j]) or is_digit(cs[j]) or cs[j] == '_')
                j += 1
            toks.push(Tok(kind: 1, text: cs.slice(i, j).join("")))
            i = j
        elif c == '=' or c == '+' or c == '-' or c == '*' or c == '/' or c == '%'
            toks.push(Tok(kind: 2, text: "{c}"))
            i += 1
        elif c == '('
            toks.push(Tok(kind: 3, text: "("))
            i += 1
        elif c == ')'
            toks.push(Tok(kind: 4, text: ")"))
            i += 1
        else
            return "syntax"
    toks

# kinds: 0 num, 1 var, 2 neg, 3 bin
struct Parser
    toks List[Tok]
    pos int
    nodes List[Node]

fn Parser.peek(self) Tok?
    if self.pos < self.toks.len()
        return self.toks[self.pos]
    none

fn Parser.add(mut self, n Node) int
    self.nodes.push(n)
    self.nodes.len() - 1

fn Parser.primary(mut self) int ! str
    t := self.peek() else return "syntax"
    if t.kind == 0
        self.pos += 1
        return self.add(Node(kind: 0, text: t.text, l: 0, r: 0))
    if t.kind == 1
        if t.text == "let" or t.text == "print"
            return "syntax"
        self.pos += 1
        return self.add(Node(kind: 1, text: t.text, l: 0, r: 0))
    if t.kind == 3
        self.pos += 1
        e := self.expr()?
        c := self.peek() else return "syntax"
        if c.kind != 4
            return "syntax"
        self.pos += 1
        return e
    if t.kind == 2 and t.text == "-"
        self.pos += 1
        e := self.primary()?
        return self.add(Node(kind: 2, text: "", l: e, r: 0))
    return "syntax"

fn Parser.term(mut self) int ! str
    mut a := self.primary()?
    while true
        t := self.peek() else break
        if t.kind == 2 and (t.text == "*" or t.text == "/" or t.text == "%")
            self.pos += 1
            b := self.primary()?
            a = self.add(Node(kind: 3, text: t.text, l: a, r: b))
        else
            break
    a

fn Parser.expr(mut self) int ! str
    mut a := self.term()?
    while true
        t := self.peek() else break
        if t.kind == 2 and (t.text == "+" or t.text == "-")
            self.pos += 1
            b := self.term()?
            a = self.add(Node(kind: 3, text: t.text, l: a, r: b))
        else
            break
    a

fn eval(nodes List[Node], i int) int ! str
    n := nodes[i]
    if n.kind == 0
        return n.text.to_int() else return "overflow"
    if n.kind == 1
        return 0
    if n.kind == 2
        v := eval(nodes, n.l)?
        return v.checked_neg() else return "overflow"
    a := eval(nodes, n.l)?
    b := eval(nodes, n.r)?
    if n.text == "+"
        return a.checked_add(b) else return "overflow"
    if n.text == "-"
        return a.checked_sub(b) else return "overflow"
    if n.text == "*"
        return a.checked_mul(b) else return "overflow"
    if b == 0
        return "division by zero"
    if n.text == "/"
        return a.checked_div(b) else return "overflow"
    if b == -1 and a == (-9223372036854775807 - 1)
        return "overflow"
    a % b

# evaluation with variables substituted via env
fn eval_env(nodes List[Node], i int, env Map[str, int]) int ! str
    n := nodes[i]
    if n.kind == 0
        return n.text.to_int() else return "overflow"
    if n.kind == 1
        return env[n.text]
    if n.kind == 2
        v := eval_env(nodes, n.l, env)?
        return v.checked_neg() else return "overflow"
    a := eval_env(nodes, n.l, env)?
    b := eval_env(nodes, n.r, env)?
    if n.text == "+"
        return a.checked_add(b) else return "overflow"
    if n.text == "-"
        return a.checked_sub(b) else return "overflow"
    if n.text == "*"
        return a.checked_mul(b) else return "overflow"
    if b == 0
        return "division by zero"
    if n.text == "/"
        return a.checked_div(b) else return "overflow"
    if b == -1 and a == (-9223372036854775807 - 1)
        return "overflow"
    a % b

fn run_line(line str, mut env Map[str, int], mut out List[str]) int ! str
    toks := lex(line)?
    mut start := 0
    mut target := ""
    if toks.len() == 0
        return "syntax"
    h := toks[0]
    if h.kind != 1
        return "syntax"
    if h.text == "let"
        if toks.len() < 3
            return "syntax"
        if toks[1].kind != 1 or toks[1].text == "let" or toks[1].text == "print"
            return "syntax"
        if toks[2].kind != 2 or toks[2].text != "="
            return "syntax"
        target = toks[1].text
        start = 3
    elif h.text == "print"
        start = 1
    else
        return "syntax"
    rest := toks.slice(start)
    mut p := Parser(toks: rest, pos: 0, nodes: [])
    root := p.expr()?
    if p.pos != rest.len()
        return "syntax"
    for t in rest
        if t.kind == 1 and not env.contains(t.text)
            return "unknown {t.text}"
    v := eval_env(p.nodes, root, env)?
    if target == ""
        out.push("{v}")
    else
        env[target] = v
    0

fn main()
    if env.args().len() > 0
        io.eprint("usage: calc")
        io.exit(1)
    text := io.read_all()
    mut vars := Map[str, int]()
    mut failed := false
    mut k := 0
    for line in text.split("\n")
        k += 1
        mut blank := true
        mut first := ' '
        for c in line.chars()
            if c != ' '
                first = c
                blank = false
                break
        if blank or first == '#'
            continue
        mut out := List[str]()
        _ := run_line(line, mut vars, mut out) else e
            io.eprint("error: line {k}: {e}")
            failed = true
            continue
        for s in out
            print(s)
    if failed
        io.exit(2)

# ledger

Write `ledger`, a command-line program. It reads a CSV of transactions from stdin and prints a report.

Input: the first line is exactly `date,account,amount_cents,memo`. Every other line has exactly four comma-separated fields (no quoting; memo may be empty and has no commas). `date` is `YYYY-MM-DD` (digits only, month 01-12, day 01-31). `account` is non-empty. `amount_cents` is an integer with an optional leading `-`.     mut lo := a.lo + r

        lo += 1000000000
        hi -= 1
    elif lo >= 1000000000

    ml := m.2

Input: the first line is exactly `date,account,amount_cents,memo`. Every other line has exactly four comma-separated fields (no quoting; memo may be empty and has no commas). `date` is `YYYY-MM-DD` (digits only, month 01-12, day 01-31). `account` is non-empty. `amount_cents` is an integer with an optional leading `-`. A line that breaks any rule is skipped and reported on stderr as `error: line K: REASON` (K is the 1-based line number, header is line 1). If any line was skipped the exit code is 2, else 0, but stdout is still printed. A bad header prints `error: line 1: bad header`, nothing on stdout, exit 2. Empty input is a bad header. A trailing blank line at the end of input is ignored.

Commands (first argument):
- `balance`: one line per account, `ACCOUNT<TAB>AMOUNT`, accounts in ascending byte order.
- `top N`: the N transactions with the largest absolute amount, one per line `DATE<TAB>ACCOUNT<TAB>AMOUNT<TAB>MEMO`, largest first, ties in input order. Fewer than N lines if fewer exist. N is a non-negative integer.
- `monthly`: one line per `YYYY-MM`, `MONTH<TAB>AMOUNT`, months ascending.

AMOUNT prints cents as dollars with exactly two decimals and a leading `-` for negatives: `1234.05`, `-0.50`, `0.00`. Amounts fit in 64-bit signed integers; sums may be large.

A missing, unknown or malformed command (including a bad N) prints `usage: ledger balance|top N|monthly` on stderr and exits 1 without reading stdin.

Layout: sources live in `src/` (`src/main.ail`, `src/main.c` or `src/main.rs`); `./build` builds `./ledger`; `./test` runs the visible cases.

struct Tx
    date str
    account str
    amt int
    memo str

fn usage() never
    io.eprint("usage: ledger balance|top N|monthly")
    io.exit(1)

fn all_digits(s str) bool
    for c in s.chars()
        if c < '0' or c > '9'
            return false
    true

fn valid_date(d str) bool
    if d.len() != 10
        return false
    if d.slice(4, 5) != "-" or d.slice(7, 8) != "-"
        return false
    y := d.slice(0, 4)
    m := d.slice(5, 7)
    dd := d.slice(8, 10)
    if not all_digits(y) or not all_digits(m) or not all_digits(dd)
        return false
    mn := m.to_int() else 0
    dn := dd.to_int() else 0
    mn >= 1 and mn <= 12 and dn >= 1 and dn <= 31

# cents as (h, l): value = h * 1e9 + l, normalised to the same sign
fn fmt(h0 int, l0 int) str
    mut h := h0 + l0 / 1000000000
    mut l := l0 % 1000000000
    if h > 0 and l < 0
        h -= 1
        l += 1000000000
    elif h < 0 and l > 0
        h += 1
        l -= 1000000000
    neg := h < 0 or l < 0
    ah := if h < 0 then -h else h
    al := if l < 0 then -l else l
    mut digits := "{al}"
    if ah > 0
        digits = "{ah}{al:09}"
    if digits.len() < 3
        digits = "{digits:0>3}"
    n := digits.len()
    body := "{digits.slice(0, n - 2)}.{digits.slice(n - 2, n)}"
    if neg
        return "-{body}"
    body

fn money(a int) str
    fmt(a / 1000000000, a % 1000000000)

fn absv(a int) int
    if a < 0 then -a else a

fn main() !
    args := env.args()
    if args.len() < 1
        usage()
    cmd := args[0]
    mut topn := 0
    if cmd == "top"
        if args.len() != 2 or args[1].len() == 0 or not all_digits(args[1])
            usage()
        topn = args[1].to_int() else usage()
    elif cmd == "balance" or cmd == "monthly"
        if args.len() != 1
            usage()
    else
        usage()
    text := io.read_all()
    lines := text.lines()
    if lines.len() == 0 or lines[0] != "date,account,amount_cents,memo"
        io.eprint("error: line 1: bad header")
        io.exit(2)
    mut txs := List[Tx]()
    mut bad := false
    for i, line in lines.enumerate()
        if i == 0
            continue
        if i == lines.len() - 1 and line == ""
            continue
        f := line.split(",")
        mut why := ""
        if f.len() != 4
            why = "wrong field count"
        elif not valid_date(f[0])
            why = "bad date"
        elif f[1].len() == 0
            why = "empty account"
        elif f[2].to_int() == none
            why = "bad amount"
        if why != ""
            io.eprint("error: line {i + 1}: {why}")
            bad = true
            continue
        a := f[2].to_int() else 0
        txs.push(Tx(date: f[0], account: f[1], amt: a, memo: f[3]))
    if cmd == "top"
        s1 := txs.sorted(by: |t| -absv(t.amt % 1000000000))
        s2 := s1.sorted(by: |t| -absv(t.amt / 1000000000))
        mut k := 0
        for t in s2
            if k >= topn
                break
            print("{t.date}\t{t.account}\t{money(t.amt)}\t{t.memo}")
            k += 1
    else
        mut hs := Map[str, int]()
        mut ls := Map[str, int]()
        for t in txs
            key := if cmd == "balance" then t.account else t.date.slice(0, 7)
            hs[key] += t.amt / 1000000000
            ls[key] += t.amt % 1000000000
        for key in hs.keys().sorted()
            print("{key}\t{fmt(hs[key], ls[key])}")
    if bad
        io.exit(2)

    date str
    account str
    amount int
    memo str

fn usage() never
    io.eprint("usage: ledger balance|top N|monthly")
    io.exit(1)

fn fmt_parts(q int, r int) str
    # q whole dollars (truncated), r cents remainder, both any sign
    mut qq := q + r / 100
    mut rr := r % 100
    if qq > 0 and rr < 0
        qq -= 1
        rr += 100
    elif qq < 0 and rr > 0
        qq += 1
        rr -= 100
    neg := qq < 0 or rr < 0
    mut a := qq
    if a < 0
        a = -a
    mut c := rr
    if c < 0
        c = -c
    sign := if neg then "-" else ""
    "{sign}{a}.{c:02}"

fn fmt(a int) str
    s := a.to_str()
    neg := s.starts_with("-")
    mut d := s
    if neg
        d = s.slice(1, s.len())
    while d.len() < 3
        d = "0{d}"
    sign := if neg then "-" else ""
    "{sign}{d.slice(0, d.len() - 2)}.{d.slice(d.len() - 2, d.len())}"

fn all_digits(s str) bool
    for c in s.chars()
        if c < '0' or c > '9'
            return false

        return true

        return true

    mo := d.slice(5, 7)
    dy := d.slice(8, 10)
    if not all_digits(y) or not all_digits(mo) or not all_digits(dy)

    m := mo.to_int() else 0
    n := dy.to_int() else 0

        usage()

        if args.len() != 2
            usage()
        topn = args[1].to_int() else usage()
        if topn < 0
            usage()

        if args.len() != 1
            usage()

        usage()

    mut lines := text.lines()
    if lines.len() > 0 and lines[lines.len() - 1] == ""
        lines.pop()
    if lines.len() == 0 or lines[0] != "date,account,amount_cents,memo"

            why = "bad date"

            why = "empty account"

            why = "bad amount"

            bad = true

            amt := parts[2].to_int() else 0

            qs[key] += t.amount / 100
            rs[key] += t.amount % 100
        for key in qs.keys().sorted()
            print("{key}\t{fmt_parts(qs[key], rs[key])}")
    else
        p1 := txs.sorted(by: |t| -(t.amount % 2 * t.amount % 2))

            if shown < topn
                print("{t.date}\t{t.account}\t{fmt(t.amount)}\t{t.memo}")

        return "wrong field count"
    if not date_ok(f[0])
        return "bad date"
    if f[1].len() == 0

    a := f[2]
    body := if a.starts_with("-") then a.slice(1, a.len()) else a

    Tx(date: f[0], account: f[1], amount: n, memo: f[3])

    mut c := cc % 100
    if d > 0 and c < 0

    ad := if d < 0 then -d else d
    ac := if c < 0 then -c else c

        usage()

# depgraph

Write `depgraph`, a command-line program. It reads a dependency list from stdin and answers one question about it.

Input, one item per line:
- `A -> B` means A needs B.
- `A` alone declares a node with no dependencies yet.
- An empty line or a line starting with `#` is ignored.
- A name is one or more of `a-z A-Z 0-9 _ . -`. The separator is exactly one space, `->`, one space. Any other line (extra or missing spaces, a third name, an illegal character, a carriage return) is bad: skip it and print `error: line K: bad line` to stderr (K is 1-based). Repeated edges count once. `A -> A` is a self-dependency. There are at most 500 distinct names.

Commands (first argument), output on stdout, one name per line:
- `order`: every node, dependencies first. Among nodes ready at the same time, the smallest name in byte order comes first.
- `cycles`: every node that lies on a cycle (reaches itself through one or more edges), in ascending byte order.
- `deps NAME`: everything NAME needs, directly or not, ascending. NAME itself appears only if it lies on a cycle.
- `rdeps NAME`: everything that needs NAME, directly or not, ascending, under the same rule.

Exit codes, first that applies wins: 1 for a missing, unknown or malformed command, including a wrong number of arguments and a NAME argument that is not a valid name by the rule above (print `usage: depgraph order|cycles|deps NAME|rdeps NAME` to stderr, do not read stdin); 4 if `deps`/`rdeps` names a node that is not in the input (print `error: unknown ` and the name to stderr, e.g. `error: unknown lib`, nothing on stdout); 3 if `order` finds a cycle (print `error: cycle` to stderr, nothing on stdout); 2 if any line was bad (stdout is still printed); else 0.

fn usage() never
    io.eprint("usage: depgraph order|cycles|deps NAME|rdeps NAME")
    io.exit(1)

fn valid(s str) bool
    if s.is_empty()
        return false
    for c in s.chars()
        ok := match c
            'a'..='z' => true
            'A'..='Z' => true
            '0'..='9' => true
            '_' | '.' | '-' => true
            _ => false
        if not ok
            return false
    true

fn reach(g Map[str, Set[str]], start str) Set[str]
    mut seen := Set[str]()
    mut stack := (g.get(start) else Set[str]()).to_list()
    while top := stack.pop()
        if seen.add(top)
            for n in g.get(top) else Set[str]()
                stack.push(n)
    seen

fn main()
    args := env.args()
    if args.len() == 0
        usage()
    cmd := args[0]
    if cmd == "order" or cmd == "cycles"
        if args.len() != 1
            usage()
    elif cmd == "deps" or cmd == "rdeps"
        if args.len() != 2 or not valid(args[1])
            usage()
    else
        usage()
    text := io.read_all()
    mut adj := Map[str, Set[str]]()
    mut radj := Map[str, Set[str]]()
    mut nodes := Set[str]()
    mut bad := false
    mut k := 0
    for line in text.split("\n")
        k += 1
        if line.is_empty() or line.starts_with("#")
            continue
        parts := line.split(" -> ")
        if parts.len() == 1 and valid(line)
            nodes.add(line)
        elif parts.len() == 2 and valid(parts[0]) and valid(parts[1])
            a := parts[0]
            b := parts[1]
            nodes.add(a)
            nodes.add(b)
            if not adj.contains(a)
                adj[a] = Set[str]()
            if not radj.contains(b)
                radj[b] = Set[str]()
            adj[a].add(b)
            radj[b].add(a)
        else
            bad = true
            io.eprint("error: line {k}: bad line")
    names := nodes.sorted()
    mut out := List[str]()
    if cmd == "order"
        mut indeg := Map[str, int]()
        for n in names
            indeg[n] = (adj.get(n) else Set[str]()).len()
        mut ready := names.filter(|n| indeg[n] == 0)
        mut done := 0
        while ready.len() > 0
            ready.sort()
            n := ready[0]
            ready.remove_at(0)
            out.push(n)
            done += 1
            for p in radj.get(n) else Set[str]()
                indeg[p] -= 1
                if indeg[p] == 0
                    ready.push(p)
        if done != names.len()
            io.eprint("error: cycle")
            io.exit(3)
    elif cmd == "cycles"
        out = names.filter(|n| reach(adj, n).contains(n))
    else

        if not nodes.contains(name)
            io.eprint("error: unknown {name}")
            io.exit(4)
        g := if cmd == "deps" then adj else radj
        out = reach(g, name).sorted()
    for n in out
        print(n)
    if bad
        io.exit(2)

fn usage() never
    io.eprint("usage: invjson json [TITLE]|tags")

fn all_in(s str, allowed str) bool
    if s.len() == 0
        return false
    for c in s.chars()
        if not allowed.contains("{c}")
            return false
    true

fn esc(s str) str
    mut out := []
    for c in s.chars()
        n := c.code()
        if c == '"'
            out.push("\\\"")
        elif c == '\\'
            out.push("\\\\")
        elif n == 9
            out.push("\\t")
        elif n == 10
            out.push("\\n")
        elif n < 32
            h := n.to_hex()
            out.push("\\u00{h:0>2}")
        else
            out.push("{c}")
    out.join("")

fn main()
    args := env.args()
    if args.len() == 0
        usage()
    cmd := args[0]
    if cmd == "json"
        if args.len() > 2
            usage()
    elif cmd == "tags"
        if args.len() != 1
            usage()
    else

    lower := "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"

    mut tags := Map[str, List[str]]()
    mut bad := false
    mut k := 0

        parts := line.split(" ")

                if not all_in(parts[i], lower)
                    ok = false
        if not ok
            io.eprint("error: line {k}: bad line")
            bad = true
            continue
        sku := parts[0]
        n := parts[1].to_int() else 0
        if not qty.contains(sku)
            qty[sku] = 0
            tags[sku] = []
        qty[sku] += n
        mut tl := tags[sku]
        for i in 2..parts.len()
            if not tl.contains(parts[i])
                tl.push(parts[i])
        tags[sku] = tl
    if cmd == "json"
        mut lines := ["\{"]
        if args.len() == 2
            lines.push("  \"title\": \"{esc(args[1])}\",")
        skus := qty.keys().sorted()
        if skus.len() == 0
            lines.push("  \"items\": [],")
        else
            lines.push("  \"items\": [")
            for i, s in skus.enumerate()
                tg := [ "\"{t}\"" for t in tags[s] ].join(", ")
                comma := if i < skus.len() - 1 then "," else ""
                lines.push("    \{\"sku\": \"{s}\", \"qty\": {qty[s]}, \"tags\": [{tg}]}{comma}")
            lines.push("  ],")
        mut total := 0
        for s in skus
            total += qty[s]
        lines.push("  \"total\": {total}")
        lines.push("}")
        print(lines.join("\n"))
    else
        mut sums := Map[str, int]()
        for s in qty.keys()
            for t in tags[s]
                sums[t] += qty[s]
        names := sums.keys().sorted()
        for t in names.sorted(by: |x| -sums[x])
            print("{t}\t{sums[t]}")
    if bad
        io.exit(2)

# invjson

Write `invjson`, a command-line program. It reads an inventory from stdin and prints it as JSON, or as a tag summary.

Input, one item per line: `SKU QTY` followed by zero or more `TAG`s, separated by exactly one space.
- SKU is one or more of `A-Z 0-9 -`. QTY is one to seven decimal digits (no sign). A TAG is one or more of `a-z`.
- An empty line or a line starting with `#` is ignored.
- Any other line (extra or missing spaces, a bad character, a carriage return) is bad: skip it and print
  `error: line K: bad line` to stderr (K is 1-based).
- A SKU seen again adds its QTY to the earlier total and adds its tags that are new to that SKU, after the earlier ones.
  A tag repeated on one line counts once.

Commands (first argument):
- `json` or `json TITLE`: the inventory as JSON, exactly in this layout (two-space indent, one item per line,
  items in ascending byte order of SKU, tags in the order first seen):

  ```

    "title": "Spring count",
    "items": [
      {"sku": "A-1", "qty": 3, "tags": ["red", "big"]},
      {"sku": "B7", "qty": 0, "tags": []}
    ],
    "total": 3
  }
  ```

  `"total"` is the sum of all quantities. In TITLE, `"` is written `\"`, `\` is written `\\`, a tab `\t`, a newline
  `\n`, any other character below U+0020 as `\u00XX` with lowercase hex digits; every other character as it is.
- `tags`: one line per tag, `TAG<TAB>QTY`, where QTY is the sum over the items that carry the tag; larger QTY first,
  equal QTY in ascending byte order of TAG.

fn usage() never
    io.eprint("usage: invjson json [TITLE]|tags")
    io.exit(1)

fn valid_sku(s str) bool
    if s.is_empty()
        return false
    for c in s.chars()
        ok := match c
            'A'..='Z' => true
            '0'..='9' => true
            '-' => true
            _ => false
        if not ok
            return false
    true

fn valid_qty(s str) bool
    if s.len() < 1 or s.len() > 7
        return false
    for c in s.chars()
        if c < '0' or c > '9'
            return false
    true

fn valid_tag(s str) bool
    if s.is_empty()
        return false
    for c in s.chars()
        if c < 'a' or c > 'z'
            return false
    true

fn esc(s str) str
    mut out := []
    for c in s.chars()
        n := c.code()
        piece := match c
            '"' => "\\\""
            '\\' => "\\\\"
            '\t' => "\\t"
            '\n' => "\\n"
            _ => if n < 32 then "\\u00{n.to_hex().pad_left(2, '0')}" else "{c}"
        out.push(piece)
    out.join("")

fn main()
    args := env.args()
    if args.len() == 0
        usage()
    cmd := args[0]
    if cmd == "json"
        if args.len() > 2
            usage()
    elif cmd == "tags"
        if args.len() != 1
            usage()
    else
        usage()
    text := io.read_all()
    mut qty := Map[str, int]()
    mut tags := Map[str, List[str]]()
    mut bad := false
    mut k := 0
    for line in text.split("\n")
        k += 1
        if line.is_empty() or line.starts_with("#")
            continue
        parts := line.split(" ")
        mut ok := parts.len() >= 2 and valid_sku(parts[0]) and valid_qty(parts[1])
        if ok
            for t in parts.skip(2)
                if not valid_tag(t)
                    ok = false
        if not ok
            bad = true
            io.eprint("error: line {k}: bad line")
            continue
        sku := parts[0]
        n := parts[1].to_int() else 0
        if not qty.contains(sku)
            qty[sku] = 0
            tags[sku] = []
        qty[sku] += n
        for t in parts.skip(2)
            if not tags[sku].contains(t)
                tags[sku].push(t)
    if cmd == "json"
        mut lines := []
        lines.push("\{")

            lines.push("  \"title\": \"{esc(args[1])}\",")
        skus := qty.keys().sorted()
        if skus.is_empty()

struct Tx

    account str
    amount int
    memo str
    seq int

fn usage() never
    io.eprint("usage: ledger balance|top N|monthly")
    io.exit(1)

fn money(x int) str
    q := x / 100
    r := x % 100
    if x < 0
        "-{-q}.{-r:02}"
    else
        "{q}.{r:02}"

fn all_digits(s str) bool
    if s.len() == 0
        return false
    for c in s.chars()
        if c < '0' or c > '9'
            return false
    true

fn check_date(d str) str?
    if d.len() != 10
        return "bad date"
    ys := d.slice(0, 4)
    ms := d.slice(5, 7)
    ds := d.slice(8, 10)
    if d.slice(4, 5) != "-" or d.slice(7, 8) != "-"
        return "bad date"
    if not all_digits(ys) or not all_digits(ms) or not all_digits(ds)
        return "bad date"
    m := ms.to_int() else 0
    dd := ds.to_int() else 0
    if m < 1 or m > 12 or dd < 1 or dd > 31
        return "bad date"
    none

fn main()
    args := env.args()
    if args.len() == 0
        usage()
    cmd := args[0]
    mut n := 0
    if cmd == "top"
        if args.len() != 2
            usage()
        n = args[1].to_int() else usage()
        if n < 0
            usage()
    elif cmd == "balance" or cmd == "monthly"
        if args.len() != 1
            usage()
    else
        usage()
    mut lines := io.read_all().lines()
    if lines.len() == 0 or lines[0] != "date,account,amount_cents,memo"
        io.eprint("error: line 1: bad header")
        io.exit(2)

        lines.pop()
    mut txs := List[Tx]()
    mut bad := false
    for i, line in lines.enumerate()
        if i == 0
            continue
        f := line.split(",")
        mut why := "wrong field count"
        mut ok := false
        mut amt := 0
        if f.len() == 4
            e := check_date(f[0])
            if e != none
                why = "bad date"
            elif f[1] == ""
                why = "empty account"
            else
                a := f[2]
                body := if a.starts_with("-") then a.slice(1, a.len()) else a
                v := a.to_int()
                if all_digits(body) and v != none
                    amt = v else 0
                    ok = true
                else
                    why = "bad amount"
        if ok
            txs.push(Tx(date: f[0], account: f[1], amount: amt, memo: f[3], seq: i))
        else
            bad = true
            io.eprint("error: line {i + 1}: {why}")
    if cmd == "balance"
        mut m := Map[str, int]()
        for t in txs
            m[t.account] += t.amount
        for k in m.keys().sorted()
            print("{k}\t{money(m[k])}")
    elif cmd == "monthly"
        mut m := Map[str, int]()
        for t in txs
            m[t.date.slice(0, 7)] += t.amount
        for k in m.keys().sorted()
            print("{k}\t{money(m[k])}")
    else
        order := txs.sorted(by: |t| (if t.amount < 0 then t.amount else -t.amount, t.seq))
        mut c := 0
        for t in order
            if c >= n
                break
            print("{t.date}\t{t.account}\t{money(t.amount)}\t{t.memo}")
            c += 1
    if bad
        io.exit(2)

    mi := m.to_int() else 0

    mi >= 1 and mi <= 12 and di >= 1 and di <= 31

Write `ledger`, a command-line program. It reads a CSV of transactions from stdin and prints a report.

Input: the first line is exactly `date,account,amount_cents,memo`. Every other line has exactly four comma-separated fields (no quoting; memo may be empty and has no commas). `date` is `YYYY-MM-DD` (digits only, month 01-12, day 01-31). `account` is non-empty. `amount_cents` is an integer with an optional leading `-`. A line that breaks any rule is skipped and reported on stderr as `error: line K: REASON` (K is the 1-based line number, header is line 1). If any line was skipped the exit code is 2, else 0, but stdout is still printed. A bad header prints `error: line 1: bad header`, nothing on stdout, exit 2. Empty input is a bad header. A trailing blank line at the end of input is ignored.

Commands (first argument):
- `balance`: one line per account, `ACCOUNT<TAB>AMOUNT`, accounts in ascending byte order.
- `top N`: the N transactions with the largest absolute amount, one per line `DATE<TAB>ACCOUNT<TAB>AMOUNT<TAB>MEMO`, largest first, ties in input order. Fewer than N lines if fewer exist. N is a non-negative integer.
- `monthly`: one line per `YYYY-MM`, `MONTH<TAB>AMOUNT`, months ascending.

AMOUNT prints cents as dollars with exactly two decimals and a leading `-` for negatives: `1234.05`, `-0.50`, `0.00`. Amounts fit in 64-bit signed integers; sums may be large.

A missing, unknown or malformed command (including a bad N) prints `usage: ledger balance|top N|monthly` on stderr and exits 1 without reading stdin.

Layout: sources live in `src/` (`src/main.ail`, `src/main.c` or `src/main.rs`); `./build` builds `./ledger`; `./test` runs the visible cases.

struct Tx
    date str
    account str
    amount int
    memo str

fn usage() never
    io.eprint("usage: ledger balance|top N|monthly")
    io.exit(1)

fn money(b bigint.BigInt) str
    neg := b < bigint.from_int(0)
    s := if neg then "{-b}" else "{b}"
    p := s.pad_left(3, '0')
    n := p.len()
    body := "{p.slice(0, n - 2)}.{p.slice(n - 2)}"
    if neg then "-{body}" else body

fn digits(s str) bool
    s.chars().all(|c| c >= '0' and c <= '9')

fn valid_date(d str) str?
    if d.len() != 10
        return "bad date"
    if d.char_at(4) != '-' or d.char_at(7) != '-'
        return "bad date"
    y := d.slice(0, 4)
    m := d.slice(5, 7)
    dd := d.slice(8, 10)
    if not (digits(y) and digits(m) and digits(dd))
        return "bad date"
    mi := m.to_int() else 0
    di := dd.to_int() else 0
    if mi < 1 or mi > 12 or di < 1 or di > 31
        return "bad date"
    none

fn parse_line(line str) Tx ! str
    f := line.split(",")
    if f.len() != 4
        return "wrong field count"
    bad := valid_date(f[0])
    if bad != none
        return "bad date"
    if f[1] == ""
        return "empty account"
    a := f[2].to_int() else return "bad amount"
    Tx(date: f[0], account: f[1], amount: a, memo: f[3])

fn main()
    args := env.args()
    if args.len() < 1
        usage()
    cmd := args[0]
    mut topn := 0
    if cmd == "top"
        if args.len() != 2
            usage()
        topn = args[1].to_int() else usage()
        if topn < 0
            usage()
    elif (cmd == "balance" or cmd == "monthly") and args.len() == 1
        topn = 0
    else
        usage()
    text := io.read_all()
    mut lines := text.lines()
    while lines.len() > 0 and lines[lines.len() - 1] == ""
        lines.pop()
    if lines.len() == 0 or lines[0] != "date,account,amount_cents,memo"
        io.eprint("error: line 1: bad header")
        io.exit(2)
    mut txs := List[Tx]()
    mut errs := 0
    for i in 1..lines.len()
        t := parse_line(lines[i]) else e
            io.eprint("error: line {i + 1}: {e}")
            errs += 1
            continue
        txs.push(t)
    mut out := List[str]()
    if cmd == "balance"
        mut m := Map[str, bigint.BigInt]()
        for t in txs
            m[t.account] = (m.get(t.account) else bigint.from_int(0)) + bigint.from_int(t.amount)
        for k in m.keys().sorted()
            out.push("{k}\t{money(m[k])}")
    elif cmd == "monthly"
        mut m := Map[str, bigint.BigInt]()
        for t in txs
            k := t.date.slice(0, 7)
            m[k] = (m.get(k) else bigint.from_int(0)) + bigint.from_int(t.amount)
        for k in m.keys().sorted()
            out.push("{k}\t{money(m[k])}")
    else
        s := txs.sorted(by: |t| if t.amount < 0 then t.amount else -t.amount)
        for t in s.take(topn)
            out.push("{t.date}\t{t.account}\t{money(bigint.from_int(t.amount))}\t{t.memo}")
    if out.len() > 0
        print(out.join("\n"))
    if errs > 0
        io.exit(2)

struct Tx
    date str
    account str
    amount int
    memo str

fn usage() never
    io.eprint("usage: ledger balance|top N|monthly")
    io.exit(1)

fn fmt(b bigint.BigInt) str
    s := "{b}"
    neg := s.starts_with("-")
    digits := if neg then s.slice(1) else s
    d := digits.pad_left(3, '0')
    n := d.len()
    body := "{d.slice(0, n - 2)}.{d.slice(n - 2)}"
    if neg then "-{body}" else body

fn is_digits(s str) bool
    s.chars().all(|c| c >= '0' and c <= '9')

fn check_date(d str) bool
    if d.len() != 10
        return false
    if d.slice(4, 5) != "-" or d.slice(7, 8) != "-"
        return false
    y := d.slice(0, 4)
    m := d.slice(5, 7)
    dd := d.slice(8, 10)
    if not (is_digits(y) and is_digits(m) and is_digits(dd))
        return false
    mi := m.to_int() else 0
    di := dd.to_int() else 0
    mi >= 1 and mi <= 12 and di >= 1 and di <= 31

fn abskey(a int) (int, int)
    if a >= 0
        return (-(a / 2), -(a % 2))
    m := -(a + 1)
    if m % 2 == 0
        (-(m / 2), -1)
    else
        (-(m / 2 + 1), 0)

fn main()
    args := env.args()
    mut cmd := ""
    mut topn := 0
    if args.len() == 0
        usage()
    cmd = args[0]
    if cmd == "balance" or cmd == "monthly"
        if args.len() != 1
            usage()
    elif cmd == "top"
        if args.len() != 2
            usage()
        topn = args[1].to_int() else usage()
        if topn < 0 or not is_digits(args[1])
            usage()
    else
        usage()

    text := io.read_all()
    mut lines := text.split("\n")
    if lines.len() > 0 and lines[lines.len() - 1] == ""
        lines.pop()
    if lines.len() == 0 or lines[0] != "date,account,amount_cents,memo"
        io.eprint("error: line 1: bad header")
        io.exit(2)
    mut txs := List[Tx]()
    mut bad := false
    for i in 1..lines.len()
        f := lines[i].split(",")
        k := i + 1
        mut why := ""
        if f.len() != 4
            why = "wrong field count"
        elif not check_date(f[0])
            why = "bad date"
        elif f[1] == ""
            why = "empty account"
        else
            amt := f[2].to_int()
            if amt == none
                why = "bad amount"
            else
                txs.push(Tx(date: f[0], account: f[1], amount: amt else 0, memo: f[3]))
        if why != ""
            bad = true
            io.eprint("error: line {k}: {why}")
    out := List[str]()
    mut res := out
    if cmd == "balance"
        mut m := Map[str, bigint.BigInt]()
        for t in txs
            m[t.account] = (m.get(t.account) else bigint.from_int(0)) + bigint.from_int(t.amount)
        for a in m.keys().sorted()
            res.push("{a}\t{fmt(m[a])}")
    elif cmd == "monthly"
        mut m := Map[str, bigint.BigInt]()
        for t in txs
            mo := t.date.slice(0, 7)
            m[mo] = (m.get(mo) else bigint.from_int(0)) + bigint.from_int(t.amount)
        for a in m.keys().sorted()
            res.push("{a}\t{fmt(m[a])}")
    else
        s := txs.sorted(by: |t| abskey(t.amount))
        for t in s.take(topn)
            res.push("{t.date}\t{t.account}\t{fmt(bigint.from_int(t.amount))}\t{t.memo}")

        print(res.join("\n"))

        io.exit(2)

# stock

`stock` is a command-line program that reads a stock log on stdin and prints a report about it.

Input: one event per line. Fields are separated by exactly one space.
- `receive SKU QTY PRICE`: QTY units arrive, each costing PRICE cents.
- `ship SKU QTY`: QTY units leave.
- `count SKU QTY`: a stocktake found QTY units on hand.

SKU is one or more of `A-Z 0-9 -`. QTY and PRICE are 1 to 5 digits (`0-9`, no sign). QTY must be at least 1 for `receive` and `ship`, and may be 0 for `count`. An empty line or a line starting with `#` is ignored, but still counts for line numbers. A trailing newline at the end of input is not an extra line. A carriage return is part of the line, so a line ending in `\r` (a Windows line ending) is not a valid event.

Each SKU has an on-hand quantity and a cost (total cents), both starting at 0 the first time the SKU is received:
- `receive` adds QTY to the quantity and QTY × PRICE to the cost.
- `ship` removes QTY units at their average cost: the cost falls by `cost × QTY / quantity` (integer division, rounded down), then the quantity falls by QTY.
- `count` sets the quantity to QTY. If the old quantity was above 0, the cost becomes `cost × QTY / old quantity` (rounded down); otherwise the cost is unchanged.

A line that breaks a rule is skipped, and one line goes to stderr, where K is the 1-based line number:
- `error: line K: bad line` for a line that is not a valid event;
- `error: line K: unknown ` and the SKU itself, for `ship` or `count` of a SKU never received: `error: line 3: unknown AB-1`;
- `error: line K: short ` and the SKU itself, for `ship` of more units than are on hand: `error: line 4: short AB-1`.

The word `SKU` never appears in these lines; it stands for the SKU's own text.

Nothing else is printed to stderr, apart from the usage line below.

Commands (first argument), output on stdout:
- `report`: one line per SKU ever received, `SKU<TAB>QUANTITY<TAB>VALUE`, SKUs in ascending byte order. VALUE is the cost.
- `low N`: every SKU ever received whose quantity is below N, one per line, ascending. N is 1 to 5 digits.
- `total`: one line, the sum of every SKU's cost.

Money prints cents as dollars with exactly two decimals and a leading `-` for negatives: `1234.05`, `0.50`, `0.00`.

Exit codes: 1 for a missing, unknown or malformed command, including a wrong number of arguments and an `N` that is not 1 to 5 digits (print `usage: stock report|low N|total` to stderr; do not read stdin); 2 if any line was skipped (stdout is still printed); else 0.

Layout: the program lives in `src/`; `./build` builds `./stock`; `./test` runs the visible cases.
