## Pricing of order lines (spec "Prices"). The amounts are computed from the fields an
## order fixes when it is placed (price, tax rate, tier discount) and the order's promo.
use catalog
use customers
use promos

pub struct Line
    pub sku str
    pub qty int
    pub price int
    pub cat str
    ## Tax rate of the category, in percent, when the order was placed.
    pub rate int
    ## Tier discount of the customer, in percent, when the order was placed.
    pub tier int
    pub gross int
    ## Tier discount plus promo discount.
    pub discount int
    pub net int
    pub tax int
    pub total int
    ## What the shipped units cost the shop; 0 until the order ships.
    pub cost int
    ## Units returned, and the net, tax and cost shares taken back so far.
    pub back int
    pub back_net int
    pub back_tax int
    pub back_cost int

## A line whose amounts `priced` has still to fill in.
pub fn fresh_line(sku str, qty int, price int, cat str, rate int, tier int) Line
    Line(
        sku: sku,
        qty: qty,
        price: price,
        cat: cat,
        rate: rate,
        tier: tier,
        gross: 0,
        discount: 0,
        net: 0,
        tax: 0,
        total: 0,
        cost: 0,
        back: 0,
        back_net: 0,
        back_tax: 0,
        back_cost: 0,
    )

## The line with its amounts computed. The promo (`promo_pct` off lines of `promo_cat`)
## applies only to lines of that category; pass `""` when the order has no promo.
pub fn priced(l Line, promo_cat str, promo_pct int) Line
    mut p := l
    p.gross = l.price * l.qty
    tier_off := customers.discount(p.gross, l.tier)
    mut promo_off := 0
    if promo_cat == l.cat
        promo_off = promos.discount(p.gross - tier_off, promo_pct)
    p.discount = tier_off + promo_off
    p.net = p.gross - p.discount
    p.tax = catalog.tax(p.net, l.rate)
    p.total = p.net + p.tax
    p

## The shapes of journal and command-line fields (spec "Fields").

fn upper(ch char) bool
    match ch
        'A'..='Z' => true
        _ => false

fn lower(ch char) bool
    match ch
        'a'..='z' => true
        _ => false

fn digit(ch char) bool
    match ch
        '0'..='9' => true
        _ => false

fn sku_char(ch char) bool
    upper(ch) or digit(ch) or ch == '-'

fn code_char(ch char) bool
    upper(ch) or digit(ch)

fn id_char(ch char) bool
    lower(ch) or digit(ch)

## `lo` to `hi` characters, the first accepted by `first` and every one by `rest`.
fn shaped(s str, lo int, hi int, first fn(char) bool, rest fn(char) bool) bool
    if s.len() < lo or s.len() > hi
        return false
    cs := s.chars()
    if not first(cs[0])
        return false
    for ch in cs
        if not rest(ch)
            return false
    true

## 1 to `width` ASCII digits, as a number (leading zeros allowed); `none` for anything else.
pub fn digits(s str, width int) int?
    if s.is_empty() or s.len() > width
        return none
    for ch in s.chars()
        if not digit(ch)
            return none
    s.to_int()

## SKU: 1 to 12 of `A-Z 0-9 -`, starting with a letter.
pub fn is_sku(s str) bool
    shaped(s, 1, 12, upper, sku_char)

## CAT: 1 to 12 letters `a-z`.
pub fn is_cat(s str) bool
    shaped(s, 1, 12, lower, lower)

## ID: 1 to 12 of `a-z 0-9`, starting with a letter.
pub fn is_id(s str) bool
    shaped(s, 1, 12, lower, id_char)

## CODE: 3 to 10 of `A-Z 0-9`, starting with a letter.
pub fn is_code(s str) bool
    shaped(s, 3, 10, upper, code_char)

## ORDER: `o` and 1 to 6 digits.
pub fn is_order(s str) bool
    rest := s.strip_prefix("o") else return false
    (digits(rest, 6) else -1) >= 0

## PO: `p` and 1 to 6 digits.
pub fn is_po(s str) bool
    rest := s.strip_prefix("p") else return false
    (digits(rest, 6) else -1) >= 0

## CARD: `g` and 1 to 6 digits.
pub fn is_card(s str) bool
    rest := s.strip_prefix("g") else return false
    (digits(rest, 6) else -1) >= 0

## TIER: `basic`, `silver` or `gold`.
pub fn is_tier(s str) bool
    s == "basic" or s == "silver" or s == "gold"

## `a × p / 100` rounded to the nearest cent, halves up. `a` is never negative.

## The command line: which report to print (spec "Reports", "Exit codes and stderr").
use fields

pub enum Command
    ShowOrders
    Invoice(id str)
    ShowStock
    Low(n int)
    ShowCustomers
    History(cust str)
    Sales
    Margin
    Purchases
    Gifts
    ShowPromos
    ## Missing, unknown or malformed: print the usage line and exit 1.
    Usage

pub fn usage() str
    "usage: till orders|invoice ORDER|stock|low N|customers|history ID|sales|margin|purchases|gifts|promos"

## The command the arguments ask for (the program name is not one of them).
pub fn parse(args List[str]) Command
    if args.len() == 1
        return match args[0]
            "orders" => Command.ShowOrders
            "stock" => Command.ShowStock
            "customers" => Command.ShowCustomers
            "sales" => Command.Sales
            "margin" => Command.Margin
            "purchases" => Command.Purchases
            "gifts" => Command.Gifts
            "promos" => Command.ShowPromos
            _ => Command.Usage
    if args.len() != 2
        return Command.Usage
    arg := args[1]
    if args[0] == "invoice" and fields.is_order(arg)
        return Command.Invoice(id: arg)
    if args[0] == "history" and fields.is_id(arg)
        return Command.History(cust: arg)
    if args[0] == "low"
        n := fields.digits(arg, 5) else return Command.Usage
        return Command.Low(n: n)
    Command.Usage

## The shop's state and the journal entries that change it (spec "Journal").
## Each entry checks its rules in the spec's order and changes nothing when one fails.
use catalog
use customers
use gifts
use journal
use orders
use pricing
use promos
use purchasing

pub error enum Problem
    CategoryChanged(sku str) "category changed {sku}"
    UnknownItem(sku str) "unknown item {sku}"
    BelowReserved(sku str) "below reserved {sku}"
    DuplicatePromo(code str) "duplicate promo {code}"
    DuplicateOrder(id str) "duplicate order {id}"
    UnknownCustomer(cust str) "unknown customer {cust}"
    Short(sku str) "short {sku}"
    UnknownOrder(id str) "unknown order {id}"
    WrongStatus(id str, status str) "order {id} is {status}"
    UnknownPromo(code str) "unknown promo {code}"
    PromoAlready(id str) "promo already on {id}"
    UsedUp(code str) "promo {code} used up"
    NotApplicable(code str) "promo {code} does not apply"
    NoCredit(cust str) "no credit {cust}"
    DuplicatePurchase(po str) "duplicate purchase {po}"
    UnknownPurchase(po str) "unknown purchase {po}"
    PurchaseStatus(po str, status str) "purchase {po} is {status}"
    DuplicateGift(card str) "duplicate gift {card}"
    UnknownGift(card str) "unknown gift {card}"
    NotInOrder(sku str, id str) "{sku} not in {id}"
    TooMany(sku str) "too many {sku}"
    EmptyGift(card str) "gift {card} is empty"

pub struct Shop
    pub stock catalog.Catalog
    pub people customers.Customers
    pub deals promos.Promos
    pub book orders.Orders
    pub buying purchasing.Purchases
    pub cards gifts.Cards

pub fn Shop.new() Shop
    Shop(
        stock: catalog.Catalog.new(),
        people: customers.Customers.new(),
        deals: promos.Promos.new(),
        book: orders.Orders.new(),
        buying: purchasing.Purchases.new(),
        cards: gifts.Cards.new(),
    )

## Applies one entry; a rejected entry changes nothing.
pub fn Shop.apply(mut self, e journal.Entry) ! Problem
    match e
        Item(sku, cat, cents) => self.item(sku, cat, cents)?
        Tax(cat, pct) => self.stock.set_rate(cat, pct)
        Restock(sku, qty) => self.restock(sku, qty)?
        Adjust(sku, qty) => self.adjust(sku, qty)?
        Customer(cust, tier) => self.people.set_tier(cust, tier)
        Promo(code, cat, pct, uses) => self.promo(code, cat, pct, uses)?
        Purchase(po, buys) => self.purchase(po, buys)?
        Receive(po) => self.receive(po)?
        Gift(card, cents) => self.gift(card, cents)?
        Order(id, cust, wants) => self.order(id, cust, wants)?
        Apply(id, code) => self.apply_promo(id, code)?
        Pay(id, cents) => self.pay(id, cents)?
        PayCredit(id) => self.pay_credit(id)?
        PayGift(id, card) => self.pay_gift(id, card)?
        Ship(id) => self.ship(id)?
        Cancel(id) => self.cancel(id)?
        Giveback(id, sku, qty) => self.giveback(id, sku, qty)?

fn Shop.item(mut self, sku str, cat str, cents int) ! Problem
    mut it := self.stock.get(sku) else catalog.Item(
        cat: cat,
        price: cents,
        onhand: 0,
        reserved: 0,
        value: 0,
    )
    if it.cat != cat
        return CategoryChanged(sku)
    it.price = cents
    self.stock.put(sku, it)

fn Shop.restock(mut self, sku str, qty int) ! Problem
    mut it := self.stock.get(sku) else return UnknownItem(sku)
    it.onhand += qty
    self.stock.put(sku, it)

fn Shop.adjust(mut self, sku str, qty int) ! Problem
    it := self.stock.get(sku) else return UnknownItem(sku)
    if qty < it.reserved
        return BelowReserved(sku)
    self.stock.stocktake(sku, qty)

fn Shop.promo(mut self, code str, cat str, pct int, uses int) ! Problem
    if self.deals.has(code)
        return DuplicatePromo(code)
    self.deals.add(code, promos.Promo(cat: cat, pct: pct, uses: uses, used: 0))

fn Shop.purchase(mut self, po str, buys List[journal.Buy]) ! Problem
    if self.buying.has(po)
        return DuplicatePurchase(po)
    for b in buys
        if not self.stock.has(b.sku)
            return UnknownItem(b.sku)
    self.buying.put(purchasing.Purchase(po: po, status: purchasing.PoStatus.Ordered, buys: buys))

fn Shop.receive(mut self, po str) ! Problem
    mut p := self.buying.find(po) else return UnknownPurchase(po)
    if p.status != purchasing.PoStatus.Ordered
        return PurchaseStatus(po, p.status.text())
    for b in p.buys
        self.stock.receive(b.sku, b.qty, b.qty * b.cents)
    p.status = purchasing.PoStatus.Received
    self.buying.put(p)

fn Shop.gift(mut self, card str, cents int) ! Problem
    if self.cards.has(card)
        return DuplicateGift(card)
    self.cards.sell(card, cents)

fn Shop.order(mut self, id str, cust str, wants List[journal.Want]) ! Problem
    if self.book.has(id)
        return DuplicateOrder(id)
    if not self.people.has(cust)
        return UnknownCustomer(cust)
    for known in wants
        if not self.stock.has(known.sku)
            return UnknownItem(known.sku)
    for enough in wants
        if self.stock.item(enough.sku).available() < enough.qty
            return Short(enough.sku)
    tier := customers.tier_pct(self.people.get(cust).tier)
    mut lines := List[pricing.Line]()
    for w in wants
        it := self.stock.item(w.sku)
        lines.push(pricing.fresh_line(
            w.sku,
            w.qty,
            it.price,
            it.cat,
            self.stock.rate(it.cat),
            tier,
        ))
        self.stock.reserve(w.sku, w.qty)
    placed := orders.Order(
        id: id,
        cust: cust,
        status: orders.Status.Open,
        lines: lines,
        promo: "",
        paid: 0,
    )
    self.book.put(self.repriced(placed))

## The order with every line priced again under its promo, if it has one.
fn Shop.repriced(self, o orders.Order) orders.Order
    mut cat := ""
    mut pct := 0
    if p := self.deals.get(o.promo)
        cat = p.cat
        pct = p.pct
    mut lines := List[pricing.Line]()
    for l in o.lines
        lines.push(pricing.priced(l, cat, pct))
    mut out := o
    out.lines = lines
    out

## The order `id`, which must have status `want`.
fn Shop.order_in(self, id str, want orders.Status) orders.Order ! Problem
    o := self.book.find(id) else return UnknownOrder(id)
    if o.status != want
        return WrongStatus(id, o.status.text())
    o

fn Shop.apply_promo(mut self, id str, code str) ! Problem
    o := self.order_in(id, orders.Status.Open)?
    p := self.deals.get(code) else return UnknownPromo(code)
    if o.promo != ""
        return PromoAlready(id)
    if p.used >= p.uses
        return UsedUp(code)
    if not o.has_cat(p.cat)
        return NotApplicable(code)
    self.deals.count_use(code, 1)
    mut with_promo := o
    with_promo.promo = code
    mut done := self.repriced(with_promo)
    if done.paid >= done.total()
        self.people.add_credit(done.cust, done.paid - done.total())
        done.paid = done.total()
        done.status = orders.Status.Paid
    self.book.put(done)

fn Shop.pay(mut self, id str, cents int) ! Problem
    o := self.order_in(id, orders.Status.Open)?
    self.settle(o, cents)

fn Shop.pay_credit(mut self, id str) ! Problem
    o := self.order_in(id, orders.Status.Open)?
    credit := self.people.get(o.cust).credit
    if credit == 0
        return NoCredit(o.cust)
    amount := credit.min(o.due())
    self.people.add_credit(o.cust, -amount)
    self.settle(o, amount)

fn Shop.pay_gift(mut self, id str, card str) ! Problem
    o := self.order_in(id, orders.Status.Open)?
    c := self.cards.find(card) else return UnknownGift(card)
    if c.balance == 0
        return EmptyGift(card)
    amount := c.balance.min(o.due())
    self.cards.draw(card, amount)
    self.settle(o, amount)

## Counts `amount` towards what is due on `o`; any amount above it goes to the customer's credit.
fn Shop.settle(mut self, o orders.Order, amount int)
    applied := amount.min(o.due())
    mut settled := o
    settled.paid += applied
    self.people.add_credit(o.cust, amount - applied)
    if settled.paid == settled.total()
        settled.status = orders.Status.Paid
    self.book.put(settled)

fn Shop.ship(mut self, id str) ! Problem
    mut o := self.order_in(id, orders.Status.Paid)?
    mut lines := List[pricing.Line]()
    for l in o.lines
        mut shipped := l
        shipped.cost = self.stock.take(l.sku, l.qty)
        lines.push(shipped)
    o.lines = lines
    o.status = orders.Status.Shipped
    self.book.put(o)

fn Shop.cancel(mut self, id str) ! Problem
    mut o := self.book.find(id) else return UnknownOrder(id)
    if o.status == orders.Status.Shipped or o.status == orders.Status.Cancelled or o.status == orders.Status.Returned
        return WrongStatus(id, o.status.text())
    for l in o.lines
        self.stock.reserve(l.sku, -l.qty)
    self.people.add_credit(o.cust, o.paid)
    o.paid = 0
    if o.promo != ""
        self.deals.count_use(o.promo, -1)
    o.status = orders.Status.Cancelled
    self.book.put(o)

fn Shop.giveback(mut self, id str, sku str, qty int) ! Problem
    mut o := self.order_in(id, orders.Status.Shipped)?
    mut at := -1
    for i in 0..o.lines.len()
        if o.lines[i].sku == sku
            at = i
    if at < 0
        return NotInOrder(sku, id)
    l := o.lines[at]
    if qty > l.qty - l.back
        return TooMany(sku)
    r := l.back
    r2 := r + qty
    net := l.net * r2 / l.qty - l.net * r / l.qty
    tax := l.tax * r2 / l.qty - l.tax * r / l.qty
    cost := l.cost * r2 / l.qty - l.cost * r / l.qty
    o.lines[at].back = r2
    o.lines[at].back_net += net
    o.lines[at].back_tax += tax
    o.lines[at].back_cost += cost
    self.stock.give_back(sku, qty, cost)
    self.people.add_credit(o.cust, net + tax)
    mut all := true
    for x in o.lines
        if x.back < x.qty
            all = false
    if all
        o.status = orders.Status.Returned
    self.book.put(o)

## The catalog: each SKU's category, price and stock, and each category's tax rate.
use money

pub struct Item
    pub cat str
    pub price int
    pub onhand int
    ## Units held by orders that are open or paid.
    pub reserved int
    ## What the units on hand cost the shop, in cents (average cost).
    pub value int

## Units on hand that no order holds.
pub fn Item.available(self) int
    self.onhand - self.reserved

pub struct Catalog
    items Map[str, Item]
    rates Map[str, int]

pub fn Catalog.new() Catalog
    Catalog(items: Map[str, Item](), rates: Map[str, int]())

pub fn Catalog.has(self, sku str) bool
    self.items.contains(sku)

pub fn Catalog.get(self, sku str) Item?
    self.items.get(sku)

## The item of a SKU that `has` reports; traps otherwise.
pub fn Catalog.item(self, sku str) Item
    self.items[sku]

## Every SKU in the catalog, in ascending byte order.
pub fn Catalog.skus(self) List[str]
    self.items.keys().sorted()

pub fn Catalog.put(mut self, sku str, it Item)
    self.items[sku] = it

## The tax rate of a category in percent; 0 until a `tax` entry sets it.
pub fn Catalog.rate(self, cat str) int
    self.rates.get(cat) else 0

pub fn Catalog.set_rate(mut self, cat str, pct int)
    self.rates[cat] = pct

## Changes the reserved quantity of a SKU by `by` units; a negative `by` releases them.
pub fn Catalog.reserve(mut self, sku str, by int)
    mut it := self.items[sku]
    it.reserved += by
    self.items[sku] = it

## Ships `qty` reserved units: they leave both the on-hand and the reserved quantity,
## taking their share of the stock value. Returns that share, the cost of the units.
pub fn Catalog.take(mut self, sku str, qty int) int
    mut it := self.items[sku]
    cost := it.value * qty / it.onhand
    it.value -= cost
    it.onhand -= qty
    it.reserved -= qty
    self.items[sku] = it
    cost

## Returned units: back on hand, with their cost share back in the stock value.
pub fn Catalog.give_back(mut self, sku str, qty int, cost int)
    mut it := self.items[sku]
    it.onhand += qty
    it.value += cost
    self.items[sku] = it

## Adds `qty` units that cost `cents` in all.
pub fn Catalog.receive(mut self, sku str, qty int, cents int)
    mut it := self.items[sku]
    it.onhand += qty
    it.value += cents
    self.items[sku] = it

## A stocktake: sets the units on hand, scaling the stock value with them.
pub fn Catalog.stocktake(mut self, sku str, qty int)
    mut it := self.items[sku]
    if it.onhand > 0
        it.value = it.value * qty / it.onhand
    it.onhand = qty
    self.items[sku] = it

## The tax on a line's net amount at `rate` percent.
pub fn tax(net int, rate int) int
    money.percent(net, rate)

# depgraph

Write `depgraph`, a command-line program. It reads a dependency list from stdin and answers one question about it.

Input, one item per line:
- `A -> B` means A needs B.
- `A` alone declares a node with no dependencies yet.
- An empty line or a line starting with `#` is ignored.
- A name is one or more of `a-z A-Z 0-9 _ . -`. The separator is exactly one space, `->`, one space. Any other line (extra or missing spaces, a third name, an illegal character, a carriage return) is bad: skip it and print `error: line K: bad line` to stderr (K is 1-based). Repeated edges count once. `A -> A` is a self-dependency. There are at most 500 distinct names.

Commands (first argument), output on stdout, one name per line:
- `order`: every node, dependencies first. Among nodes ready at the same time, the smallest name in byte order comes first.
- `cycles`: every node that lies on a cycle (reaches itself through one or more edges), in ascending byte order.
- `deps NAME`: everything NAME needs, directly or not, ascending. NAME itself appears only if it lies on a cycle.
- `rdeps NAME`: everything that needs NAME, directly or not, ascending, under the same rule.

Exit codes, first that applies wins: 1 for a missing, unknown or malformed command, including a wrong number of arguments and a NAME argument that is not a valid name by the rule above (print `usage: depgraph order|cycles|deps NAME|rdeps NAME` to stderr, do not read stdin); 4 if `deps`/`rdeps` names a node that is not in the input (print `error: unknown ` and the name to stderr, e.g. `error: unknown lib`, nothing on stdout); 3 if `order` finds a cycle (print `error: cycle` to stderr, nothing on stdout); 2 if any line was bad (stdout is still printed); else 0.

Layout: sources live in `src/` (`src/main.ail`, `src/main.c` or `src/main.rs`); `./build` builds `./depgraph`; `./test` runs the visible cases.

Read every file in `DOCS/` in full before you write any code. A file longer than 24 KB is split into numbered parts (`NAME.part1.md`, `NAME.part2.md`, ...): read each part, in order, with its own call (a tool result over 30 KB is cut short), and do not stop at the first lines of a part.

fn usage() never
    io.eprint("usage: depgraph order|cycles|deps NAME|rdeps NAME")
    io.exit(1)

fn valid_name(s str) bool
    if s.len() == 0
        return false
    for c in s.chars()
        ok := (c >= 'a' and c <= 'z') or (c >= 'A' and c <= 'Z') or (c >= '0' and c <= '9') or c == '_' or c == '.' or c == '-'
        if not ok
            return false
    true

fn reach(start str, g Map[str, List[str]]) Set[str]
    mut seen := Set[str]()
    mut stack := List[str]()
    for n in g[start]
        stack.push(n)
    while stack.len() > 0
        cur := stack.pop() else ""
        if seen.add(cur)
            for n in g[cur]
                stack.push(n)
    seen

fn main()
    args := env.args()
    if args.len() == 0
        usage()
    cmd := args[0]
    mut target := ""
    if cmd == "order" or cmd == "cycles"
        if args.len() != 1
            usage()
    elif cmd == "deps" or cmd == "rdeps"
        if args.len() != 2
            usage()
        target = args[1]
        if not valid_name(target)
            usage()
    else
        usage()
    text := io.read_all()
    mut deps := Map[str, List[str]]()
    mut rdeps := Map[str, List[str]]()
    mut edges := Set[str]()
    mut bad := false
    mut k := 0
    for line in text.split("\n")
        k += 1
        if line == "" or line.starts_with("#")
            continue
        parts := line.split(" -> ")
        mut ok := true
        if parts.len() == 1
            if not valid_name(parts[0])
                ok = false
        elif parts.len() == 2
            if not (valid_name(parts[0]) and valid_name(parts[1]))
                ok = false
        else
            ok = false
        if not ok
            io.eprint("error: line {k}: bad line")
            bad = true
            continue
        for p in parts
            if not deps.contains(p)
                deps[p] = List[str]()
                rdeps[p] = List[str]()
        if parts.len() == 2
            if edges.add("{parts[0]} {parts[1]}")
                deps[parts[0]].push(parts[1])
                rdeps[parts[1]].push(parts[0])
    names := deps.keys().sorted()
    if cmd == "order"
        mut pending := Map[str, int]()
        for n in names
            pending[n] = deps[n].len()
        mut done := Set[str]()
        mut out := List[str]()
        while out.len() < names.len()
            mut pick := ""
            for n in names
                if pending[n] == 0 and not done.contains(n)
                    pick = n
                    break
            if pick == ""
                io.eprint("error: cycle")
                io.exit(3)
            done.add(pick)
            out.push(pick)
            for r in rdeps[pick]
                pending[r] -= 1
        for n in out
            print(n)
    elif cmd == "cycles"
        for n in names
            if reach(n, deps).contains(n)
                print(n)
    else
        if not deps.contains(target)
            io.eprint("error: unknown {target}")
            io.exit(4)
        g := if cmd == "deps" then deps else rdeps
        for n in reach(target, g).sorted()
            print(n)
    if bad
        io.exit(2)

# invjson

Write `invjson`, a command-line program. It reads an inventory from stdin and prints it as JSON, or as a tag summary.

Input, one item per line: `SKU QTY` followed by zero or more `TAG`s, separated by exactly one space.
- SKU is one or more of `A-Z 0-9 -`. QTY is one to seven decimal digits (no sign). A TAG is one or more of `a-z`.
- An empty line or a line starting with `#` is ignored.
- Any other line (extra or missing spaces, a bad character, a carriage return) is bad: skip it and print
  `error: line K: bad line` to stderr (K is 1-based).
- A SKU seen again adds its QTY to the earlier total and adds its tags that are new to that SKU, after the earlier ones.
  A tag repeated on one line counts once.

Commands (first argument):
- `json` or `json TITLE`: the inventory as JSON, exactly in this layout (two-space indent, one item per line,
  items in ascending byte order of SKU, tags in the order first seen):

  ```
  {
    "title": "Spring count",
    "items": [
      {"sku": "A-1", "qty": 3, "tags": ["red", "big"]},
      {"sku": "B7", "qty": 0, "tags": []}
    ],
    "total": 3
  }
  ```

  The `"title"` line appears only when TITLE is given. With no items the items line is `  "items": [],`.
  `"total"` is the sum of all quantities. In TITLE, `"` is written `\"`, `\` is written `\\`, a tab `\t`, a newline
  `\n`, any other character below U+0020 as `\u00XX` with lowercase hex digits; every other character as it is.
- `tags`: one line per tag, `TAG<TAB>QTY`, where QTY is the sum over the items that carry the tag; larger QTY first,
  equal QTY in ascending byte order of TAG.

Exit codes: 1 for a missing or unknown command or the wrong number of arguments (`json` takes at most one more,
`tags` none): print `usage: invjson json [TITLE]|tags` to stderr and do not read stdin. Otherwise 2 if any line was
bad (stdout is still printed), else 0.

Layout: sources live in `src/` (`src/main.ail`, `src/main.c` or `src/main.rs`); `./build` builds `./invjson`;
`./test` runs the visible cases.

fn usage() never
    io.eprint("usage: invjson json [TITLE]|tags")
    io.exit(1)

fn all_in(s str, lo char, hi char) bool
    if s.len() == 0
        return false
    for c in s.chars()
        if c < lo or c > hi
            return false
    true

fn sku_ok(s str) bool
    if s.len() == 0
        return false
    for c in s.chars()
        ok := (c >= 'A' and c <= 'Z') or (c >= '0' and c <= '9') or c == '-'
        if not ok
            return false
    true

fn esc(s str) str
    mut out := []
    for c in s.chars()
        n := c.code()
        if c == '"'
            out.push("\\\"")
        elif c == '\\'
            out.push("\\\\")
        elif n == 9
            out.push("\\t")
        elif n == 10
            out.push("\\n")
        elif n < 32
            out.push("\\u00{n:02x}")
        else
            out.push("{c}")
    out.join("")

fn main()
    args := env.args()
    if args.len() == 0
        usage()
    cmd := args[0]
    if cmd == "json"
        if args.len() > 2
            usage()
    elif cmd == "tags"
        if args.len() != 1
            usage()
    else
        usage()
    text := io.read_all()
    mut qty := Map[str, int]()
    mut tags := Map[str, List[str]]()
    mut bad := false
    for i, line in text.split("\n").enumerate()
        if line.len() == 0 or line.starts_with("#")
            continue
        parts := line.split(" ")
        mut ok := parts.len() >= 2 and sku_ok(parts[0]) and all_in(parts[1], '0', '9') and parts[1].len() <= 7
        if ok
            for j in 2..parts.len()
                if not all_in(parts[j], 'a', 'z')
                    ok = false
        if not ok
            io.eprint("error: line {i + 1}: bad line")
            bad = true
            continue
        sku := parts[0]
        q := parts[1].to_int() else 0
        if not qty.contains(sku)
            qty[sku] = 0
            tags[sku] = List[str]()
        qty[sku] += q
        mut tl := tags[sku]
        for j in 2..parts.len()
            if not tl.contains(parts[j])
                tl.push(parts[j])
        tags[sku] = tl
    if cmd == "json"
        mut lines := ["\{"]
        if args.len() == 2
            lines.push("  \"title\": \"{esc(args[1])}\",")
        skus := qty.keys().sorted()
        mut total := 0
        if skus.len() == 0
            lines.push("  \"items\": [],")
        else
            lines.push("  \"items\": [")
            for i, s in skus.enumerate()
                total += qty[s]
                ts := ["\"{t}\"" for t in tags[s]].join(", ")
                comma := if i + 1 < skus.len() then "," else ""
                lines.push("    \{\"sku\": \"{s}\", \"qty\": {qty[s]}, \"tags\": [{ts}]}{comma}")
            lines.push("  ],")
        lines.push("  \"total\": {total}")
        lines.push("}")
        print(lines.join("\n"))
    else
        mut sums := Map[str, int]()
        for s, tl in tags
            for t in tl
                sums[t] += qty[s]
        ks := sums.keys().sorted()
        ordered := ks.sorted(by: |t| -sums[t])
        for t in ordered
            print("{t}\t{sums[t]}")
    if bad
        io.exit(2)

struct Item

    tags List[str]

fn usage() never
    io.eprint("usage: invjson json [TITLE]|tags")
    io.exit(1)

fn all_in(s str, lo char, hi char, dash bool) bool
    if s.is_empty()
        return false
    for c in s.chars()
        ok := (c >= lo and c <= hi) or (dash and c == '-')
        if not ok
            return false
    true

fn valid_sku(s str) bool
    if s.is_empty()
        return false
    for c in s.chars()
        ok := (c >= 'A' and c <= 'Z') or (c >= '0' and c <= '9') or c == '-'
        if not ok
            return false
    true

fn esc(s str) str
    mut out := []
    for c in s.chars()
        code := c.code()
        if c == '"'
            out.push("\\\"")
        elif c == '\\'
            out.push("\\\\")
        elif c == '\t'
            out.push("\\t")
        elif c == '\n'
            out.push("\\n")
        elif code < 32
            out.push("\\u00{code.to_hex().pad_left(2, '0')}")
        else
            out.push("{c}")
    out.join("")

fn main()
    args := env.args()
    if args.len() == 0
        usage()
    cmd := args[0]
    if cmd == "json"
        if args.len() > 2
            usage()
    elif cmd == "tags"
        if args.len() != 1
            usage()
    else
        usage()
    text := io.read_all()
    mut items := Map[str, Item]()
    mut bad := false
    mut k := 0
    for line in text.split("\n")
        k += 1
        if line.is_empty() or line.starts_with("#")
            continue
        parts := line.split(" ")
        mut ok := parts.len() >= 2 and valid_sku(parts[0])
        if ok
            q := parts[1]
            ok = q.len() <= 7 and all_in(q, '0', '9', false)
        if ok
            for t in parts.skip(2)
                if not all_in(t, 'a', 'z', false)
                    ok = false
        if not ok
            bad = true
            io.eprint("error: line {k}: bad line")
            continue
        qty := parts[1].to_int() else 0
        if not items.contains(parts[0])
            items[parts[0]] = Item(qty: 0, tags: [])
        items[parts[0]].qty += qty
        for t in parts.skip(2)
            if not items[parts[0]].tags.contains(t)
                items[parts[0]].tags.push(t)

        out.push("}")
        print(out.join("\n"))
    else
        mut sums := Map[str, int]()

# ledger

Write `ledger`, a command-line program. It reads a CSV of transactions from stdin and prints a report.

Input: the first line is exactly `date,account,amount_cents,memo`. Every other line has exactly four comma-separated fields (no quoting; memo may be empty and has no commas). `date` is `YYYY-MM-DD` (digits only, month 01-12, day 01-31). `account` is non-empty. `amount_cents` is an integer with an optional leading `-`. A line that breaks any rule is skipped and reported on stderr as `error: line K: REASON` (K is the 1-based line number, header is line 1). If any line was skipped the exit code is 2, else 0, but stdout is still printed. A bad header prints `error: line 1: bad header`, nothing on stdout, exit 2. Empty input is a bad header. A trailing blank line at the end of input is ignored.

Commands (first argument):
- `balance`: one line per account, `ACCOUNT<TAB>AMOUNT`, accounts in ascending byte order.
- `top N`: the N transactions with the largest absolute amount, one per line `DATE<TAB>ACCOUNT<TAB>AMOUNT<TAB>MEMO`, largest first, ties in input order. Fewer than N lines if fewer exist. N is a non-negative integer.
- `monthly`: one line per `YYYY-MM`, `MONTH<TAB>AMOUNT`, months ascending.

AMOUNT prints cents as dollars with exactly two decimals and a leading `-` for negatives: `1234.05`, `-0.50`, `0.00`. Amounts fit in 64-bit signed integers; sums may be large.

A missing, unknown or malformed command (including a bad N) prints `usage: ledger balance|top N|monthly` on stderr and exits 1 without reading stdin.

struct Tx
    date str
    account str
    amount int
    memo str

fn usage() never
    io.eprint("usage: ledger balance|top N|monthly")
    io.exit(1)

fn money(n int) str
    neg := n < 0
    mut q := n / 100
    mut r := n % 100
    if neg
        q = -q
        r = -r
    sign := if neg then "-" else ""
    "{sign}{q}.{r:02}"

fn all_digits(s str) bool
    for c in s.chars()
        if c < '0' or c > '9'
            return false
    true

fn date_ok(d str) bool
    if d.len() != 10
        return false
    y := d.slice(0, 4)
    mo := d.slice(5, 7)
    da := d.slice(8, 10)
    if d.slice(4, 5) != "-" or d.slice(7, 8) != "-"
        return false
    if not all_digits(y) or not all_digits(mo) or not all_digits(da)
        return false
    m := mo.to_int() else 0
    dd := da.to_int() else 0
    m >= 1 and m <= 12 and dd >= 1 and dd <= 31

fn parse_line(line str) Tx ! str
    f := line.split(",")
    if f.len() != 4
        return "wrong field count"
    if not date_ok(f[0])
        return "bad date"
    if f[1] == ""
        return "empty account"
    a := f[2].to_int() else return "bad amount"
    Tx(date: f[0], account: f[1], amount: a, memo: f[3])

fn absval(n int) int
    if n < 0
        return -n
    n

fn main()
    args := env.args()
    if args.len() == 0
        usage()
    cmd := args[0]
    mut topn := 0
    if cmd == "top"
        if args.len() != 2
            usage()
        topn = args[1].to_int() else usage()
        if topn < 0
            usage()
    elif (cmd != "balance" and cmd != "monthly") or args.len() != 1
        usage()
    lines := io.read_all().lines()
    if lines.len() == 0 or lines[0] != "date,account,amount_cents,memo"
        io.eprint("error: line 1: bad header")
        io.exit(2)
    mut n := lines.len()
    while n > 1 and lines[n - 1] == ""
        n -= 1
    mut txs := List[Tx]()
    mut bad := false
    for i in 1..n
        t := parse_line(lines[i]) else e
            io.eprint("error: line {i + 1}: {e}")
            bad = true
            continue
        txs.push(t)
    if cmd == "balance"
        mut m := Map[str, int]()
        for t in txs
            m[t.account] += t.amount
        for k in m.keys().sorted()
            print("{k}\t{money(m[k])}")
    elif cmd == "monthly"
        mut m := Map[str, int]()
        for t in txs
            m[t.date.slice(0, 7)] += t.amount
        for k in m.keys().sorted()
            print("{k}\t{money(m[k])}")
    else
        s := txs.sorted(by: |t| -absval(t.amount))
        mut c := 0
        for t in s
            if c >= topn
                break
            print("{t.date}\t{t.account}\t{money(t.amount)}\t{t.memo}")
            c += 1
    if bad
        io.exit(2)

        if not ok
            return false
    true

    q := cost / b
    r := cost % b

    a := if neg then -c else c

                p := f[3].to_int() else 0

use parse

## On-hand quantities and average cost per SKU.

pub struct Entry
    pub qty int
    pub cost int

pub error enum Problem
    Unknown(sku str) "unknown {sku}"
    Short(sku str) "short {sku}"

pub struct Store
    items Map[str, Entry]

pub fn Store.new() Store
    Store(items: Map[str, Entry]())

## Every SKU ever received, in ascending byte order.
pub fn Store.skus(self) List[str]
    self.items.keys().sorted()

## The entry of a SKU from `skus()`.
pub fn Store.entry(self, sku str) Entry
    self.items[sku]

## Applies one event; a rejected event changes nothing.
pub fn Store.apply(mut self, e parse.Event) ! Problem
    if e.kind == parse.Kind.Receive
        mut fresh := self.items.get(e.sku) else Entry(qty: 0, cost: 0)
        fresh.qty += e.qty
        fresh.cost += e.qty * e.price
        self.items[e.sku] = fresh
        return
    mut it := self.items.get(e.sku) else return Problem.Unknown(e.sku)
    if e.kind == parse.Kind.Ship
        if e.qty > it.qty
            return Problem.Short(e.sku)
        it.cost -= it.cost * e.qty / it.qty
        it.qty -= e.qty
    else
        if it.qty > 0
            it.cost = it.cost * e.qty / it.qty
        it.qty = e.qty
    self.items[e.sku] = it

## One line of the stock log.

pub enum Kind
    Receive
    Ship
    Count

pub struct Event
    pub kind Kind
    pub sku str
    pub qty int
    pub price int

pub error enum ParseError
    BadLine "bad line"

## 1 to 5 ASCII digits, as a number.
pub fn number(s str) int?
    if s.is_empty() or s.len() > 5
        return none
    for ch in s.chars()
        if ch.code() < 48 or ch.code() > 57
            return none
    s.to_int()

fn valid_sku(s str) bool
    if s.is_empty()
        return false
    for ch in s.chars()
        upper := ch.code() >= 65 and ch.code() <= 90
        digit := ch.code() >= 48 and ch.code() <= 57
        if not (upper or digit or ch == '-')
            return false
    true

## The event on a line, or `BadLine` if the line is not a valid
pub fn parse(line str) Event ! ParseError
    f := line.split(" ")
    mut kind := Kind.Receive
    if f[0] == "receive" and f.len() == 4
        kind = Kind.Receive
    elif f[0] == "ship" and f.len() == 3
        kind = Kind.Ship
    elif f[0] == "count" and f.len() == 3
        kind = Kind.Count
    else
        return BadLine
    if not valid_sku(f[1])
        return BadLine
    qty := number(f[2]) else return BadLine
    mut price := 0
    if kind == Kind.Receive
        p := number(f[3]) else return BadLine
        price = p
    if qty == 0 and kind != Kind.Count
        return BadLine
    Event(kind: kind, sku: f[1], qty: qty, price: price)

use parse

## On-hand quantities and average cost per SKU.

pub struct Entry
    pub qty int
    pub cost int

pub error enum Problem
    Unknown(sku str) "unknown {sku}"
    Short(sku str) "short {sku}"

pub struct Store
    items Map[str, Entry]

pub fn Store.new() Store
    Store(items: Map[str, Entry]())

## Every SKU ever received, in ascending byte order.
pub fn Store.skus(self) List[str]
    self.items.keys().sorted()

## The entry of a SKU from `skus()`.
pub fn Store.entry(self, sku str) Entry
    self.items[sku]

## Applies one event; a rejected event changes nothing.
pub fn Store.apply(mut self, e parse.Event) ! Problem
    if e.kind == parse.Kind.Receive
        mut fresh := self.items.get(e.sku) else Entry(qty: 0, cost: 0)
        fresh.qty += e.qty
        fresh.cost += e.qty * e.price
        self.items[e.sku] = fresh
        return
    mut it := self.items.get(e.sku) else return Problem.Unknown(e.sku)
    if e.kind == parse.Kind.Ship
        if e.qty > it.qty
            return Problem.Short(e.sku)
        it.cost -= it.cost * e.qty / it.qty
        it.qty -= e.qty
    else
        if it.qty > 0
            it.cost = it.cost * e.qty / it.qty
        it.qty = e.qty
    self.items[e.sku] = it

## One line of the stock log.

pub enum Kind
    Receive
    Ship
    Count

pub struct Event
    pub kind Kind
    pub sku str
    pub qty int
    pub price int

pub error enum ParseError
    BadLine "bad line"

## 1 to 5 ASCII digits, as a number.
pub fn number(s str) int?
    if s.is_empty() or s.len() > 5
        return none
    for ch in s.chars()
        if ch.code() < 48 or ch.code() > 57
            return none
    s.to_int()

fn valid_sku(s str) bool
    if s.is_empty()
        return false
    for ch in s.chars()
        upper := ch.code() >= 65 and ch.code() <= 90
        digit := ch.code() >= 48 and ch.code() <= 57
        if not (upper or digit or ch == '-')
            return false
    true

## The event on a line, or `BadLine` if the line is not a valid
pub fn parse(line str) Event ! ParseError
    f := line.split(" ")
    mut kind := Kind.Receive
    if f[0] == "receive" and f.len() == 4
        kind = Kind.Receive
    elif f[0] == "ship" and f.len() == 3
        kind = Kind.Ship
    elif f[0] == "count" and f.len() == 3
        kind = Kind.Count
    else
        return BadLine
    if not valid_sku(f[1])
        return BadLine
    qty := number(f[2]) else return BadLine
    mut price := 0
    if kind == Kind.Receive
        p := number(f[3]) else return BadLine
        price = p
    if qty == 0 and kind != Kind.Count
        return BadLine
    Event(kind: kind, sku: f[1], qty: qty, price: price)

# Issue: tier discounts are a cent short

`till` (spec in `DOCS/spec.md`, sources in `src/`) gives silver and gold customers a tier discount that is sometimes one cent smaller than the spec's rule. With

```
item LAMP home 1995
customer ann gold
restock LAMP 5
order o1 ann LAMP:1
```

use cli
use journal
use reports
use shop

## Prints `error: no WHAT` and ends the program with exit code 3.
fn missing(what str)
    io.eprint("error: no {what}")
    io.exit(3)

fn main()
    cmd := cli.parse(env.args())
    if cmd == cli.Command.Usage
        io.eprint(cli.usage())
        io.exit(1)
    mut lines := io.read_all().split("\n")
    if (lines.last() else "x") == ""
        lines.pop()
    mut s := shop.Shop.new()
    mut bad := 0
    for k in 0..lines.len()
        line := lines[k]
        if line.is_empty() or line.starts_with("#")
            continue
        e := journal.parse(line) else err
            io.eprint("error: line {k + 1}: {err}")
            bad += 1
            continue
        s.apply(e) else err
            io.eprint("error: line {k + 1}: {err}")
            bad += 1
    mut out := List[str]()
    match cmd
        ShowOrders => out = reports.order_lines(s)
        Invoice(id) =>
            out = reports.invoice(s, id) else List[str]()
            if not s.book.has(id)
                missing("order {id}")
        ShowStock => out = reports.stock_lines(s)
        Low(n) => out = reports.low(s, n)
        ShowCustomers => out = reports.customer_lines(s)
        History(cust) =>
            out = reports.history(s, cust) else List[str]()
            if not s.people.has(cust)
                missing("customer {cust}")
        Sales => out = reports.sales(s)
        Margin => out = reports.margin(s)
        Purchases => out = reports.purchase_lines(s)
        Gifts => out = reports.gift_lines(s)
        ShowPromos => out = reports.promo_lines(s)
        Usage => return
    for l in out
        print(l)
    if bad > 0
        io.exit(2)

## The reports, as lines without their newline (spec "Reports").
use money
use orders
use shop

## Each placed order: `ORDER ID STATUS TOTAL PAID`.
pub fn order_lines(s shop.Shop) List[str]
    mut out := List[str]()
    for o in s.book.all()
        out.push("{o.id}\t{o.cust}\t{o.status.text()}\t{money.show(o.total())}\t{money.show(o.paid)}")
    out

## The invoice of order `id`, or `none` if it was never placed.
pub fn invoice(s shop.Shop, id str) List[str]?
    o := s.book.find(id) else return none
    mut out := ["order {o.id} {o.cust} {o.status.text()}"]
    mut gross := 0
    mut discount := 0
    mut tax := 0
    for l in o.lines
        amounts := [l.price, l.gross, l.discount, l.tax, l.total].map(|c| money.show(c)).join("\t")
        out.push("{l.sku}\t{l.qty}\t{amounts}")
        gross += l.gross
        discount += l.discount
        tax += l.tax
    if o.promo != ""
        out.push("promo\t{o.promo}")
    due := if o.status == orders.Status.Open then o.due() else 0
    out.push("subtotal\t{money.show(gross)}")
    out.push("discount\t{money.show(discount)}")
    out.push("tax\t{money.show(tax)}")
    out.push("total\t{money.show(o.total())}")
    out.push("paid\t{money.show(o.paid)}")
    out.push("due\t{money.show(due)}")
    out

## Each catalog SKU: `SKU CAT PRICE ONHAND RESERVED AVAILABLE VALUE`.
pub fn stock_lines(s shop.Shop) List[str]
    mut out := List[str]()
    for sku in s.stock.skus()
        it := s.stock.item(sku)
        out.push("{sku}\t{it.cat}\t{money.show(it.price)}\t{it.onhand}\t{it.reserved}\t{it.available()}\t{money.show(it.value)}")
    out

## Each catalog SKU with fewer than `n` units available: `SKU AVAILABLE`.
pub fn low(s shop.Shop, n int) List[str]
    mut out := List[str]()
    for sku in s.stock.skus()
        left := s.stock.item(sku).available()
        if left < n
            out.push("{sku}\t{left}")
    out

## Each customer: `ID TIER ORDERS SPENT CREDIT`.
pub fn customer_lines(s shop.Shop) List[str]
    mut out := List[str]()
    for cust in s.people.ids()
        c := s.people.get(cust)
        mut placed := 0
        mut spent := 0
        for o in s.book.of(cust)
            if o.status != orders.Status.Cancelled
                placed += 1
            if o.status == orders.Status.Shipped
                spent += o.total()
        out.push("{cust}\t{c.tier}\t{placed}\t{money.show(spent)}\t{money.show(c.credit)}")
    out

## A customer's orders, `ORDER STATUS TOTAL`, then `credit`; `none` for a customer never registered.
pub fn history(s shop.Shop, cust str) List[str]?
    if not s.people.has(cust)
        return none
    mut out := List[str]()
    for o in s.book.of(cust)
        out.push("{o.id}\t{o.status.text()}\t{money.show(o.total())}")
    out.push("credit\t{money.show(s.people.get(cust).credit)}")
    out

struct Tally
    units int
    net int
    tax int

## Units, net and tax of the shipped lines, by category, then `total`.
pub fn sales(s shop.Shop) List[str]
    mut cats := Map[str, Tally]()
    mut overall := Tally(units: 0, net: 0, tax: 0)
    for o in s.book.all()
        if o.status != orders.Status.Shipped
            continue
        for l in o.lines
            mut t := cats.get(l.cat) else Tally(units: 0, net: 0, tax: 0)
            t.units += l.qty
            t.net += l.net
            t.tax += l.tax
            cats[l.cat] = t
            overall.units += l.qty
            overall.net += l.net
            overall.tax += l.tax
    mut out := List[str]()
    for cat in cats.keys().sorted()
        row := cats[cat]
        out.push("{cat}\t{row.units}\t{money.show(row.net)}\t{money.show(row.tax)}")
    out.push("total\t{overall.units}\t{money.show(overall.net)}\t{money.show(overall.tax)}")
    out

struct Margin
    net int
    cost int

fn margin_line(name str, m Margin) str
    "{name}\t{money.show(m.net)}\t{money.show(m.cost)}\t{money.show(m.net - m.cost)}"

## Net, cost and margin of the shipped lines, by category, then `total`.
pub fn margin(s shop.Shop) List[str]
    mut cats := Map[str, Margin]()
    mut overall := Margin(net: 0, cost: 0)
    for o in s.book.all()
        if o.status != orders.Status.Shipped
            continue
        for l in o.lines
            mut m := cats.get(l.cat) else Margin(net: 0, cost: 0)
            m.net += l.net
            m.cost += l.cost
            cats[l.cat] = m
            overall.net += l.net
            overall.cost += l.cost
    mut out := List[str]()
    for cat in cats.keys().sorted()
        out.push(margin_line(cat, cats[cat]))
    out.push(margin_line("total", overall))
    out

## Each purchase order: `PO STATUS UNITS COST`.
pub fn purchase_lines(s shop.Shop) List[str]
    mut out := List[str]()
    for p in s.buying.all()
        out.push("{p.po}\t{p.status.text()}\t{p.units()}\t{money.show(p.cost())}")
    out

## Each gift card: `CARD SOLD BALANCE`.
pub fn gift_lines(s shop.Shop) List[str]
    mut out := List[str]()
    for card in s.cards.all_cards()
        c := s.cards.find(card) else continue
        out.push("{card}\t{money.show(c.sold)}\t{money.show(c.balance)}")
    out

## Each promo code: `CODE CAT PCT% USED/USES`.
pub fn promo_lines(s shop.Shop) List[str]
    mut out := List[str]()
    for code in s.deals.all_codes()
        p := s.deals.get(code) else continue
        out.push("{code}\t{p.cat}\t{p.pct}%\t{p.used}/{p.uses}")
    out

## Pricing of order lines (spec "Prices"). The amounts are computed from the fields an
## order fixes when it is placed (price, tax rate, tier discount) and the order's promo.
use catalog
use customers
use promos

pub struct Line
    pub sku str
    pub qty int
    pub price int
    pub cat str
    ## Tax rate of the category, in percent, when the order was placed.
    pub rate int
    ## Tier discount of the customer, in percent, when the order was placed.
    pub tier int
    pub gross int
    ## Tier discount plus promo discount.
    pub discount int
    pub net int
    pub tax int
    pub total int
    ## What the shipped units cost the shop; 0 until the order ships.
    pub cost int

## A line whose amounts `priced` has still to fill in.
pub fn fresh_line(sku str, qty int, price int, cat str, rate int, tier int) Line
    Line(
        sku: sku,
        qty: qty,
        price: price,
        cat: cat,
        rate: rate,
        tier: tier,
        gross: 0,
        discount: 0,
        net: 0,
        tax: 0,
        total: 0,
        cost: 0,
    )

## The line with its amounts computed. The promo (`promo_pct` off lines of `promo_cat`)
## applies only to lines of that category; pass `""` when the order has no promo.
pub fn priced(l Line, promo_cat str, promo_pct int) Line
    mut p := l
    p.gross = l.price * l.qty
    tier_off := customers.discount(p.gross, l.tier)
    mut promo_off := 0
    if promo_cat == l.cat
        promo_off = promos.discount(p.gross - tier_off, promo_pct)
    p.discount = tier_off + promo_off
    p.net = p.gross - p.discount
    p.tax = catalog.tax(p.net, l.rate)
    p.total = p.net + p.tax
    p

## The shapes of journal and command-line fields (spec "Fields").

fn upper(ch char) bool
    match ch
        'A'..='Z' => true
        _ => false

fn lower(ch char) bool
    match ch
        'a'..='z' => true
        _ => false

fn digit(ch char) bool
    match ch
        '0'..='9' => true
        _ => false

fn sku_char(ch char) bool
    upper(ch) or digit(ch) or ch == '-'

fn code_char(ch char) bool
    upper(ch) or digit(ch)

fn id_char(ch char) bool
    lower(ch) or digit(ch)

## `lo` to `hi` characters, the first accepted by `first` and every one by `rest`.
fn shaped(s str, lo int, hi int, first fn(char) bool, rest fn(char) bool) bool
    if s.len() < lo or s.len() > hi
        return false
    cs := s.chars()
    if not first(cs[0])
        return false
    for ch in cs
        if not rest(ch)
            return false
    true

## 1 to `width` ASCII digits, as a number (leading zeros allowed); `none` for anything else.
pub fn digits(s str, width int) int?
    if s.is_empty() or s.len() > width
        return none
    for ch in s.chars()
        if not digit(ch)
            return none
    s.to_int()

## SKU: 1 to 12 of `A-Z 0-9 -`, starting with a letter.
pub fn is_sku(s str) bool
    shaped(s, 1, 12, upper, sku_char)

## CAT: 1 to 12 letters `a-z`.
pub fn is_cat(s str) bool
    shaped(s, 1, 12, lower, lower)

## ID: 1 to 12 of `a-z 0-9`, starting with a letter.
pub fn is_id(s str) bool
    shaped(s, 1, 12, lower, id_char)

## CODE: 3 to 10 of `A-Z 0-9`, starting with a letter.
pub fn is_code(s str) bool
    shaped(s, 3, 10, upper, code_char)

## ORDER: `o` and 1 to 6 digits.
pub fn is_order(s str) bool
    rest := s.strip_prefix("o") else return false
    (digits(rest, 6) else -1) >= 0

## PO: `p` and 1 to 6 digits.
pub fn is_po(s str) bool
    rest := s.strip_prefix("p") else return false
    (digits(rest, 6) else -1) >= 0

## CARD: `g` and 1 to 6 digits.
pub fn is_card(s str) bool
    rest := s.strip_prefix("g") else return false
    (digits(rest, 6) else -1) >= 0

## TIER: `basic`, `silver` or `gold`.
pub fn is_tier(s str) bool
    s == "basic" or s == "silver" or s == "gold"

## The command line: which report to print (spec "Reports", "Exit codes and stderr").
use fields

pub enum Command
    ShowOrders
    Invoice(id str)
    ShowStock
    Low(n int)
    ShowCustomers
    History(cust str)
    Sales
    Margin
    Purchases
    Gifts
    ShowPromos
    ## Missing, unknown or malformed: print the usage line and exit 1.
    Usage

pub fn usage() str
    "usage: till orders|invoice ORDER|stock|low N|customers|history ID|sales|margin|purchases|gifts|promos"

## The command the arguments ask for (the program name is not one of them).
pub fn parse(args List[str]) Command
    if args.len() == 1
        return match args[0]
            "orders" => Command.ShowOrders
            "stock" => Command.ShowStock
            "customers" => Command.ShowCustomers
            "sales" => Command.Sales
            "margin" => Command.Margin
            "purchases" => Command.Purchases
            "gifts" => Command.Gifts
            "promos" => Command.ShowPromos
            _ => Command.Usage
    if args.len() != 2
        return Command.Usage
    arg := args[1]
    if args[0] == "invoice" and fields.is_order(arg)
        return Command.Invoice(id: arg)
    if args[0] == "history" and fields.is_id(arg)
        return Command.History(cust: arg)
    if args[0] == "low"
        n := fields.digits(arg, 5) else return Command.Usage
        return Command.Low(n: n)

## The shop's state and the journal entries that change it (spec "Journal").
## Each entry checks its rules in the spec's order and changes nothing when one fails.
use catalog
use customers
use gifts
use journal
use orders
use pricing
use promos
use purchasing

pub error enum Problem
    CategoryChanged(sku str) "category changed {sku}"
    UnknownItem(sku str) "unknown item {sku}"
    BelowReserved(sku str) "below reserved {sku}"
    DuplicatePromo(code str) "duplicate promo {code}"
    DuplicateOrder(id str) "duplicate order {id}"
    UnknownCustomer(cust str) "unknown customer {cust}"
    Short(sku str) "short {sku}"
    UnknownOrder(id str) "unknown order {id}"
    WrongStatus(id str, status str) "order {id} is {status}"
    UnknownPromo(code str) "unknown promo {code}"
    PromoAlready(id str) "promo already on {id}"
    UsedUp(code str) "promo {code} used up"
    NotApplicable(code str) "promo {code} does not apply"
    NoCredit(cust str) "no credit {cust}"
    DuplicatePurchase(po str) "duplicate purchase {po}"
    UnknownPurchase(po str) "unknown purchase {po}"
    PurchaseStatus(po str, status str) "purchase {po} is {status}"
    DuplicateGift(card str) "duplicate gift {card}"
    UnknownGift(card str) "unknown gift {card}"
    EmptyGift(card str) "gift {card} is empty"

pub struct Shop
    pub stock catalog.Catalog
    pub people customers.Customers
    pub deals promos.Promos
    pub book orders.Orders
    pub buying purchasing.Purchases
    pub cards gifts.Cards

pub fn Shop.new() Shop
    Shop(
        stock: catalog.Catalog.new(),
        people: customers.Customers.new(),
        deals: promos.Promos.new(),
        book: orders.Orders.new(),
        buying: purchasing.Purchases.new(),
        cards: gifts.Cards.new(),
    )

## Applies one entry; a rejected entry changes nothing.
pub fn Shop.apply(mut self, e journal.Entry) ! Problem
    match e
        Item(sku, cat, cents) => self.item(sku, cat, cents)?
        Tax(cat, pct) => self.stock.set_rate(cat, pct)
        Restock(sku, qty) => self.restock(sku, qty)?
        Adjust(sku, qty) => self.adjust(sku, qty)?
        Customer(cust, tier) => self.people.set_tier(cust, tier)
        Promo(code, cat, pct, uses) => self.promo(code, cat, pct, uses)?
        Purchase(po, buys) => self.purchase(po, buys)?
        Receive(po) => self.receive(po)?
        Gift(card, cents) => self.gift(card, cents)?
        Order(id, cust, wants) => self.order(id, cust, wants)?
        Apply(id, code) => self.apply_promo(id, code)?
        Pay(id, cents) => self.pay(id, cents)?
        PayCredit(id) => self.pay_credit(id)?
        PayGift(id, card) => self.pay_gift(id, card)?
        Ship(id) => self.ship(id)?
        Cancel(id) => self.cancel(id)?

fn Shop.item(mut self, sku str, cat str, cents int) ! Problem
    mut it := self.stock.get(sku) else catalog.Item(
        cat: cat,
        price: cents,
        onhand: 0,
        reserved: 0,
        value: 0,
    )
    if it.cat != cat
        return CategoryChanged(sku)
    it.price = cents
    self.stock.put(sku, it)

fn Shop.restock(mut self, sku str, qty int) ! Problem
    mut it := self.stock.get(sku) else return UnknownItem(sku)
    it.onhand += qty
    self.stock.put(sku, it)

fn Shop.adjust(mut self, sku str, qty int) ! Problem
    it := self.stock.get(sku) else return UnknownItem(sku)
    if qty < it.reserved
        return BelowReserved(sku)
    self.stock.stocktake(sku, qty)

fn Shop.promo(mut self, code str, cat str, pct int, uses int) ! Problem
    if self.deals.has(code)
        return DuplicatePromo(code)
    self.deals.add(code, promos.Promo(cat: cat, pct: pct, uses: uses, used: 0))

fn Shop.purchase(mut self, po str, buys List[journal.Buy]) ! Problem
    if self.buying.has(po)
        return DuplicatePurchase(po)
    for b in buys
        if not self.stock.has(b.sku)
            return UnknownItem(b.sku)
    self.buying.put(purchasing.Purchase(po: po, status: purchasing.PoStatus.Ordered, buys: buys))

fn Shop.receive(mut self, po str) ! Problem
    mut p := self.buying.find(po) else return UnknownPurchase(po)
    if p.status != purchasing.PoStatus.Ordered
        return PurchaseStatus(po, p.status.text())
    for b in p.buys
        self.stock.receive(b.sku, b.qty, b.qty * b.cents)
    p.status = purchasing.PoStatus.Received
    self.buying.put(p)

fn Shop.gift(mut self, card str, cents int) ! Problem
    if self.cards.has(card)
        return DuplicateGift(card)
    self.cards.sell(card, cents)

fn Shop.order(mut self, id str, cust str, wants List[journal.Want]) ! Problem
    if self.book.has(id)
        return DuplicateOrder(id)
    if not self.people.has(cust)
        return UnknownCustomer(cust)
    for known in wants
        if not self.stock.has(known.sku)
            return UnknownItem(known.sku)
    for enough in wants
        if self.stock.item(enough.sku).available() < enough.qty
            return Short(enough.sku)
    tier := customers.tier_pct(self.people.get(cust).tier)
    mut lines := List[pricing.Line]()
    for w in wants
        it := self.stock.item(w.sku)
        lines.push(pricing.fresh_line(
            w.sku,
            w.qty,
            it.price,
            it.cat,
            self.stock.rate(it.cat),
            tier,
        ))
        self.stock.reserve(w.sku, w.qty)
    placed := orders.Order(
        id: id,
        cust: cust,
        status: orders.Status.Open,
        lines: lines,
        promo: "",
        paid: 0,
    )
    self.book.put(self.repriced(placed))

## The order with every line priced again under its promo, if it has one.
fn Shop.repriced(self, o orders.Order) orders.Order
    mut cat := ""
    mut pct := 0
    if p := self.deals.get(o.promo)
        cat = p.cat
        pct = p.pct
    mut lines := List[pricing.Line]()
    for l in o.lines
        lines.push(pricing.priced(l, cat, pct))
    mut out := o
    out.lines = lines
    out

## The order `id`, which must have status `want`.
fn Shop.order_in(self, id str, want orders.Status) orders.Order ! Problem
    o := self.book.find(id) else return UnknownOrder(id)
    if o.status != want
        return WrongStatus(id, o.status.text())
    o

fn Shop.apply_promo(mut self, id str, code str) ! Problem
    o := self.order_in(id, orders.Status.Open)?
    p := self.deals.get(code) else return UnknownPromo(code)
    if o.promo != ""
        return PromoAlready(id)
    if p.used >= p.uses
        return UsedUp(code)
    if not o.has_cat(p.cat)
        return NotApplicable(code)
    self.deals.count_use(code, 1)
    mut with_promo := o
    with_promo.promo = code
    mut done := self.repriced(with_promo)
    if done.paid >= done.total()
        self.people.add_credit(done.cust, done.paid - done.total())
        done.paid = done.total()
        done.status = orders.Status.Paid
    self.book.put(done)

fn Shop.pay(mut self, id str, cents int) ! Problem
    o := self.order_in(id, orders.Status.Open)?
    self.settle(o, cents)

fn Shop.pay_credit(mut self, id str) ! Problem
    o := self.order_in(id, orders.Status.Open)?
    credit := self.people.get(o.cust).credit
    if credit == 0
        return NoCredit(o.cust)
    amount := credit.min(o.due())
    self.people.add_credit(o.cust, -amount)
    self.settle(o, amount)

fn Shop.pay_gift(mut self, id str, card str) ! Problem
    o := self.order_in(id, orders.Status.Open)?
    c := self.cards.find(card) else return UnknownGift(card)
    if c.balance == 0
        return EmptyGift(card)
    amount := c.balance.min(o.due())
    self.cards.draw(card, amount)
    self.settle(o, amount)

## Counts `amount` towards what is due on `o`; any amount above it goes to the customer's credit.
fn Shop.settle(mut self, o orders.Order, amount int)
    applied := amount.min(o.due())
    mut settled := o
    settled.paid += applied
    self.people.add_credit(o.cust, amount - applied)
    if settled.paid == settled.total()
        settled.status = orders.Status.Paid
    self.book.put(settled)

fn Shop.ship(mut self, id str) ! Problem
    mut o := self.order_in(id, orders.Status.Paid)?
    mut lines := List[pricing.Line]()
    for l in o.lines
        mut shipped := l
        shipped.cost = self.stock.take(l.sku, l.qty)
        lines.push(shipped)
    o.lines = lines
    o.status = orders.Status.Shipped
    self.book.put(o)

fn Shop.cancel(mut self, id str) ! Problem
    mut o := self.book.find(id) else return UnknownOrder(id)
    if o.status == orders.Status.Shipped or o.status == orders.Status.Cancelled
        return WrongStatus(id, o.status.text())
    for l in o.lines
        self.stock.reserve(l.sku, -l.qty)
    self.people.add_credit(o.cust, o.paid)
    o.paid = 0
    if o.promo != ""
        self.deals.count_use(o.promo, -1)
    o.status = orders.Status.Cancelled
    self.book.put(o)

## The catalog: each SKU's category, price and stock, and each category's tax rate.
use money

pub struct Item
    pub cat str
    pub price int
    pub onhand int
    ## Units held by orders that are open or paid.
    pub reserved int
    ## What the units on hand cost the shop, in cents (average cost).
    pub value int

## Units on hand that no order holds.
pub fn Item.available(self) int
    self.onhand - self.reserved

pub struct Catalog
    items Map[str, Item]
    rates Map[str, int]

pub fn Catalog.new() Catalog
    Catalog(items: Map[str, Item](), rates: Map[str, int]())

pub fn Catalog.has(self, sku str) bool
    self.items.contains(sku)

pub fn Catalog.get(self, sku str) Item?
    self.items.get(sku)

## The item of a SKU that `has` reports; traps otherwise.
pub fn Catalog.item(self, sku str) Item
    self.items[sku]

## Every SKU in the catalog, in ascending byte order.
pub fn Catalog.skus(self) List[str]
    self.items.keys().sorted()

pub fn Catalog.put(mut self, sku str, it Item)
    self.items[sku] = it

## The tax rate of a category in percent; 0 until a `tax` entry sets it.
pub fn Catalog.rate(self, cat str) int
    self.rates.get(cat) else 0

pub fn Catalog.set_rate(mut self, cat str, pct int)
    self.rates[cat] = pct

## Changes the reserved quantity of a SKU by `by` units; a negative `by` releases them.
pub fn Catalog.reserve(mut self, sku str, by int)
    mut it := self.items[sku]
    it.reserved += by
    self.items[sku] = it

## Ships `qty` reserved units: they leave both the on-hand and the reserved quantity,
## taking their share of the stock value. Returns that share, the cost of the units.
pub fn Catalog.take(mut self, sku str, qty int) int
    mut it := self.items[sku]
    cost := it.value * qty / it.onhand
    it.value -= cost
    it.onhand -= qty
    it.reserved -= qty
    self.items[sku] = it
    cost

## Adds `qty` units that cost `cents` in all.
pub fn Catalog.receive(mut self, sku str, qty int, cents int)
    mut it := self.items[sku]
    it.onhand += qty
    it.value += cents
    self.items[sku] = it

## A stocktake: sets the units on hand, scaling the stock value with them.
pub fn Catalog.stocktake(mut self, sku str, qty int)
    mut it := self.items[sku]
    if it.onhand > 0
        it.value = it.value * qty / it.onhand
    it.onhand = qty
    self.items[sku] = it

## The tax on a line's net amount at `rate` percent.
pub fn tax(net int, rate int) int
    money.percent(net, rate)

## Purchase orders to suppliers: goods ordered, then received into stock.
use journal

pub enum PoStatus
    Ordered
    Received

pub fn PoStatus.text(self) str
    match self
        Ordered => "ordered"
        Received => "received"

pub struct Purchase
    pub po str
    pub status PoStatus
    pub buys List[journal.Buy]

## The units of every SKU on the purchase order.
pub fn Purchase.units(self) int
    mut sum := 0
    for b in self.buys
        sum += b.qty
    sum

## What the goods cost: QTY × CENTS over every SKU.
pub fn Purchase.cost(self) int
    mut sum := 0
    for b in self.buys
        sum += b.qty * b.cents
    sum

pub struct Purchases
    entered Map[str, Purchase]

pub fn Purchases.new() Purchases
    Purchases(entered: Map[str, Purchase]())

pub fn Purchases.has(self, po str) bool
    self.entered.contains(po)

pub fn Purchases.find(self, po str) Purchase?
    self.entered.get(po)

## Adds a new purchase order after the others, or replaces the one with the same PO in place.
pub fn Purchases.put(mut self, p Purchase)
    self.entered[p.po] = p

## Every purchase order, in the order they were entered.
pub fn Purchases.all(self) List[Purchase]
    self.entered.values()

## Registered customers: their tier and their credit.
use money

pub struct Customer
    pub tier str
    ## Cents the shop owes the customer: overpayments and refunds of cancelled orders.
    pub credit int

pub struct Customers
    known Map[str, Customer]

pub fn Customers.new() Customers
    Customers(known: Map[str, Customer]())

pub fn Customers.has(self, id str) bool
    self.known.contains(id)

## The customer `id`, which `has` reports; traps otherwise.
pub fn Customers.get(self, id str) Customer
    self.known[id]

## Every registered customer, in ascending byte order.
pub fn Customers.ids(self) List[str]
    self.known.keys().sorted()

## Registers `id` with no credit, or changes the tier of a registered customer.
pub fn Customers.set_tier(mut self, id str, tier str)
    mut c := self.known.get(id) else Customer(tier: tier, credit: 0)
    c.tier = tier
    self.known[id] = c

## Adds `cents` to the customer's credit; a negative amount takes credit away.
pub fn Customers.add_credit(mut self, id str, cents int)
    mut c := self.known[id]
    c.credit += cents
    self.known[id] = c

## The tier discount in percent: 0 for `basic`, 5 for `silver`, 10 for `gold`.
pub fn tier_pct(tier str) int
    if tier == "gold"
        return 10
    if tier == "silver"
        return 5
    0

## The tier discount on a line's gross amount.
pub fn discount(gross int, pct int) int
    money.percent(gross, pct)

The shop now calls its customers *accounts*, in the journal, in the reports and in the code. Change `till` (spec in `DOCS/spec.md`, sources in `src/`) as follows, and keep everything else as specified there.

## till: a shop's back office. Reads the journal on stdin and prints one report (spec.md).
use cli
use journal
use reports
use shop

## Prints `error: no WHAT` and ends the program with exit code 3.
fn missing(what str)
    io.eprint("error: no {what}")
    io.exit(3)

fn main()
    cmd := cli.parse(env.args())
    if cmd == cli.Command.Usage
        io.eprint(cli.usage())
        io.exit(1)
    mut lines := io.read_all().split("\n")
    if (lines.last() else "x") == ""
        lines.pop()
    mut s := shop.Shop.new()
    mut bad := 0
    for k in 0..lines.len()
        line := lines[k]
        if line.is_empty() or line.starts_with("#")
            continue
        e := journal.parse(line) else err
            io.eprint("error: line {k + 1}: {err}")
            bad += 1
            continue
        s.apply(e) else err
            io.eprint("error: line {k + 1}: {err}")
            bad += 1
    mut out := List[str]()
    match cmd
        ShowOrders => out = reports.order_lines(s)
        Invoice(id) =>
            out = reports.invoice(s, id) else List[str]()
            if not s.book.has(id)
                missing("order {id}")
        ShowStock => out = reports.stock_lines(s)
        Low(n) => out = reports.low(s, n)
        ShowAccounts => out = reports.account_lines(s)
        History(acct) =>
            out = reports.history(s, acct) else List[str]()
            if not s.people.has(acct)
                missing("account {acct}")
        Sales => out = reports.sales(s)
        Margin => out = reports.margin(s)
        Purchases => out = reports.purchase_lines(s)
        Gifts => out = reports.gift_lines(s)
        ShowPromos => out = reports.promo_lines(s)
        Usage => return
    for l in out
        print(l)
    if bad > 0
        io.exit(2)

## The reports, as lines without their newline (spec "Reports").
use money
use orders
use shop

## Each placed order: `ORDER ID STATUS TOTAL PAID`.
pub fn order_lines(s shop.Shop) List[str]
    mut out := List[str]()
    for o in s.book.all()
        out.push("{o.id}\t{o.acct}\t{o.status.text()}\t{money.show(o.total())}\t{money.show(o.paid)}")
    out

## The invoice of order `id`, or `none` if it was never placed.
pub fn invoice(s shop.Shop, id str) List[str]?
    o := s.book.find(id) else return none
    mut out := ["order {o.id} {o.acct} {o.status.text()}"]
    mut gross := 0
    mut discount := 0
    mut tax := 0
    for l in o.lines
        amounts := [l.price, l.gross, l.discount, l.tax, l.total].map(|c| money.show(c)).join("\t")
        out.push("{l.sku}\t{l.qty}\t{amounts}")
        gross += l.gross
        discount += l.discount
        tax += l.tax
    if o.promo != ""
        out.push("promo\t{o.promo}")
    due := if o.status == orders.Status.Open then o.due() else 0
    out.push("subtotal\t{money.show(gross)}")
    out.push("discount\t{money.show(discount)}")
    out.push("tax\t{money.show(tax)}")
    out.push("total\t{money.show(o.total())}")
    out.push("paid\t{money.show(o.paid)}")
    out.push("due\t{money.show(due)}")
    out

## Each catalog SKU: `SKU CAT PRICE ONHAND RESERVED AVAILABLE VALUE`.
pub fn stock_lines(s shop.Shop) List[str]
    mut out := List[str]()
    for sku in s.stock.skus()
        it := s.stock.item(sku)
        out.push("{sku}\t{it.cat}\t{money.show(it.price)}\t{it.onhand}\t{it.reserved}\t{it.available()}\t{money.show(it.value)}")
    out

## Each catalog SKU with fewer than `n` units available: `SKU AVAILABLE`.
pub fn low(s shop.Shop, n int) List[str]
    mut out := List[str]()
    for sku in s.stock.skus()
        left := s.stock.item(sku).available()
        if left < n
            out.push("{sku}\t{left}")
    out

## Each account: `ID TIER ORDERS SPENT CREDIT`.
pub fn account_lines(s shop.Shop) List[str]
    mut out := List[str]()
    for acct in s.people.ids()
        c := s.people.get(acct)
        mut placed := 0
        mut spent := 0
        for o in s.book.of(acct)
            if o.status != orders.Status.Cancelled
                placed += 1
            if o.status == orders.Status.Shipped
                spent += o.total()
        out.push("{acct}\t{c.tier}\t{placed}\t{money.show(spent)}\t{money.show(c.credit)}")
    out

## An account's orders, `ORDER STATUS TOTAL`, then `credit`; `none` for an account never registered.
pub fn history(s shop.Shop, acct str) List[str]?
    if not s.people.has(acct)
        return none
    mut out := List[str]()
    for o in s.book.of(acct)
        out.push("{o.id}\t{o.status.text()}\t{money.show(o.total())}")
    out.push("credit\t{money.show(s.people.get(acct).credit)}")
    out

struct Tally
    units int
    net int
    tax int

## Units, net and tax of the shipped lines, by category, then `total`.
pub fn sales(s shop.Shop) List[str]
    mut cats := Map[str, Tally]()
    mut overall := Tally(units: 0, net: 0, tax: 0)
    for o in s.book.all()
        if o.status != orders.Status.Shipped
            continue
        for l in o.lines
            mut t := cats.get(l.cat) else Tally(units: 0, net: 0, tax: 0)
            t.units += l.qty
            t.net += l.net
            t.tax += l.tax
            cats[l.cat] = t
            overall.units += l.qty
            overall.net += l.net
            overall.tax += l.tax
    mut out := List[str]()
    for cat in cats.keys().sorted()
        row := cats[cat]
        out.push("{cat}\t{row.units}\t{money.show(row.net)}\t{money.show(row.tax)}")
    out.push("total\t{overall.units}\t{money.show(overall.net)}\t{money.show(overall.tax)}")
    out

struct Margin
    net int
    cost int

fn margin_line(name str, m Margin) str
    "{name}\t{money.show(m.net)}\t{money.show(m.cost)}\t{money.show(m.net - m.cost)}"

## Net, cost and margin of the shipped lines, by category, then `total`.
pub fn margin(s shop.Shop) List[str]
    mut cats := Map[str, Margin]()
    mut overall := Margin(net: 0, cost: 0)
    for o in s.book.all()
        if o.status != orders.Status.Shipped
            continue
        for l in o.lines
            mut m := cats.get(l.cat) else Margin(net: 0, cost: 0)
            m.net += l.net
            m.cost += l.cost
            cats[l.cat] = m
            overall.net += l.net
            overall.cost += l.cost
    mut out := List[str]()
    for cat in cats.keys().sorted()
        out.push(margin_line(cat, cats[cat]))
    out.push(margin_line("total", overall))
    out

## Each purchase order: `PO STATUS UNITS COST`.
pub fn purchase_lines(s shop.Shop) List[str]
    mut out := List[str]()
    for p in s.buying.all()
        out.push("{p.po}\t{p.status.text()}\t{p.units()}\t{money.show(p.cost())}")
    out

## Each gift card: `CARD SOLD BALANCE`.
pub fn gift_lines(s shop.Shop) List[str]
    mut out := List[str]()
    for card in s.cards.all_cards()
        c := s.cards.find(card) else continue
        out.push("{card}\t{money.show(c.sold)}\t{money.show(c.balance)}")
    out

## Each promo code: `CODE CAT PCT% USED/USES`.
pub fn promo_lines(s shop.Shop) List[str]
    mut out := List[str]()
    for code in s.deals.all_codes()
        p := s.deals.get(code) else continue
        out.push("{code}\t{p.cat}\t{p.pct}%\t{p.used}/{p.uses}")
    out

## Pricing of order lines (spec "Prices"). The amounts are computed from the fields an
## order fixes when it is placed (price, tax rate, tier discount) and the order's promo.
use catalog
use accounts
use promos

pub struct Line
    pub sku str
    pub qty int
    pub price int
    pub cat str
    ## Tax rate of the category, in percent, when the order was placed.
    pub rate int
    ## Tier discount of the account, in percent, when the order was placed.
    pub tier int
    pub gross int
    ## Tier discount plus promo discount.
    pub discount int
    pub net int
    pub tax int
    pub total int
    ## What the shipped units cost the shop; 0 until the order ships.
    pub cost int

## A line whose amounts `priced` has still to fill in.
pub fn fresh_line(sku str, qty int, price int, cat str, rate int, tier int) Line
    Line(
        sku: sku,
        qty: qty,
        price: price,
        cat: cat,
        rate: rate,
        tier: tier,
        gross: 0,
        discount: 0,
        net: 0,
        tax: 0,
        total: 0,
        cost: 0,
    )

## The line with its amounts computed. The promo (`promo_pct` off lines of `promo_cat`)
## applies only to lines of that category; pass `""` when the order has no promo.
pub fn priced(l Line, promo_cat str, promo_pct int) Line
    mut p := l
    p.gross = l.price * l.qty
    tier_off := accounts.discount(p.gross, l.tier)
    mut promo_off := 0
    if promo_cat == l.cat
        promo_off = promos.discount(p.gross - tier_off, promo_pct)
    p.discount = tier_off + promo_off
    p.net = p.gross - p.discount
    p.tax = catalog.tax(p.net, l.rate)
    p.total = p.net + p.tax
    p

## The shapes of journal and command-line fields (spec "Fields").

fn upper(ch char) bool
    match ch
        'A'..='Z' => true
        _ => false

fn lower(ch char) bool
    match ch
        'a'..='z' => true
        _ => false

fn digit(ch char) bool
    match ch
        '0'..='9' => true
        _ => false

fn sku_char(ch char) bool
    upper(ch) or digit(ch) or ch == '-'

fn code_char(ch char) bool
    upper(ch) or digit(ch)

fn id_char(ch char) bool
    lower(ch) or digit(ch)

## `lo` to `hi` characters, the first accepted by `first` and every one by `rest`.
fn shaped(s str, lo int, hi int, first fn(char) bool, rest fn(char) bool) bool
    if s.len() < lo or s.len() > hi
        return false
    cs := s.chars()
    if not first(cs[0])
        return false
    for ch in cs
        if not rest(ch)
            return false
    true

## 1 to `width` ASCII digits, as a number (leading zeros allowed); `none` for anything else.
pub fn digits(s str, width int) int?
    if s.is_empty() or s.len() > width
        return none
    for ch in s.chars()
        if not digit(ch)
            return none
    s.to_int()

## SKU: 1 to 12 of `A-Z 0-9 -`, starting with a letter.
pub fn is_sku(s str) bool
    shaped(s, 1, 12, upper, sku_char)

## CAT: 1 to 12 letters `a-z`.
pub fn is_cat(s str) bool
    shaped(s, 1, 12, lower, lower)

## ID: 1 to 12 of `a-z 0-9`, starting with a letter.
pub fn is_id(s str) bool
    shaped(s, 1, 12, lower, id_char)

## CODE: 3 to 10 of `A-Z 0-9`, starting with a letter.
pub fn is_code(s str) bool
    shaped(s, 3, 10, upper, code_char)

## ORDER: `o` and 1 to 6 digits.
pub fn is_order(s str) bool
    rest := s.strip_prefix("o") else return false
    (digits(rest, 6) else -1) >= 0

## PO: `p` and 1 to 6 digits.
pub fn is_po(s str) bool
    rest := s.strip_prefix("p") else return false
    (digits(rest, 6) else -1) >= 0

## CARD: `g` and 1 to 6 digits.
pub fn is_card(s str) bool
    rest := s.strip_prefix("g") else return false
    (digits(rest, 6) else -1) >= 0

## TIER: `basic`, `silver` or `gold`.
pub fn is_tier(s str) bool
    s == "basic" or s == "silver" or s == "gold"

## Money is whole cents; reports print it as dollars (spec "Prices").

## `a × p / 100` rounded to the nearest cent, halves up. `a` is never negative.
pub fn percent(a int, p int) int
    (a * p + 50) / 100

## Cents as dollars with exactly two decimals: `1234.05`, `0.50`, `-0.50`.
pub fn show(c int) str
    sign := if c < 0 then "-" else ""
    a := c.abs()
    "{sign}{a / 100}.{a % 100:0>2}"

## The command line: which report to print (spec "Reports", "Exit codes and stderr").
use fields

pub enum Command
    ShowOrders
    Invoice(id str)
    ShowStock
    Low(n int)
    ShowAccounts
    History(acct str)
    Sales
    Margin
    Purchases
    Gifts
    ShowPromos
    ## Missing, unknown or malformed: print the usage line and exit 1.
    Usage

pub fn usage() str
    "usage: till orders|invoice ORDER|stock|low N|accounts|history ID|sales|margin|purchases|gifts|promos"

## The command the arguments ask for (the program name is not one of them).
pub fn parse(args List[str]) Command
    if args.len() == 1
        return match args[0]
            "orders" => Command.ShowOrders
            "stock" => Command.ShowStock
            "accounts" => Command.ShowAccounts
            "sales" => Command.Sales
            "margin" => Command.Margin
            "purchases" => Command.Purchases
            "gifts" => Command.Gifts
            "promos" => Command.ShowPromos
            _ => Command.Usage
    if args.len() != 2
        return Command.Usage
    arg := args[1]
    if args[0] == "invoice" and fields.is_order(arg)
        return Command.Invoice(id: arg)
    if args[0] == "history" and fields.is_id(arg)
        return Command.History(acct: arg)
    if args[0] == "low"
        n := fields.digits(arg, 5) else return Command.Usage
        return Command.Low(n: n)
    Command.Usage
