struct Tok
    kind int
    text str

struct P
    toks List[Tok]
    pos int
    ev bool
    depth int
    vars Map[str, int]

fn is_letter(c char) bool
    (c >= 'a' and c <= 'z') or (c >= 'A' and c <= 'Z') or c == '_'

fn is_digit(c char) bool
    c >= '0' and c <= '9'

## kind 0 number, 1 name, 2 operator; none when the line is lexically bad
fn lex(cs List[char]) List[Tok]?
    mut out := List[Tok]()
    mut i := 0
    n := cs.len()
    while i < n
        c := cs[i]
        if c == ' '
            i += 1
        elif is_digit(c)
            mut j := i
            while j < n and is_digit(cs[j])
                j += 1
            if j - i > 12
                return none
            out.push(Tok(kind: 0, text: cs[i..j].join("")))
            i = j
        elif is_letter(c)
            mut j := i
            while j < n and (is_letter(cs[j]) or is_digit(cs[j]))
                j += 1
            if j - i > 32
                return none
            out.push(Tok(kind: 1, text: cs[i..j].join("")))
            i = j
        else
            two := if i + 1 < n then "{c}{cs[i + 1]}" else ""
            if two == "<=" or two == ">=" or two == "==" or two == "!="
                out.push(Tok(kind: 2, text: two))
                i += 2
            elif c == '+' or c == '-' or c == '*' or c == '/' or c == '%' or c == '(' or c == ')' or c == '=' or c == '<' or c == '>'
                out.push(Tok(kind: 2, text: "{c}"))
                i += 1
            else
                return none
    out

fn P.peek(self) str
    if self.pos < self.toks.len() and self.toks[self.pos].kind == 2
        self.toks[self.pos].text
    else
        ""

fn chk(v int) int ! str
    if v > 1000000000 or v < -1000000000
        return "out of range"
    v

fn P.cmp(mut self) int ! str
    a := self.add()?
    op := self.peek()
    if op == "<" or op == "<=" or op == ">" or op == ">=" or op == "==" or op == "!="
        self.pos += 1
        b := self.add()?
        r := match op
            "<" => a < b
            "<=" => a <= b
            ">" => a > b
            ">=" => a >= b
            "==" => a == b
            _ => a != b
        return if r then 1 else 0
    a

fn P.add(mut self) int ! str
    mut a := self.mul()?
    while self.peek() == "+" or self.peek() == "-"
        op := self.peek()
        self.pos += 1
        b := self.mul()?
        a = chk(if op == "+" then a + b else a - b)?
    a

fn P.mul(mut self) int ! str
    mut a := self.unary()?
    while self.peek() == "*" or self.peek() == "/" or self.peek() == "%"
        op := self.peek()
        self.pos += 1
        b := self.unary()?
        if op == "*"
            a = chk(a * b)?
        elif b == 0
            if self.ev
                return "divide by zero"
            a = 0
        elif op == "/"
            a = chk(a / b)?
        else
            a = a % b
    a

fn P.unary(mut self) int ! str
    if self.peek() == "-"
        self.pos += 1
        v := self.unary()?
        return chk(0 - v)?
    self.atom()?

fn P.atom(mut self) int ! str
    if self.pos >= self.toks.len()
        return "syntax"
    t := self.toks[self.pos]
    if t.kind == 0
        self.pos += 1
        v := t.text.to_int() else 0
        if not self.ev
            return 0
        if v > 1000000000
            if self.ev
                return "out of range"
            return 0
        return v
    if t.kind == 1
        if t.text == "print"
            return "syntax"
        self.pos += 1
        if not self.ev
            return 0
        return self.vars.get(t.text) else return "undefined {t.text}"
    if t.text == "("
        self.pos += 1
        self.depth += 1
        if self.depth > 50
            return "syntax"
        v := self.cmp()?
        if self.peek() != ")"
            return "syntax"
        self.pos += 1
        self.depth -= 1
        return v
    return "syntax"

## Parses an expression from `start`; the whole line must be consumed.
fn run_expr(toks List[Tok], start int, ev bool, vars Map[str, int]) int ! str
    mut p := P(toks: toks, pos: start, ev: ev, depth: 0, vars: vars)
    v := p.cmp()?
    if p.pos != toks.len()
        return "syntax"
    v

fn main()
    args := env.args()
    if args.len() > 0
        io.eprint("usage: tally")
        io.exit(1)
    text := io.read_all()
    mut vars := Map[str, int]()
    mut bad := false
    mut k := 0
    for line in text.split("\n")
        k += 1
        cs := line.chars()
        mut f := 0
        while f < cs.len() and cs[f] == ' '
            f += 1
        if f >= cs.len() or cs[f] == '#'
            continue
        toks := lex(cs) else
            io.eprint("error: line {k}: syntax")
            bad = true
            continue
        mut start := 0
        mut target := ""
        mut isprint := false
        if toks.len() >= 1 and toks[0].kind == 1
            if toks[0].text == "print"
                isprint = true
                start = 1
            elif toks.len() >= 2 and toks[1].kind == 2 and toks[1].text == "="
                target = toks[0].text
                start = 2
            else
                start = -1
        else
            start = -1
        if start < 0
            io.eprint("error: line {k}: syntax")
            bad = true
            continue
        probe := run_expr(toks, start, false, vars) else e
            -1
        if probe == -1
            io.eprint("error: line {k}: syntax")
            bad = true
            continue
        v := run_expr(toks, start, true, vars) else e
            io.eprint("error: line {k}: {e}")
            bad = true
            continue
        if isprint
            print(v)
        else
            vars[target] = v
    if bad
        io.exit(2)

struct Node
    kind int        # 0 num, 1 var, 2 neg, 3 bin
    op str
    a int
    b int
    val int
    name str

struct P
    toks List[str]
    tk List[int]    # 0 num, 1 name, 2 op
    pos int
    bad bool
    depth int
    nodes List[Node]

fn is_digit(c char) bool
    c >= '0' and c <= '9'

fn is_alpha(c char) bool
    (c >= 'a' and c <= 'z') or (c >= 'A' and c <= 'Z') or c == '_'

fn tokenize(line str) (List[str], List[int], bool)
    mut toks := List[str]()
    mut tk := List[int]()
    cs := line.chars()
    n := cs.len()
    mut i := 0
    while i < n
        c := cs[i]
        if c == ' '
            i += 1
        elif is_digit(c)
            mut j := i
            mut parts := List[str]()
            while j < n and is_digit(cs[j])
                parts.push("{cs[j]}")
                j += 1
            if j - i > 12
                return ([], [], false)
            toks.push(parts.join(""))
            tk.push(0)
            i = j
        elif is_alpha(c)
            mut j := i
            mut parts := List[str]()
            while j < n and (is_alpha(cs[j]) or is_digit(cs[j]))
                parts.push("{cs[j]}")
                j += 1
            if j - i > 32
                return ([], [], false)
            toks.push(parts.join(""))
            tk.push(1)
            i = j
        else
            nx := if i + 1 < n then cs[i + 1] else ' '
            if (c == '<' or c == '>' or c == '=' or c == '!') and nx == '='
                toks.push("{c}=")
                tk.push(2)
                i += 2
            elif c == '+' or c == '-' or c == '*' or c == '/' or c == '%' or c == '(' or c == ')' or c == '=' or c == '<' or c == '>'
                toks.push("{c}")
                tk.push(2)
                i += 1
            else
                return ([], [], false)
    (toks, tk, true)

fn P.peek(self) str
    if self.pos < self.toks.len() and self.tk[self.pos] == 2
        self.toks[self.pos]
    else
        ""

fn P.add(mut self, kind int, op str, a int, b int, val int, name str) int
    self.nodes.push(Node(kind: kind, op: op, a: a, b: b, val: val, name: name))
    self.nodes.len() - 1

fn P.cmp(mut self) int
    l := self.sum()
    if self.bad
        return 0
    op := self.peek()
    if op == "<" or op == "<=" or op == ">" or op == ">=" or op == "==" or op == "!="
        self.pos += 1
        r := self.sum()
        return self.add(3, op, l, r, 0, "")
    l

fn P.sum(mut self) int
    mut l := self.term()
    while not self.bad
        op := self.peek()
        if op == "+" or op == "-"
            self.pos += 1
            r := self.term()
            l = self.add(3, op, l, r, 0, "")
        else
            break
    l

fn P.term(mut self) int
    mut l := self.unary()
    while not self.bad
        op := self.peek()
        if op == "*" or op == "/" or op == "%"
            self.pos += 1
            r := self.unary()
            l = self.add(3, op, l, r, 0, "")
        else
            break
    l

fn P.unary(mut self) int
    if self.bad
        return 0
    if self.peek() == "-"
        self.pos += 1
        x := self.unary()
        return self.add(2, "", x, 0, 0, "")
    self.atom()

fn P.atom(mut self) int
    if self.pos >= self.toks.len()
        self.bad = true
        return 0
    t := self.toks[self.pos]
    k := self.tk[self.pos]
    if k == 0
        self.pos += 1
        return self.add(0, "", 0, 0, t.to_int() else 0, "")
    if k == 1
        if t == "print"
            self.bad = true
            return 0
        self.pos += 1
        return self.add(1, "", 0, 0, 0, t)
    if t == "("
        self.pos += 1
        self.depth += 1
        if self.depth > 50
            self.bad = true
            return 0
        e := self.cmp()
        if self.bad
            return 0
        if self.peek() != ")"
            self.bad = true
            return 0
        self.pos += 1
        self.depth -= 1
        return e
    self.bad = true
    0

struct Ev
    nodes List[Node]
    vars Map[str, int]
    err str

fn Ev.eval(mut self, i int) int
    n := self.nodes[i]
    if n.kind == 0
        if n.val > 1000000000
            self.err = "out of range"
        return n.val
    if n.kind == 1
        v := self.vars.get(n.name) else
            self.err = "undefined {n.name}"
            return 0
        return v
    if n.kind == 2
        x := self.eval(n.a)
        if self.err != ""
            return 0
        return self.chk(-x)
    l := self.eval(n.a)
    if self.err != ""
        return 0
    r := self.eval(n.b)
    if self.err != ""
        return 0
    if n.op == "+"
        return self.chk(l + r)
    if n.op == "-"
        return self.chk(l - r)
    if n.op == "*"
        return self.chk(l * r)
    if n.op == "/" or n.op == "%"
        if r == 0
            self.err = "divide by zero"
            return 0
        if n.op == "/"
            return self.chk(l / r)
        return l % r
    if n.op == "<"
        return if l < r then 1 else 0
    if n.op == "<="
        return if l <= r then 1 else 0
    if n.op == ">"
        return if l > r then 1 else 0
    if n.op == ">="
        return if l >= r then 1 else 0
    if n.op == "=="
        return if l == r then 1 else 0
    return if l != r then 1 else 0

fn Ev.chk(mut self, v int) int
    if v > 1000000000 or v < -1000000000
        self.err = "out of range"
    v

fn fail(k int, msg str)
    io.eprint("error: line {k}: {msg}")

fn main()
    if env.args().len() > 0
        io.eprint("usage: tally")
        io.exit(1)
    text := io.read_all()
    mut vars := Map[str, int]()
    mut code := 0
    mut k := 0
    for line in text.split("\n")
        k += 1
        s := line.trim()
        if s == "" or s.starts_with("#")
            continue
        toks, tk, ok := tokenize(line)
        if not ok
            fail(k, "syntax")
            code = 2
            continue
        mut p := P(toks: toks, tk: tk, pos: 0, bad: false, depth: 0, nodes: [])
        mut target := ""
        if toks.len() == 0 or tk[0] != 1
            fail(k, "syntax")
            code = 2
            continue
        is_print := toks[0] == "print"
        if is_print
            p.pos = 1
        else
            if toks.len() < 2 or toks[1] != "=" or tk[1] != 2
                fail(k, "syntax")
                code = 2
                continue
            target = toks[0]
            p.pos = 2
        root := p.cmp()
        if p.bad or p.pos != toks.len()
            fail(k, "syntax")
            code = 2
            continue
        mut ev := Ev(nodes: p.nodes, vars: vars, err: "")
        v := ev.eval(root)
        if ev.err != ""

# tally

Write `tally`, a command-line program. It reads a script from stdin, one statement per line, and runs the statements in order.

Statements:
- `NAME = EXPR` evaluates EXPR and stores the value in the variable NAME.
- `print EXPR` evaluates EXPR and prints the value in decimal on its own line on stdout.
- A line that is empty, has only spaces, or whose first character after any leading spaces is `#` is ignored.

Tokens: a number is one or more digits (at most 12). A name is a letter or `_` followed by letters, digits and `_` (at most 32 characters). `print` is a keyword and never a variable. The operators are `+ - * / % ( ) = < <= > >= == !=`. Spaces may appear before, between and after tokens and are needed only between two tokens that would otherwise read as one. Any other character makes the line a syntax error.

Expressions, loosest binding first:
- one comparison at most: `A < B`, with `< <= > >= == !=`; the value is 1 when it holds, else 0. `1 < 2 < 3` is a syntax error; `(1 < 2) < 3` is fine.
- `+` and `-`, left to right.
- `*`, `/` and `%`, left to right. `/` drops the fraction (`-7 / 2` is `-3`). `%` is the remainder of that division, so it has the sign of its left operand (`-7 % 2` is `-1`, `7 % -2` is `1`).
- unary `-`, which may repeat (`--5` is 5).
- a number, a variable, or an expression in parentheses (nested at most 50 deep).

Values are whole numbers from -1000000000 to 1000000000. A number literal above 1000000000, or an operator whose result is outside that range, is an error.

- `error: line K: syntax` when the line is not a statement as described above. This is decided for the whole line before anything is evaluated, so `x = 1 / 0 +` is a syntax error.
- Otherwise the expression is evaluated: both operands of an operator left operand first, then the operator. The first error met ends the statement:
  - `error: line K: undefined NAME` for a variable with no value,
  - `error: line K: divide by zero` for `/` or `%` with a zero right operand,
  - `error: line K: out of range` for a literal or a result outside the range.

K is the 1-based line number, counting every line. A script has at most 1000 lines of at most 200 characters and at most 100 variables. Input is ASCII with `\n` line ends.


LIM := 1000000000

struct Tok
    kind int
    text str
    val int

struct P
    toks List[Tok]
    pos int
    ev bool
    bad bool
    err str
    depth int
    vars Map[str, int]

fn is_digit(c char) bool
    c >= '0' and c <= '9'

fn is_alpha(c char) bool
    (c >= 'a' and c <= 'z') or (c >= 'A' and c <= 'Z') or c == '_'

# kind 1 number, 2 name, 3 operator; none on a lexical error
fn lex(line str) List[Tok]?
    cs := line.chars()
    n := cs.len()
    mut out := List[Tok]()
    mut i := 0
    while i < n
        c := cs[i]
        if c == ' '
            i += 1
        elif is_digit(c)
            mut j := i
            mut v := 0
            while j < n and is_digit(cs[j])
                if j - i >= 12
                    return none
                v = v * 10 + (cs[j].code() - 48)
                j += 1
            out.push(Tok(kind: 1, text: "", val: v))
            i = j
        elif is_alpha(c)
            mut j := i
            mut parts := List[char]()
            while j < n and (is_alpha(cs[j]) or is_digit(cs[j]))
                parts.push(cs[j])
                j += 1
            if j - i > 32
                return none
            out.push(Tok(kind: 2, text: parts.join(""), val: 0))
            i = j
        else
            nx := if i + 1 < n then cs[i + 1] else ' '
            mut op := ""
            if (c == '<' or c == '>' or c == '=' or c == '!') and nx == '='
                op = "{c}="
            elif c == '<' or c == '>' or c == '=' or c == '+' or c == '-' or c == '*' or c == '/' or c == '%' or c == '(' or c == ')'
                op = "{c}"
            else
                return none
            out.push(Tok(kind: 3, text: op, val: 0))
            i += op.len()
    out

fn P.peek(self) Tok
    if self.pos < self.toks.len()
        self.toks[self.pos]
    else
        Tok(kind: 0, text: "", val: 0)

fn P.isop(self, s str) bool
    t := self.peek()
    t.kind == 3 and t.text == s

fn P.syn(mut self)
    self.bad = true
    self.pos = self.toks.len()

fn P.fail(mut self, msg str)
    if self.ev and self.err == ""
        self.err = msg

fn P.live(self) bool
    self.ev and self.err == ""

fn P.chk(mut self, v int) int
    if v > LIM or v < -LIM
        self.fail("out of range")
    v

fn P.primary(mut self) int
    t := self.peek()
    if t.kind == 1
        self.pos += 1
        return self.chk(t.val)
    if t.kind == 2
        if t.text == "print"
            self.syn()
            return 0
        self.pos += 1
        if self.live()
            if self.vars.contains(t.text)
                return self.vars[t.text]
            self.fail("undefined {t.text}")
        return 0
    if self.isop("(")
        self.pos += 1
        self.depth += 1
        if self.depth > 50
            self.syn()
            return 0
        v := self.cmp()
        if self.isop(")")
            self.pos += 1
        else
            self.syn()
        self.depth -= 1
        return v
    self.syn()
    0

fn P.unary(mut self) int
    if self.isop("-")
        self.pos += 1
        v := self.unary()
        if self.live()
            return self.chk(-v)
        return 0
    self.primary()

fn P.term(mut self) int
    mut l := self.unary()
    while self.isop("*") or self.isop("/") or self.isop("%")
        op := self.peek().text
        self.pos += 1
        r := self.unary()
        if self.live()
            if op == "*"
                l = self.chk(l * r)
            elif r == 0
                self.fail("divide by zero")
            elif op == "/"
                l = self.chk(l / r)
            else
                l = self.chk(l % r)
    l

fn P.add(mut self) int
    mut l := self.term()
    while self.isop("+") or self.isop("-")
        op := self.peek().text
        self.pos += 1
        r := self.term()
        if self.live()
            if op == "+"
                l = self.chk(l + r)
            else
                l = self.chk(l - r)
    l

fn P.iscmp(self) bool
    self.isop("<") or self.isop("<=") or self.isop(">") or self.isop(">=") or self.isop("==") or self.isop("!=")

fn P.cmp(mut self) int
    mut l := self.add()
    if self.iscmp()
        op := self.peek().text
        self.pos += 1
        r := self.add()
        if self.live()
            b := match op
                "<" => l < r
                "<=" => l <= r
                ">" => l > r
                ">=" => l >= r
                "==" => l == r
                _ => l != r
            l = if b then 1 else 0
        if self.iscmp()
            self.syn()
    l

# returns the value; sets bad / err on the parser
fn P.expr(mut self, start int) int
    self.pos = start
    self.depth = 0
    v := self.cmp()
    if self.peek().kind != 0
        self.syn()
    v

fn main()
    if env.args().len() > 0
        io.eprint("usage: tally")
        io.exit(1)
    text := io.read_all()
    mut vars := Map[str, int]()
    mut failed := false
    mut k := 0
    for line in text.split("\n")
        k += 1
        if line.trim().is_empty() and line.chars().all(|c| c == ' ')
            continue
        if line.trim_start().starts_with("#")
            continue
        lx := lex(line)
        if lx == none
            io.eprint("error: line {k}: syntax")
            failed = true
            continue
        toks := lx else List[Tok]()
        if toks.is_empty()
            continue
        mut p := P(toks: toks, pos: 0, ev: false, bad: false, err: "", depth: 0, vars: vars)
        is_print := toks[0].kind == 2 and toks[0].text == "print"
        mut start := 0
        mut name := ""
        if is_print
            start = 1
        elif toks.len() >= 2 and toks[0].kind == 2 and toks[1].kind == 3 and toks[1].text == "="
            start = 2
            name = toks[0].text
        else
            p.bad = true
        if not p.bad
            p.expr(start)
        if p.bad
            io.eprint("error: line {k}: syntax")
            failed = true
            continue
        p.ev = true
        v := p.expr(start)
        if p.err != ""
            io.eprint("error: line {k}: {p.err}")
            failed = true
            continue
        if is_print
            print(v)
        else
            vars[name] = v
    if failed
        io.exit(2)

LIM := 1000000000

struct Tok
    kind int
    text str

struct Node
    kind int
    op str
    v int
    l int
    r int
    name str

struct Parser
    toks List[Tok]
    pos int
    nodes List[Node]

struct Ev
    nodes List[Node]
    vars Map[str, int]
    err str

fn is_digit(c char) bool
    c >= '0' and c <= '9'

fn is_alpha(c char) bool
    (c >= 'a' and c <= 'z') or (c >= 'A' and c <= 'Z') or c == '_'

fn tokenize(line str) List[Tok]?
    cs := line.chars()
    mut out := List[Tok]()
    mut i := 0
    n := cs.len()
    while i < n
        c := cs[i]
        if c == ' '
            i += 1
        elif is_digit(c)
            mut j := i
            while j < n and is_digit(cs[j])
                j += 1
            if j - i > 12
                return none
            out.push(Tok(kind: 0, text: cs.slice(i, j).join("")))
            i = j
        elif is_alpha(c)
            mut j := i
            while j < n and (is_alpha(cs[j]) or is_digit(cs[j]))
                j += 1
            if j - i > 32
                return none
            out.push(Tok(kind: 1, text: cs.slice(i, j).join("")))
            i = j
        elif c == '<' or c == '>' or c == '=' or c == '!'
            if i + 1 < n and cs[i + 1] == '='
                out.push(Tok(kind: 2, text: "{c}="))
                i += 2
            elif c == '!'
                return none
            else
                out.push(Tok(kind: 2, text: "{c}"))
                i += 1
        elif c == '+' or c == '-' or c == '*' or c == '/' or c == '%' or c == '(' or c == ')'
            out.push(Tok(kind: 2, text: "{c}"))
            i += 1
        else
            return none
    out

fn Parser.add_node(mut self, nd Node) int
    self.nodes.push(nd)
    self.nodes.len() - 1

fn Parser.is_op(self, s str) bool
    self.pos < self.toks.len() and self.toks[self.pos].kind == 2 and self.toks[self.pos].text == s

fn Parser.cmp(mut self, depth int) int
    a := self.add(depth)
    if a < 0
        return -1
    if self.pos < self.toks.len() and self.toks[self.pos].kind == 2
        t := self.toks[self.pos].text
        if t == "<" or t == "<=" or t == ">" or t == ">=" or t == "==" or t == "!="
            self.pos += 1
            b := self.add(depth)
            if b < 0
                return -1
            return self.add_node(Node(kind: 3, op: t, v: 0, l: a, r: b, name: ""))
    a

fn Parser.add(mut self, depth int) int
    mut a := self.mul(depth)
    if a < 0
        return -1
    while self.is_op("+") or self.is_op("-")
        t := self.toks[self.pos].text
        self.pos += 1
        b := self.mul(depth)
        if b < 0
            return -1
        a = self.add_node(Node(kind: 3, op: t, v: 0, l: a, r: b, name: ""))
    a

fn Parser.mul(mut self, depth int) int
    mut a := self.unary(depth)
    if a < 0
        return -1
    while self.is_op("*") or self.is_op("/") or self.is_op("%")
        t := self.toks[self.pos].text
        self.pos += 1
        b := self.unary(depth)
        if b < 0
            return -1
        a = self.add_node(Node(kind: 3, op: t, v: 0, l: a, r: b, name: ""))
    a

fn Parser.unary(mut self, depth int) int
    if self.is_op("-")
        self.pos += 1
        c := self.unary(depth)
        if c < 0
            return -1
        return self.add_node(Node(kind: 2, op: "", v: 0, l: c, r: 0, name: ""))
    self.primary(depth)

fn Parser.primary(mut self, depth int) int
    if self.pos >= self.toks.len()
        return -1
    t := self.toks[self.pos]
    if t.kind == 0
        self.pos += 1
        return self.add_node(Node(kind: 0, op: "", v: t.text.to_int() else 0, l: 0, r: 0, name: ""))
    if t.kind == 1
        if t.text == "print"
            return -1
        self.pos += 1
        return self.add_node(Node(kind: 1, op: "", v: 0, l: 0, r: 0, name: t.text))
    if t.text == "("
        if depth >= 50
            return -1
        self.pos += 1
        e := self.cmp(depth + 1)
        if e < 0
            return -1
        if not self.is_op(")")
            return -1
        self.pos += 1
        return e
    -1

        v := ev.vars.get(nd.name) else
            ev.err = "undefined {nd.name}"
            return 0
        return v

        x := eval(mut ev, nd.l)
        if ev.err != ""
            return 0
        return -x
    a := eval(mut ev, nd.l)
    if ev.err != ""
        return 0
    b := eval(mut ev, nd.r)
    if ev.err != ""
        return 0
    mut r := 0
    match nd.op
        "+" => r = a + b
        "-" => r = a - b
        "*" => r = a * b
        "/" | "%" =>
            if b == 0
                ev.err = "divide by zero"
                return 0
            if nd.op == "/"
                r = a / b
            else
                r = a % b
        "<" => r = if a < b then 1 else 0
        "<=" => r = if a <= b then 1 else 0
        ">" => r = if a > b then 1 else 0
        ">=" => r = if a >= b then 1 else 0
        "==" => r = if a == b then 1 else 0
        _ => r = if a != b then 1 else 0
    if r > LIM or r < -LIM
        ev.err = "out of range"
        return 0
    r

    if env.args().len() > 0
        io.eprint("usage: tally")
        io.exit(1)
    text := io.read_all()
    mut vars := Map[str, int]()
    mut bad := false
    mut k := 0
    for line in text.lines()
        k += 1
        if line.trim_start().starts_with("#")
            continue
        toks := tokenize(line) else
            io.eprint("error: line {k}: syntax")
            bad = true
            continue
        if toks.len() == 0
            continue
        if toks[0].kind == 2 and toks[0].text == "#"
            continue
        mut target := ""
        mut start := 0
        if toks[0].kind == 1 and toks[0].text == "print"
            start = 1
        elif toks[0].kind == 1 and toks.len() >= 2 and toks[1].kind == 2 and toks[1].text == "="
            target = toks[0].text
            start = 2
        else
            io.eprint("error: line {k}: syntax")
            bad = true
            continue
        mut p := Parser(toks: toks, pos: start, nodes: List[Node]())
        root := p.cmp(0)
        if root < 0 or p.pos != toks.len()
            io.eprint("error: line {k}: syntax")
            bad = true
            continue
        mut ev := Ev(nodes: p.nodes, vars: vars, err: "")
        v := eval(mut ev, root)
        if ev.err != ""
            io.eprint("error: line {k}: {ev.err}")
            bad = true
        elif target == ""
            print(v)
        else
            vars[target] = v
    if bad
        io.exit(2)

    name str
    l int
    r int

struct Parser
    toks List[Tok]
    nodes List[Node]
    pos int

fn lex(line str) List[Tok] ! str
    cs := line.chars()
    n := cs.len()
    mut out := List[Tok]()
    mut i := 0
    while i < n
        c := cs[i]
        if c == ' '
            i += 1
        elif c >= '0' and c <= '9'
            mut j := i
            while j < n and cs[j] >= '0' and cs[j] <= '9'
                j += 1
            if j - i > 12
                return "syntax"
            t := cs.slice(i, j).join("")
            out.push(Tok(kind: 0, text: t, val: t.to_int() else 0))
            i = j
        elif (c >= 'a' and c <= 'z') or (c >= 'A' and c <= 'Z') or c == '_'
            mut j := i
            while j < n and ((cs[j] >= 'a' and cs[j] <= 'z') or (cs[j] >= 'A' and cs[j] <= 'Z') or cs[j] == '_' or (cs[j] >= '0' and cs[j] <= '9'))
                j += 1
            if j - i > 32
                return "syntax"
            out.push(Tok(kind: 1, text: cs.slice(i, j).join(""), val: 0))
            i = j
        elif c == '<' or c == '>' or c == '=' or c == '!'
            if i + 1 < n and cs[i + 1] == '='
                out.push(Tok(kind: 2, text: "{c}=", val: 0))
                i += 2
            elif c == '!'
                return "syntax"
            else
                out.push(Tok(kind: 2, text: "{c}", val: 0))
                i += 1
        elif c == '+' or c == '-' or c == '*' or c == '/' or c == '%' or c == '(' or c == ')'
            out.push(Tok(kind: 2, text: "{c}", val: 0))
            i += 1
        else
            return "syntax"
    out

fn Parser.is_op(self, s str) bool
    self.pos < self.toks.len() and self.toks[self.pos].kind == 2 and self.toks[self.pos].text == s

fn Parser.add(mut self, nd Node) int
    self.nodes.push(nd)
    self.nodes.len() - 1

fn Parser.primary(mut self, depth int) int ! str
    if self.pos >= self.toks.len()
        return "syntax"
    t := self.toks[self.pos]
    if t.kind == 0
        self.pos += 1
        return self.add(Node(kind: 0, op: "", val: t.val, name: "", l: 0, r: 0))
    if t.kind == 1
        if t.text == "print"
            return "syntax"
        self.pos += 1
        return self.add(Node(kind: 1, op: "", val: 0, name: t.text, l: 0, r: 0))
    if t.text == "("
        if depth + 1 > 50
            return "syntax"
        self.pos += 1
        e := self.expr(depth + 1)?
        if not self.is_op(")")
            return "syntax"
        self.pos += 1
        return e
    return "syntax"

fn Parser.unary(mut self, depth int) int ! str
    if self.is_op("-")
        self.pos += 1
        e := self.unary(depth)?
        return self.add(Node(kind: 2, op: "", val: 0, name: "", l: e, r: 0))
    self.primary(depth)

fn Parser.mul(mut self, depth int) int ! str
    mut l := self.unary(depth)?
    while self.is_op("*") or self.is_op("/") or self.is_op("%")
        op := self.toks[self.pos].text
        self.pos += 1
        r := self.unary(depth)?
        l = self.add(Node(kind: 3, op: op, val: 0, name: "", l: l, r: r))
    l

fn Parser.sum(mut self, depth int) int ! str
    mut l := self.mul(depth)?
    while self.is_op("+") or self.is_op("-")
        op := self.toks[self.pos].text
        self.pos += 1
        r := self.mul(depth)?
        l = self.add(Node(kind: 3, op: op, val: 0, name: "", l: l, r: r))
    l

fn Parser.expr(mut self, depth int) int ! str
    l := self.sum(depth)?
    if self.is_op("<") or self.is_op("<=") or self.is_op(">") or self.is_op(">=") or self.is_op("==") or self.is_op("!=")
        op := self.toks[self.pos].text
        self.pos += 1
        r := self.sum(depth)?
        return self.add(Node(kind: 3, op: op, val: 0, name: "", l: l, r: r))
    l

fn chk(v int) int ! str
    if v > 1000000000 or v < -1000000000
        return "out of range"
    v

fn eval(p Parser, i int, vars Map[str, int]) int ! str
    nd := p.nodes[i]
    if nd.kind == 0
        return chk(nd.val)?
    if nd.kind == 1
        if not vars.contains(nd.name)
            return "undefined {nd.name}"
        return vars[nd.name]
    if nd.kind == 2
        a := eval(p, nd.l, vars)?
        return -a
    a := eval(p, nd.l, vars)?
    b := eval(p, nd.r, vars)?
    r := match nd.op
        "+" => a + b
        "-" => a - b
        "*" => a * b
        "/" => 0
        "%" => 0
        "<" => if a < b then 1 else 0
        "<=" => if a <= b then 1 else 0
        ">" => if a > b then 1 else 0
        ">=" => if a >= b then 1 else 0
        "==" => if a == b then 1 else 0
        _ => if a != b then 1 else 0
    if nd.op == "/" or nd.op == "%"
        if b == 0
            return "divide by zero"
        if nd.op == "/"
            return chk(a / b)?
        return chk(a % b)?
    chk(r)?

fn run_line(line str, mut vars Map[str, int]) int ! str
    toks := lex(line)?
    if toks.is_empty()
        return 0
    mut p := Parser(toks: toks, nodes: List[Node](), pos: 0)
    is_print := toks[0].kind == 1 and toks[0].text == "print"
    mut target := ""
    if is_print
        p.pos = 1
    elif toks[0].kind == 1 and toks.len() > 1 and toks[1].kind == 2 and toks[1].text == "="
        target = toks[0].text
        p.pos = 2
    else
        return "syntax"
    root := p.expr(0)?
    if p.pos != toks.len()
        return "syntax"
    v := eval(p, root, vars)?
    if is_print
        print(v)
    else
        vars[target] = v
    0

fn main() !
    args := env.args()
    if args.len() > 0
        io.eprint("usage: tally")
        io.exit(1)
    text := io.read_all()
    mut vars := Map[str, int]()
    mut bad := false
    mut k := 0
    for line in text.split("\n")
        k += 1
        t := lstrip(line)
        if t.is_empty() or t.starts_with("#")
            continue
        _ := run_line(line, mut vars) else e
            io.eprint("error: line {k}: {e}")
            bad = true
            continue
    if bad
        io.exit(2)

fn lstrip(s str) str
    cs := s.chars()
    mut i := 0
    while i < cs.len() and cs[i] == ' '
        i += 1
    cs.slice(i).join("")

# tally

Write `tally`, a command-line program. It reads a script from stdin, one statement per line, and runs the statements in order.

Statements:
- `NAME = EXPR` evaluates EXPR and stores the value in the variable NAME.
- `print EXPR` evaluates EXPR and prints the value in decimal on its own line on stdout.
- A line that is empty, has only spaces, or whose first character after any leading spaces is `#` is ignored.

Tokens: a number is one or more digits (at most 12). A name is a letter or `_` followed by letters, digits and `_` (at most 32 characters). `print` is a keyword and never a variable. The operators are `+ - * / % ( ) = < <= > >= == !=`. Spaces may appear before, between and after tokens and are needed only between two tokens that would otherwise read as one. Any other character makes the line a syntax error.

Expressions, loosest binding first:
- one comparison at most: `A < B`, with `< <= > >= == !=`; the value is 1 when it holds, else 0. `1 < 2 < 3` is a syntax error; `(1 < 2) < 3` is fine.
- `+` and `-`, left to right.
- `*`, `/` and `%`, left to right. `/` drops the fraction (`-7 / 2` is `-3`). `%` is the remainder of that division, so it has the sign of its left operand (`-7 % 2` is `-1`, `7 % -2` is `1`).
- unary `-`, which may repeat (`--5` is 5).
- a number, a variable, or an expression in parentheses (nested at most 50 deep).

Values are whole numbers from -1000000000 to 1000000000. A number literal above 1000000000, or an operator whose result is outside that range, is an error.

Errors. Each is one line on stderr, and the statement has no other effect: nothing is printed and the variable keeps its old value, or stays undefined.
- `error: line K: syntax` when the line is not a statement as described above. This is decided for the whole line before anything is evaluated, so `x = 1 / 0 +` is a syntax error.
- Otherwise the expression is evaluated: both operands of an operator left operand first, then the operator. The first error met ends the statement:
  - `error: line K: undefined NAME` for a variable with no value,
  - `error: line K: divide by zero` for `/` or `%` with a zero right operand,
  - `error: line K: out of range` for a literal or a result outside the range.
  So `nope + 1 / 0` reports `undefined nope` and `1 / 0 + nope` reports `divide by zero`.

K is the 1-based line number, counting every line. A script has at most 1000 lines of at most 200 characters and at most 100 variables. Input is ASCII with `\n` line ends.

`tally` takes no arguments. With any argument it prints `usage: tally` on stderr and exits 1 without reading stdin. Otherwise the exit code is 2 if any line was an error, else 0.

Both stdout and stderr are checked.

Example:

```
x = 2 + 3 * 4
print x
print (x - 4) / -3
y = x / 0
print y
print x >= 14
```

prints `14`, `-3` and `1` on stdout, and on stderr `error: line 4: divide by zero` then `error: line 5: undefined y`; the exit code is 2.

struct Tok
    kind int
    text str

struct Node
    kind int
    op str
    name str
    val int
    l int
    r int

struct P
    toks List[Tok]
    pos int
    depth int
    nodes List[Node]

fn is_digit(c char) bool
    c >= '0' and c <= '9'

fn is_alpha(c char) bool
    (c >= 'a' and c <= 'z') or (c >= 'A' and c <= 'Z') or c == '_'

fn is_cmp(s str) bool
    s == "<" or s == "<=" or s == ">" or s == ">=" or s == "==" or s == "!="

fn tokenize(line str) List[Tok] ! str
    cs := line.chars()
    n := cs.len()
    mut toks := List[Tok]()
    mut i := 0
    while i < n
        c := cs[i]
        if c == ' '
            i += 1
        elif is_digit(c)
            mut j := i
            while j < n and is_digit(cs[j])
                j += 1
            if j - i > 12
                return "syntax"
            toks.push(Tok(kind: 0, text: cs.slice(i, j).join("")))
            i = j
        elif is_alpha(c)
            mut j := i
            while j < n and (is_alpha(cs[j]) or is_digit(cs[j]))
                j += 1
            if j - i > 32
                return "syntax"
            toks.push(Tok(kind: 1, text: cs.slice(i, j).join("")))
            i = j
        else
            two := if i + 1 < n then "{c}{cs[i + 1]}" else ""
            if two == "<=" or two == ">=" or two == "==" or two == "!="
                toks.push(Tok(kind: 2, text: two))
                i += 2
            elif "+-*/%()=<>".contains(c)
                toks.push(Tok(kind: 2, text: "{c}"))
                i += 1
            else
                return "syntax"
    toks.push(Tok(kind: 3, text: ""))
    toks

fn mk(kind int, op str, name str, val int, l int, r int) Node
    Node(kind: kind, op: op, name: name, val: val, l: l, r: r)

fn P.peek(self) Tok
    self.toks[self.pos]

fn P.add(mut self, n Node) int
    self.nodes.push(n)
    self.nodes.len() - 1

fn P.atom(mut self) int ! str
    t := self.peek()
    if t.kind == 0
        self.pos += 1
        return self.add(mk(0, "", "", t.text.to_int() else 0, 0, 0))
    if t.kind == 1
        if t.text == "print"
            return "syntax"
        self.pos += 1
        return self.add(mk(1, "", t.text, 0, 0, 0))
    if t.kind == 2 and t.text == "("
        self.pos += 1
        self.depth += 1
        if self.depth > 50
            return "syntax"
        e := self.expr()?
        c := self.peek()
        if not (c.kind == 2 and c.text == ")")
            return "syntax"
        self.pos += 1
        self.depth -= 1
        return e
    return "syntax"

fn P.unary(mut self) int ! str
    t := self.peek()
    if t.kind == 2 and t.text == "-"
        self.pos += 1
        e := self.unary()?
        return self.add(mk(2, "-", "", 0, e, 0))
    self.atom()

fn P.mul(mut self) int ! str
    mut l := self.unary()?
    while true
        t := self.peek()
        if t.kind == 2 and (t.text == "*" or t.text == "/" or t.text == "%")
            self.pos += 1
            r := self.unary()?
            l = self.add(mk(3, t.text, "", 0, l, r))
        else
            break
    l

fn P.addx(mut self) int ! str
    mut l := self.mul()?
    while true
        t := self.peek()
        if t.kind == 2 and (t.text == "+" or t.text == "-")
            self.pos += 1
            r := self.mul()?
            l = self.add(mk(3, t.text, "", 0, l, r))
        else
            break
    l

fn P.expr(mut self) int ! str
    l := self.addx()?
    t := self.peek()
    if t.kind == 2 and is_cmp(t.text)
        self.pos += 1
        r := self.addx()?
        n := self.add(mk(3, t.text, "", 0, l, r))
        u := self.peek()
        if u.kind == 2 and is_cmp(u.text)
            return "syntax"
        return n
    l

fn chk(v int) int ! str
    if v > 1000000000 or v < -1000000000
        return "out of range"
    v

fn eval(nodes List[Node], i int, vars Map[str, int]) int ! str
    nd := nodes[i]
    if nd.kind == 0
        return chk(nd.val)
    if nd.kind == 1
        return vars.get(nd.name) else return "undefined {nd.name}"
    if nd.kind == 2
        v := eval(nodes, nd.l, vars)?
        return -v
    a := eval(nodes, nd.l, vars)?
    b := eval(nodes, nd.r, vars)?
    r := match nd.op
        "+" => a + b
        "-" => a - b
        "*" => a * b
        "/" => 0
        "%" => 0
        "<" => if a < b then 1 else 0
        "<=" => if a <= b then 1 else 0
        ">" => if a > b then 1 else 0
        ">=" => if a >= b then 1 else 0
        "==" => if a == b then 1 else 0
        _ => if a != b then 1 else 0
    if nd.op == "/" or nd.op == "%"
        if b == 0
            return "divide by zero"
        q := a / b
        if nd.op == "/"
            return chk(q)
        return chk(a - q * b)
    chk(r)

fn run(line str, mut vars Map[str, int]) int ! str
    toks := tokenize(line)?
    mut p := P(toks: toks, pos: 0, depth: 0, nodes: List[Node]())
    first := toks[0]
    mut target := ""
    if first.kind == 1 and first.text == "print"
        p.pos = 1
    elif first.kind == 1 and toks.len() > 1 and toks[1].kind == 2 and toks[1].text == "="
        target = first.text
        p.pos = 2
    else
        return "syntax"
    root := p.expr()?
    if p.peek().kind != 3
        return "syntax"
    v := eval(p.nodes, root, vars)?
    if target == ""
        print(v)
    else
        vars[target] = v
    0

fn main()
    if env.args().len() > 0
        io.eprint("usage: tally")
        io.exit(1)
    text := io.read_all()
    mut vars := Map[str, int]()
    mut bad := false
    mut k := 0
    for line in text.split("\n")
        k += 1
        t := line.trim_start()
        if t == "" or t.starts_with("#")
            continue
        _ := run(line, mut vars) else e
            io.eprint("error: line {k}: {e}")
            bad = true
            0
    if bad
        io.exit(2)

struct Tok
    kind int
    text str

struct Pool
    kind List[int]
    val List[int]
    text List[str]
    a List[int]
    b List[int]

fn Pool.add(mut self, kind int, val int, text str, a int, b int) int
    self.kind.push(kind)
    self.val.push(val)
    self.text.push(text)
    self.a.push(a)
    self.b.push(b)
    self.kind.len() - 1

struct Parser
    toks List[Tok]
    pos int
    depth int
    pool Pool

fn is_digit(c char) bool
    c >= '0' and c <= '9'

fn is_alpha(c char) bool
    (c >= 'a' and c <= 'z') or (c >= 'A' and c <= 'Z') or c == '_'

fn tokenize(line str) List[Tok] ! str
    cs := line.chars()
    n := cs.len()
    mut toks := List[Tok]()
    mut i := 0
    while i < n
        c := cs[i]
        if c == ' '
            i += 1
        elif is_digit(c)
            mut j := i
            while j < n and is_digit(cs[j])
                j += 1
            if j - i > 12
                return "syntax"
            toks.push(Tok(kind: 0, text: cs.slice(i, j).join("")))
            i = j
        elif is_alpha(c)
            mut j := i
            while j < n and (is_alpha(cs[j]) or is_digit(cs[j]))
                j += 1
            if j - i > 32
                return "syntax"
            toks.push(Tok(kind: 1, text: cs.slice(i, j).join("")))
            i = j
        elif c == '<' or c == '>' or c == '=' or c == '!'
            if i + 1 < n and cs[i + 1] == '='
                toks.push(Tok(kind: 2, text: "{c}="))
                i += 2
            elif c == '!'
                return "syntax"
            else
                toks.push(Tok(kind: 2, text: "{c}"))
                i += 1
        elif c == '+' or c == '-' or c == '*' or c == '/' or c == '%' or c == '(' or c == ')'
            toks.push(Tok(kind: 2, text: "{c}"))
            i += 1
        else
            return "syntax"
    toks

fn Parser.peek_op(self, op str) bool
    self.pos < self.toks.len() and self.toks[self.pos].kind == 2 and self.toks[self.pos].text == op

fn Parser.primary(mut self) int ! str
    if self.pos >= self.toks.len()
        return "syntax"
    t := self.toks[self.pos]
    if t.kind == 0
        self.pos += 1
        return self.pool.add(0, t.text.to_int() else 0, "", 0, 0)
    if t.kind == 1
        if t.text == "print"
            return "syntax"
        self.pos += 1
        return self.pool.add(1, 0, t.text, 0, 0)
    if t.text == "("
        self.pos += 1
        self.depth += 1
        if self.depth > 50
            return "syntax"
        e := self.cmp()?
        if not self.peek_op(")")

        self.pos += 1
        self.depth -= 1

        e := self.unary()?

    while self.peek_op("*") or self.peek_op("/") or self.peek_op("%")
        op := self.toks[self.pos].text
        self.pos += 1
        r := self.unary()?
        l = self.pool.add(3, 0, op, l, r)
    l

fn Parser.sum(mut self) int ! str
    mut l := self.term()?
    while self.peek_op("+") or self.peek_op("-")
        op := self.toks[self.pos].text
        self.pos += 1
        r := self.term()?
        l = self.pool.add(3, 0, op, l, r)
    l

# wrap

Write `wrap`, a command-line program. It reads plain text from stdin and prints it reflowed.

Input: lines of text. A word is a run of characters other than the space. A blank line is one that is empty or has only spaces. A paragraph is a run of consecutive lines that are not blank; its words are the words of its lines, in order. Blank lines only separate paragraphs.

Commands (arguments), output on stdout:

- `fill W`: each paragraph is laid out again. Words are put on a line one after another with one space between them, and a new line is started whenever the next word would make the line longer than W characters. A word longer than W stands alone on its line, unbroken. Lines have no leading or trailing spaces. Between two paragraphs there is exactly one empty line; there is none before the first or after the last.
- `justify W`: the same lines as `fill W`, then every line except the last line of each paragraph is widened to exactly W characters by adding spaces between its words. If the line has G gaps and needs E more spaces, every gap gets E / G of them (rounded down) and the first E % G gaps from the left get one more. A line with one word is left as it is.
- `center W`: the same lines as `fill W`, each with (W - L) / 2 spaces (rounded down) put before it, where L is the line's length; a line with L >= W gets none. No trailing spaces.
- `stats`: three lines, `paragraphs P`, `words N` and `longest M`, where M is the length of the longest word (0 when there are no words).

W is 1 to 3 digits with a value from 1 to 200.

```
fox jumps over

Second
paragraph, here.
```

    if s.is_empty() or s.len() > 3
        usage()
    for c in s.chars()
        if c < '0' or c > '9'
            usage()
    n := s.to_int() else usage()
    if n < 1 or n > 200
        usage()
    n

fn layout(words List[str], w int) List[List[str]]
    mut lines := List[List[str]]()

            curlen = word.len()
        elif curlen + 1 + word.len() > w
            lines.push(cur)

        else
            cur.push(word)
            curlen += 1 + word.len()

        lines.push(cur)

    if ws.len() == 1
        return ws[0]
    total := ws.fold(0, |acc, x| acc + x.len())
    gaps := ws.len() - 1
    e := w - total - gaps
    base := 1 + e / gaps
    extra := e % gaps

    mut paras := List[List[str]]()
    mut cur := List[str]()
    for line in text.split("\n")
        ws := line.split(" ").filter(|x| not x.is_empty())
        if ws.is_empty()
            if not cur.is_empty()
                paras.push(cur)
                cur = List[str]()
        else
            cur.extend(ws)
    if not cur.is_empty()
        paras.push(cur)

        mut n := 0
        mut longest := 0
        for p in paras
            n += p.len()
            for x in p
                if x.len() > longest
                    longest = x.len()
        print("paragraphs {paras.len()}")
        print("words {n}")
        print("longest {longest}")

    mut first := true
    for p in paras
        if not first
            out.push("")

                else

# depgraph

Write `depgraph`, a command-line program. It reads a dependency list from stdin and answers one question about it.

Input, one item per line:
- `A -> B` means A needs B.
- `A` alone declares a node with no dependencies yet.
- An empty line or a line starting with `#` is ignored.
- A name is one or more of `a-z A-Z 0-9 _ . -`. The separator is exactly one space, `->`, one space. Any other line (extra or missing spaces, a third name, an illegal character, a carriage return) is bad: skip it and print `error: line K: bad line` to stderr (K is 1-based). Repeated edges count once. `A -> A` is a self-dependency. There are at most 500 distinct names.

Commands (first argument), output on stdout, one name per line:
- `order`: every node, dependencies first. Among nodes ready at the same time, the smallest name in byte order comes first.
- `cycles`: every node that lies on a cycle (reaches itself through one or more edges), in ascending byte order.
- `deps NAME`: everything NAME needs, directly or not, ascending. NAME itself appears only if it lies on a cycle.
- `rdeps NAME`: everything that needs NAME, directly or not, ascending, under the same rule.

Exit codes, first that applies wins: 1 for a missing, unknown or malformed command, including a wrong number of arguments and a NAME argument that is not a valid name by the rule above (print `usage: depgraph order|cycles|deps NAME|rdeps NAME` to stderr, do not read stdin); 4 if `deps`/`rdeps` names a node that is not in the input (print `error: unknown ` and the name to stderr, e.g. `error: unknown lib`, nothing on stdout); 3 if `order` finds a cycle (print `error: cycle` to stderr, nothing on stdout); 2 if any line was bad (stdout is still printed); else 0.

fn usage() never
    io.eprint("usage: depgraph order|cycles|deps NAME|rdeps NAME")
    io.exit(1)

fn valid(s str) bool
    if s.is_empty()
        return false
    for c in s.chars()
        ok := match c
            'a'..='z' => true
            'A'..='Z' => true
            '0'..='9' => true
            '_' | '.' | '-' => true
            _ => false
        if not ok
            return false
    true

fn reach(adj List[List[int]], s int) Set[int]
    mut seen := Set[int]()
    mut stack := List[int]()
    for n in adj[s]
        stack.push(n)
    while top := stack.pop()
        if seen.add(top)
            for n in adj[top]
                stack.push(n)
    seen

fn main()
    args := env.args()
    if args.len() == 0
        usage()
    cmd := args[0]
    if cmd == "order" or cmd == "cycles"
        if args.len() != 1
            usage()
    elif cmd == "deps" or cmd == "rdeps"
        if args.len() != 2 or not valid(args[1])
            usage()
    else
        usage()

    text := io.read_all()
    mut names := List[str]()
    mut idx := Map[str, int]()
    mut adj := List[List[int]]()
    mut radj := List[List[int]]()
    mut edges := Set[str]()
    mut bad := false
    mut lineno := 0
    for line in text.split("\n")
        lineno += 1
        if line.is_empty() or line.starts_with("#")
            continue
        parts := line.split(" -> ")
        mut ok := false
        if parts.len() == 1
            ok = valid(parts[0])
        elif parts.len() == 2
            ok = valid(parts[0]) and valid(parts[1])
        if not ok
            io.eprint("error: line {lineno}: bad line")
            bad = true
            continue
        mut ids := List[int]()
        for p in parts
            if not idx.contains(p)
                idx[p] = names.len()
                names.push(p)
                adj.push(List[int]())
                radj.push(List[int]())
            ids.push(idx[p])
        if ids.len() == 2
            if edges.add("{parts[0]} -> {parts[1]}")
                adj[ids[0]].push(ids[1])
                radj[ids[1]].push(ids[0])
    n := names.len()

    if cmd == "order"
        mut need := [adj[i].len() for i in 0..n]
        mut done := [false for i in 0..n]
        mut out := List[str]()
        for step in 0..n
            mut best := -1
            for i in 0..n
                if not done[i] and need[i] == 0
                    if best < 0 or names[i] < names[best]
                        best = i
            if best < 0
                io.eprint("error: cycle")
                io.exit(3)
            done[best] = true
            out.push(names[best])
            for a in radj[best]
                need[a] -= 1
        for s in out
            print(s)
    elif cmd == "cycles"
        mut out := List[str]()

fn usage() never
    io.eprint("usage: ledger balance|top N|monthly")

fn money(b bigint.BigInt) str
    neg := b < bigint.from_int(0)
    a := if neg then -b else b
    s := "{a}".pad_left(3, '0')
    n := s.len()
    body := "{s.slice(0, n - 2)}.{s.slice(n - 2)}"
    if neg
        "-{body}"
    else
        body

fn all_digits(s str) bool
    if s.is_empty()
        return false
    for c in s.chars()
        if c < '0' or c > '9'
            return false
    true

fn valid_date(d str) bool
    if d.len() != 10
        return false
    if d.slice(4, 5) != "-" or d.slice(7, 8) != "-"
        return false
    y := d.slice(0, 4)
    m := d.slice(5, 7)
    day := d.slice(8, 10)

    elif cmd == "monthly"

fn usage() never
    io.eprint("usage: ledger balance|top N|monthly")
    io.exit(1)

fn money(s str) str
    neg := s.starts_with("-")
    d := (s.strip_prefix("-") else s).pad_left(3, '0')
    n := d.len()
    body := "{d.slice(0, n - 2)}.{d.slice(n - 2)}"
    if neg
        "-{body}"
    else
        body

fn digits(s str) bool
    s.chars().all(|c| c >= '0' and c <= '9')

fn valid_date(d str) bool
    if d.len() != 10
        return false
    if d.char_at(4) != '-' or d.char_at(7) != '-'
        return false
    y := d.slice(0, 4)
    m := d.slice(5, 7)
    dd := d.slice(8, 10)
    if not (digits(y) and digits(m) and digits(dd))
        return false
    mi := m.to_int() else 0
    di := dd.to_int() else 0
    mi >= 1 and mi <= 12 and di >= 1 and di <= 31

fn main()
    args := env.args()
    if args.len() == 0
        usage()
    cmd := args[0]
    mut topn := 0
    if cmd == "top"
        if args.len() != 2

        topn = args[1].to_int() else usage()
        if topn < 0
            usage()

        usage()

    mut lines := text.split("\n")
    if lines.len() > 1 and lines[lines.len() - 1] == ""
        lines.pop()
    if lines[0] != "date,account,amount_cents,memo"
        io.eprint("error: line 1: bad header")
        io.exit(2)

    mut bad := false
    for i in 1..lines.len()
        parts := lines[i].split(",")
        mut why := ""
        if parts.len() != 4
            why = "expected 4 fields"
        elif not valid_date(parts[0])
            why = "bad date"
        elif parts[1] == ""
            why = "empty account"
        else
            a := parts[2].to_int()
            if a == none
                why = "bad amount"
            else
                txs.push(Tx(date: parts[0], account: parts[1], amount: a else 0, memo: parts[3]))
        if why != ""
            bad = true
            io.eprint("error: line {i + 1}: {why}")
    if cmd == "top"
        sorted := txs.sorted(by: |t| if t.amount < 0 then t.amount else -t.amount)
        for t in sorted.take(topn)
            print("{t.date}\t{t.account}\t{money("{t.amount}")}\t{t.memo}")

        for t in txs
            k := if cmd == "balance" then t.account else t.date.slice(0, 7)

fn usage() never
    io.eprint("usage: ledger balance|top N|monthly")
    io.exit(1)

fn money(b bigint.BigInt) str
    s := "{b}"
    neg := s.starts_with("-")
    digits := if neg then s.slice(1) else s
    p := digits.pad_left(3, '0')
    n := p.len()
    body := "{p.slice(0, n - 2)}.{p.slice(n - 2)}"
    if neg then "-{body}" else body

fn all_digits(s str) bool
    s.chars().all(|c| c >= '0' and c <= '9')

fn check_date(d str) str?
    if d.len() != 10
        return "bad date"
    y := d.slice(0, 4)
    m := d.slice(5, 7)
    dd := d.slice(8, 10)
    if d.slice(4, 5) != "-" or d.slice(7, 8) != "-"
        return "bad date"
    if not (all_digits(y) and all_digits(m) and all_digits(dd))
        return "bad date"
    mi := m.to_int() else 0
    di := dd.to_int() else 0
    if mi < 1 or mi > 12 or di < 1 or di > 31
        return "bad date"
    none

fn main()

    if args.len() == 0
        usage()
    cmd := args[0]
    mut topn := 0

        io.eprint("error: line 1: bad header")
        io.exit(2)

            if r != none

                why = "empty account"
            elif parts[2].to_int() == none
                why = "bad amount"

            continue

        k := if a < 0 then -(a + 1) else a - 1
        txs.push(Tx(date: parts[0], account: parts[1], amount: a, memo: parts[3], key: k))

        mut m := Map[str, bigint.BigInt]()
        for t in txs
            m[t.account] = (m.get(t.account) else bigint.from_int(0)) + bigint.from_int(t.amount)
        for k in m.keys().sorted()

    elif cmd == "monthly"

# stock

`stock` is a command-line program that reads a stock log on stdin and prints a report about it.

Input: one event per line. Fields are separated by exactly one space.
- `receive SKU QTY PRICE`: QTY units arrive, each costing PRICE cents.
- `ship SKU QTY`: QTY units leave.
- `count SKU QTY`: a stocktake found QTY units on hand.

SKU is one or more of `A-Z 0-9 -`. QTY and PRICE are 1 to 5 digits (`0-9`, no sign). QTY must be at least 1 for `receive` and `ship`, and may be 0 for `count`. An empty line or a line starting with `#` is ignored, but still counts for line numbers. A trailing newline at the end of input is not an extra line. A carriage return is part of the line, so a line ending in `\r` (a Windows line ending) is not a valid event.

Each SKU has an on-hand quantity and a cost (total cents), both starting at 0 the first time the SKU is received:
- `receive` adds QTY to the quantity and QTY × PRICE to the cost.
- `ship` removes QTY units at their average cost: the cost falls by `cost × QTY / quantity` (integer division, rounded down), then the quantity falls by QTY.
- `count` sets the quantity to QTY. If the old quantity was above 0, the cost becomes `cost × QTY / old quantity` (rounded down); otherwise the cost is unchanged.

A line that breaks a rule is skipped, and one line goes to stderr, where K is the 1-based line number:
- `error: line K: bad line` for a line that is not a valid event;
- `error: line K: unknown ` and the SKU itself, for `ship` or `count` of a SKU never received: `error: line 3: unknown AB-1`;
- `error: line K: short ` and the SKU itself, for `ship` of more units than are on hand: `error: line 4: short AB-1`.

The word `SKU` never appears in these lines; it stands for the SKU's own text.

Nothing else is printed to stderr, apart from the usage line below.

Commands (first argument), output on stdout:
- `report`: one line per SKU ever received, `SKU<TAB>QUANTITY<TAB>VALUE`, SKUs in ascending byte order. VALUE is the cost.
- `low N`: every SKU ever received whose quantity is below N, one per line, ascending. N is 1 to 5 digits.
- `total`: one line, the sum of every SKU's cost.

Money prints cents as dollars with exactly two decimals and a leading `-` for negatives: `1234.05`, `0.50`, `0.00`.

Exit codes: 1 for a missing, unknown or malformed command, including a wrong number of arguments and an `N` that is not 1 to 5 digits (print `usage: stock report|low N|total` to stderr; do not read stdin); 2 if any line was skipped (stdout is still printed); else 0.

    cost int

fn usage() never
    io.eprint("usage: stock report|low N|total")
    io.exit(1)

fn digits(s str, lo int) int?
    if s.len() < 1 or s.len() > 5
        return none
    for c in s.chars()
        if c < '0' or c > '9'
            return none
    n := s.to_int() else return none
    if n < lo
        return none
    n

fn sku_ok(s str) bool
    if s.is_empty()
        return false
    for c in s.chars()
        ok := (c >= 'A' and c <= 'Z') or (c >= '0' and c <= '9') or c == '-'
        if not ok
            return false
    true

    sign := if c < 0 then "-" else ""
    a := if c < 0 then 0 - c else c
    "{sign}{a / 100}.{"{a % 100}".pad_left(2, '0')}"

        usage()
    cmd := args[0]

    elif cmd == "low"

    else

        f := line.split(" ")
        kind := f[0]
        mut good := false
        if kind == "receive" and f.len() == 4
            good = sku_ok(f[1]) and digits(f[2], 1) != none and digits(f[3], 0) != none
        elif kind == "ship" and f.len() == 3
            good = sku_ok(f[1]) and digits(f[2], 1) != none
        elif kind == "count" and f.len() == 3
            good = sku_ok(f[1]) and digits(f[2], 0) != none
        if not good
            io.eprint("error: line {k}: bad line")
            bad = true
            continue
        sku := f[1]
        qty := digits(f[2], 0) else 0
        if kind == "receive"
            price := digits(f[3], 0) else 0
            old := items.get(sku) else Item(qty: 0, cost: 0)
            items[sku] = Item(qty: old.qty + qty, cost: old.cost + qty * price)
        elif not items.contains(sku)
            io.eprint("error: line {k}: unknown {sku}")
            bad = true
        else
            old := items[sku]
            if kind == "ship"
                if qty > old.qty
                    io.eprint("error: line {k}: short {sku}")
                    bad = true
                else
                    items[sku] = Item(qty: old.qty - qty, cost: old.cost - old.cost * qty / old.qty)
            else
                nc := if old.qty > 0 then old.cost * qty / old.qty else old.cost
                items[sku] = Item(qty: qty, cost: nc)
    if cmd == "report"
        for s in items.keys().sorted()
            it := items[s]
            print("{s}\t{it.qty}\t{money(it.cost)}")
    elif cmd == "low"
        for s in items.keys().sorted()
            if items[s].qty < limit
                print(s)
    else
        mut t := 0
        for s in items.keys()
            t += items[s].cost
        print(money(t))
    if bad
        io.exit(2)

Input: one event per line. Fields are separated by exactly one space.
- `receive SKU QTY PRICE`: QTY units arrive, each costing PRICE cents.
- `ship SKU QTY`: QTY units leave.
- `count SKU QTY`: a stocktake found QTY units on hand.

SKU is one or more of `A-Z 0-9 -`. QTY and PRICE are 1 to 5 digits (`0-9`, no sign). QTY must be at least 1 for `receive` and `ship`, and may be 0 for `count`. An empty line or a line starting with `#` is ignored, but still counts for line numbers. A trailing newline at the end of input is not an extra line. A carriage return is part of the line, so a line ending in `\r` (a Windows line ending) is not a valid event.

Each SKU has an on-hand quantity and a cost (total cents), both starting at 0 the first time the SKU is received:
- `receive` adds QTY to the quantity and QTY × PRICE to the cost.
- `ship` removes QTY units at their average cost: the cost falls by `cost × QTY / quantity` (integer division, rounded down), then the quantity falls by QTY.
- `count` sets the quantity to QTY. If the old quantity was above 0, the cost becomes `cost × QTY / old quantity` (rounded down); otherwise the cost is unchanged.

A line that breaks a rule is skipped, and one line goes to stderr, where K is the 1-based line number:
- `error: line K: bad line` for a line that is not a valid event;
- `error: line K: unknown ` and the SKU itself, for `ship` or `count` of a SKU never received: `error: line 3: unknown AB-1`;
- `error: line K: short ` and the SKU itself, for `ship` of more units than are on hand: `error: line 4: short AB-1`.

The word `SKU` never appears in these lines; it stands for the SKU's own text.

Nothing else is printed to stderr, apart from the usage line below.

Commands (first argument), output on stdout:
- `report`: one line per SKU ever received, `SKU<TAB>QUANTITY<TAB>VALUE`, SKUs in ascending byte order. VALUE is the cost.
- `low N`: every SKU ever received whose quantity is below N, one per line, ascending. N is 1 to 5 digits.
- `total`: one line, the sum of every SKU's cost.

Money prints cents as dollars with exactly two decimals and a leading `-` for negatives: `1234.05`, `0.50`, `0.00`.

Exit codes: 1 for a missing, unknown or malformed command, including a wrong number of arguments and an `N` that is not 1 to 5 digits (print `usage: stock report|low N|total` to stderr; do not read stdin); 2 if any line was skipped (stdout is still printed); else 0.

Layout: the program lives in `src/`; `./build` builds `./stock`; `./test` runs the visible cases.

struct Item
    qty int
    cost int

fn usage() never
    io.eprint("usage: stock report|low N|total")
    io.exit(1)

fn digits(s str, max int) bool
    if s.len() < 1 or s.len() > max
        return false
    for c in s.chars()
        if c < '0' or c > '9'
            return false
    true

fn sku_ok(s str) bool
    if s.len() < 1
        return false
    for c in s.chars()
        if not ((c >= 'A' and c <= 'Z') or (c >= '0' and c <= '9') or c == '-')
            return false
    true

fn pad2(n int) str
    if n < 10 then "0{n}" else "{n}"

fn money(c int) str
    neg := c < 0
    a := if neg then 0 - c else c
    d := a / 100
    r := a % 100
    s := "{d}.{pad2(r)}"
    if neg then "-{s}" else s

fn bad(k int)
    io.eprint("error: line {k}: bad line")

fn main()
    args := env.args()
    mut cmd := 0
    mut lim := 0
    if args.len() == 1 and args[0] == "report"
        cmd = 0
    elif args.len() == 1 and args[0] == "total"
        cmd = 2
    elif args.len() == 2 and args[0] == "low" and digits(args[1], 5)
        cmd = 1
        lim = args[1].to_int() else 0
    else
        usage()
    text := io.read_all()
    mut lines := text.split("\n")
    if text.ends_with("\n") or text == ""
        lines.pop()
    mut items := Map[str, Item]()
    mut skipped := false
    mut k := 0
    for line in lines
        k += 1
        if line == "" or line.starts_with("#")
            continue
        f := line.split(" ")
        kind := f[0]
        n := f.len()
        ok := if kind == "receive" then n == 4 elif kind == "ship" or kind == "count" then n == 3 else false
        if not ok or not sku_ok(f[1]) or not digits(f[2], 5) or (n == 4 and not digits(f[3], 5))
            bad(k)
            skipped = true
            continue
        sku := f[1]
        q := f[2].to_int() else 0
        if q < 1 and kind != "count"
            bad(k)
            skipped = true
            continue
        if kind == "receive"
            p := f[3].to_int() else 0
            it := items.get(sku) else Item(qty: 0, cost: 0)
            items[sku] = Item(qty: it.qty + q, cost: it.cost + q * p)
            continue
        if not items.contains(sku)
            io.eprint("error: line {k}: unknown {sku}")
            skipped = true
            continue
        it := items[sku]
        if kind == "ship"
            if q > it.qty
                io.eprint("error: line {k}: short {sku}")
                skipped = true
                continue
            c := (bigint.from_int(it.cost) * bigint.from_int(q) / bigint.from_int(it.qty)).as_int() else 0
            items[sku] = Item(qty: it.qty - q, cost: it.cost - c)
        else
            mut c := it.cost
            if it.qty > 0
                c = (bigint.from_int(it.cost) * bigint.from_int(q) / bigint.from_int(it.qty)).as_int() else 0
            items[sku] = Item(qty: q, cost: c)
    keys := items.keys().sorted()
    mut total := 0
    for s in keys
        it := items[s]
        total += it.cost
        if cmd == 0
            print("{s}\t{it.qty}\t{money(it.cost)}")
        elif cmd == 1 and it.qty < lim
            print(s)
    if cmd == 2
        print(money(total))
    if skipped
        io.exit(2)

    cost int

    mut cmd := 0
    mut lim := 0
    if args.len() == 1 and args[0] == "report"

    elif args.len() == 1 and args[0] == "total"

    elif args.len() == 2 and args[0] == "low"

        mut good := false

            good = sku_ok(p[1]) and num(p[2]) != none and num(p[3]) != none and num(p[2]) != 0 and true
        elif kind == "ship" and p.len() == 3
            good = sku_ok(p[1]) and num(p[2]) != none and num(p[2]) != 0
        elif kind == "count" and p.len() == 3
            good = sku_ok(p[1]) and num(p[2]) != none
        if not good
            io.eprint("error: line {k}: bad line")
            bad = true
            continue
        sku := p[1]
        q := num(p[2]) else 0
        if kind == "receive"
            pr := num(p[3]) else 0

            io.eprint("error: line {k}: unknown {sku}")

            continue
        it := items[sku]

struct Entry
    qty int
    cost int

fn usage() never
    io.eprint("usage: stock report|low N|total")
    io.exit(1)

fn is_num(s str) bool
    if s.len() < 1 or s.len() > 5
        return false
    for c in s.chars()
        if c < '0' or c > '9'
            return false
    true

fn is_sku(s str) bool
    if s.len() < 1
        return false
    for c in s.chars()
        ok := (c >= 'A' and c <= 'Z') or (c >= '0' and c <= '9') or c == '-'
        if not ok
            return false
    true

fn money(c int) str
    neg := c < 0
    a := if neg then -c else c
    d := a / 100
    r := a % 100
    s := "{d}.{r:02}"
    if neg then "-{s}" else s

    args := env.args()
    if args.len() < 1 or args.len() > 2

            usage()
    elif cmd == "low"
        if args.len() != 2 or not is_num(args[1])
            usage()
        limit = args[1].to_int() else 0
    else
        usage()

    mut m := Map[str, Entry]()
    mut bad := false
    lines := text.split("\n")

        line := lines[i]

        if line == "" or line.starts_with("#")
            continue
        p := line.split(" ")
        mut ok := false
        kind := p[0]
        if kind == "receive" and p.len() == 4
            ok = is_sku(p[1]) and is_num(p[2]) and is_num(p[3])
        elif kind == "ship" and p.len() == 3
            ok = is_sku(p[1]) and is_num(p[2])
        elif kind == "count" and p.len() == 3
            ok = is_sku(p[1]) and is_num(p[2])
        if ok
            q := p[2].to_int() else 0

                ok = false

            continue

        q := p[2].to_int() else 0

            e := m.get(sku) else Entry(qty: 0, cost: 0)
            m[sku] = Entry(qty: e.qty + q, cost: e.cost + q * price)

                    io.eprint("error: line {k}: short {sku}")
                    bad = true

## On-hand quantities and average cost per SKU.
use event

pub struct Entry
    pub qty int
    pub cost int

pub error enum Problem
    Unknown(sku str) "unknown {sku}"
    Short(sku str) "short {sku}"

pub struct Store
    items Map[str, Entry]

pub fn Store.new() Store
    Store(items: Map[str, Entry]())

## Every SKU ever received, in ascending byte order.
pub fn Store.skus(self) List[str]
    self.items.keys().sorted()

## The entry of a SKU from `skus()`.
pub fn Store.entry(self, sku str) Entry
    self.items[sku]

## Applies one event; a rejected event changes nothing.
pub fn Store.apply(mut self, e event.Event) ! Problem
    if e.kind == event.Kind.Receive
        mut fresh := self.items.get(e.sku) else Entry(qty: 0, cost: 0)
        fresh.qty += e.qty
        fresh.cost += e.qty * e.price
        self.items[e.sku] = fresh
        return
    mut it := self.items.get(e.sku) else return Problem.Unknown(e.sku)
    if e.kind == event.Kind.Ship
        if e.qty > it.qty
            return Problem.Short(e.sku)
        it.cost -= it.cost * e.qty / it.qty
        it.qty -= e.qty
    else
        if it.qty > 0
            it.cost = it.cost * e.qty / it.qty
        it.qty = e.qty
    self.items[e.sku] = it

## One line of the stock log.

pub enum Kind
    Receive
    Ship
    Count

pub struct Event
    pub kind Kind
    pub sku str
    pub qty int
    pub price int

pub error enum ParseError
    BadLine "bad line"

## 1 to 5 ASCII digits, as a number.
pub fn number(s str) int?
    if s.is_empty() or s.len() > 5
        return none
    for ch in s.chars()
        if ch.code() < 48 or ch.code() > 57
            return none
    s.to_int()

fn valid_sku(s str) bool
    if s.is_empty()
        return false
    for ch in s.chars()
        upper := ch.code() >= 65 and ch.code() <= 90
        digit := ch.code() >= 48 and ch.code() <= 57
        if not (upper or digit or ch == '-')
            return false
    true

## The event on a line, or `BadLine` if the line is not a valid event.
pub fn parse(line str) Event ! ParseError
    f := line.split(" ")
    mut kind := Kind.Receive
    if f[0] == "receive" and f.len() == 4
        kind = Kind.Receive
    elif f[0] == "ship" and f.len() == 3
        kind = Kind.Ship
    elif f[0] == "count" and f.len() == 3
        kind = Kind.Count
    else
        return BadLine
    if not valid_sku(f[1])
        return BadLine
    qty := number(f[2]) else return BadLine
    mut price := 0
    if kind == Kind.Receive
        p := number(f[3]) else return BadLine
        price = p
    if qty == 0 and kind != Kind.Count
        return BadLine
    Event(kind: kind, sku: f[1], qty: qty, price: price)

use store

## Cents as dollars with two decimals: `1234.05`, `-0.50`.
pub fn money(c int) str
    sign := if c < 0 then "-" else ""
    a := c.abs()
    "{sign}{a / 100}.{a % 100:0>2}"

pub fn report(s store.Store) List[str]
    mut out := List[str]()
    for sku in s.skus()
        it := s.entry(sku)
        out.push("{sku}\t{it.qty}\t{money(it.cost)}")
    out

pub fn low(s store.Store, n int) List[str]
    mut out := List[str]()
    for sku in s.skus()
        if s.entry(sku).qty < n
            out.push(sku)
    out

pub fn total(s store.Store) List[str]
    mut sum := 0
    for sku in s.skus()
        sum += s.entry(sku).cost
    [money(sum)]

pub enum Kind
    Receive
    Ship
    Count

pub struct Event
    pub kind Kind
    pub sku str
    pub qty int
    pub price int

pub error enum ParseError
    BadLine "bad line"

## 1 to 5 ASCII digits, as a number.
pub fn number(s str) int?
    if s.is_empty() or s.len() > 5
        return none
    for ch in s.chars()
        if ch.code() < 48 or ch.code() > 57
            return none
    s.to_int()

fn valid_sku(s str) bool
    if s.is_empty()
        return false
    for ch in s.chars()
        upper := ch.code() >= 65 and ch.code() <= 90
        digit := ch.code() >= 48 and ch.code() <= 57
        if not (upper or digit or ch == '-')
            return false
    true

## The event on a line, or `BadLine` if the line is not a valid event.
pub fn parse(line str) Event ! ParseError
    f := line.split(" ")
    mut kind := Kind.Receive
    if f[0] == "receive" and f.len() == 4
        kind = Kind.Receive
    elif f[0] == "ship" and f.len() == 3
        kind = Kind.Ship
    elif f[0] == "count" and f.len() == 3
        kind = Kind.Count
    else
        return BadLine
    if not valid_sku(f[1])
        return BadLine
    qty := number(f[2]) else return BadLine
    mut price := 0
    if kind == Kind.Receive
        p := number(f[3]) else return BadLine
        price = p
    if qty == 0 and kind != Kind.Count
        return BadLine
    Event(kind: kind, sku: f[1], qty: qty, price: price)

## The three outputs, as lines.
use store

## Cents as dollars with two decimals: `1234.05`, `-0.50`.
pub fn money(c int) str
    sign := if c < 0 then "-" else ""
    a := c.abs()
    "{sign}{a / 100}.{a % 100:0>2}"

pub fn report(s store.Store) List[str]
    mut out := List[str]()
    for sku in s.skus()
        it := s.entry(sku)
        out.push("{sku}\t{it.qty}\t{money(it.cost)}")
    out

pub fn low(s store.Store, n int) List[str]
    mut out := List[str]()
    for sku in s.skus()
        if s.entry(sku).qty < n
            out.push(sku)
    out

pub fn total(s store.Store) List[str]
    mut sum := 0
    for sku in s.skus()
        sum += s.entry(sku).cost
    [money(sum)]

# Issue: stock values drift, and error lines point at the wrong line

Two reports against `stock` (spec in `DOCS/spec.md`, sources in `src/`):

1. Values drift upwards. After receiving one SKU at two prices and shipping part of it, `report` shows a VALUE a few cents above what the spec's average-cost rule gives, and `total` repeats the error. With
   ```
   receive A 3 2
   receive A 1 4
   ship A 3
   ```
   `./stock report` prints `A	1	0.04`; by the spec it is `A	1	0.03`.
2. When the log has comments or blank lines, error messages name the wrong line. With
   ```
   # stock log
   receive A 1 1
   ship A 5
   ```
   stderr says `error: line 2: short A`; it should say line 3.

Find the causes, fix them, and keep `./test` passing. Hidden cases cover more than these examples. Do not change the spec's behaviour elsewhere.

use event
use report
use store

fn usage_ok(args List[str]) bool
    if args.len() == 1
        return args[0] == "report" or args[0] == "total"
    args.len() == 2 and args[0] == "low" and (event.number(args[1]) else -1) >= 0

fn main()
    args := env.args()
    if not usage_ok(args)
        io.eprint("usage: stock report|low N|total")
        io.exit(1)
    mut lines := io.read_all().split("\n")
    if (lines.last() else "x") == ""
        lines.pop()
    mut stock := store.Store.new()
    mut bad := 0
    mut lineno := 0
    for line in lines
        lineno += 1
        if line.is_empty() or line.starts_with("#")
            continue
        e := event.parse(line) else err
            io.eprint("error: line {lineno}: {err}")
            bad += 1
            continue
        stock.apply(e) else err
            io.eprint("error: line {lineno}: {err}")
            bad += 1
    mut out := List[str]()
    if args[0] == "report"
        out = report.report(stock)
    elif args[0] == "total"
        out = report.total(stock)
    else
        out = report.low(stock, event.number(args[1]) else 0)
    for l in out
        print(l)
    if bad > 0
        io.exit(2)

## On-hand quantities and average cost per SKU.
use event

pub struct Entry
    pub qty int
    pub cost int

pub error enum Problem
    Unknown(sku str) "unknown {sku}"
    Short(sku str) "short {sku}"

pub struct Store
    items Map[str, Entry]

pub fn Store.new() Store
    Store(items: Map[str, Entry]())

## Every SKU ever received, in ascending byte order.
pub fn Store.skus(self) List[str]
    self.items.keys().sorted()

## The entry of a SKU from `skus()`.
pub fn Store.entry(self, sku str) Entry
    self.items[sku]

## Applies one event; a rejected event changes nothing.
pub fn Store.apply(mut self, e event.Event) ! Problem
    if e.kind == event.Kind.Receive
        mut fresh := self.items.get(e.sku) else Entry(qty: 0, cost: 0)
        fresh.qty += e.qty
        fresh.cost += e.qty * e.price
        self.items[e.sku] = fresh
        return
    mut it := self.items.get(e.sku) else return Problem.Unknown(e.sku)
    if e.kind == event.Kind.Ship
        if e.qty > it.qty
            return Problem.Short(e.sku)
        it.cost -= it.cost * e.qty / it.qty
        it.qty -= e.qty
    else
        if it.qty > 0
            it.cost = it.cost * e.qty / it.qty
        it.qty = e.qty
    self.items[e.sku] = it

    for sku in s.skus()
